## Administration

Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/sections/5709579927964-Administration

### Business Units (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709562165916-Business-Units-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-06-17T10:40:08Z  
> Labels: Administration, 2BTr, ar_tms

#### Available for

- Business and Enterprise plans

Get in touch with [Sales](https://phrase.com/demo/) for licensing questions.

#### Available for

- Ultimate and Enterprise plans (Legacy)

Get in touch with [Sales](https://phrase.com/demo/) for licensing questions.

Business units provide the grouping of projects into sub-organizations or departments within a profile. This allows for the application and management of access rights to these groups rather than individuals projects.

Access rights can be restricted for:

- [Projects](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709748435484#UUID-fd006a60-d1b0-dc4b-8681-00d5464cd76e)
- [Project templates](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709647439772#UUID-94346683-ae2a-16b5-7e16-94a554612687)
- [Translation memories](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709688865692#UUID-9e5b1c50-0408-738b-59b5-baa05a312eea)
- [Term bases](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709733372188#UUID-ca45e09b-442e-336f-3257-2983bccd0503)

#### Business Unit Use Case

A company has divisions in the US and in the EU and don't want all Project managers to have access to all projects. Business units are created for each locale and Administrators set individual Project manager access rights based on the locale in which they have projects while declining access to outside projects.

#### Create a Business Unit

To create a business unit, follow these steps:

1. From the Settings ![Setup_gear.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682358955676) page, scroll down to the Project Metadata section and click on Business units.

   The Business units page opens.
2. Click New.

   The Create page opens.
3. Provide a name for the business unit.
4. Click Save.

   The new business unit is added to the list.

#### Assign a Business Unit

To assign a business unit, follow these steps:

1. From a project page, click Edit.

   The Edit project page opens.
2. Select a Business unit from the dropdown list.
3. Click Save.

   The selected nusiness unit is associated with the project.

#### Apply a Business Unit

To apply a business unit, follow these steps:

1. Select a PM from the Users page and click Edit.

   The Edit page opens.
2. In each category, apply required business units with *Active* or *Inactive* status.
3. Click Save.

   PM access rights are applied to specified business units.

### Feature Request Policy and Process

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709562182044-Feature-Request-Policy-and-Process  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2025-02-19T06:42:54Z  
> Labels: 2BTr

We built our company by listening to customers.

Phrase is a comprehensive software platform used by thousands of organizations. That means we receive a lot of valuable feedback and suggestions. Unfortunately, we cannot follow through on every suggestion and we need to say ‘no’ more than we would like to.

While we don’t publish our product roadmap, we do want to be transparent about how we handle your feature ideas.

This policy does not apply to bugs.

#### How to Submit a Feature Idea

Discuss the idea with our support team by opening a [support ticket](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/requests/new).

1. Select New feature request as the Request type.
2. Ensure all the details about the feature are included. Provide examples or use cases to demonstrate the need for the feature.
3. CC the Solution Architect or Customer Success Manager if you have one assigned.
4. Create separate posts for separate feature requests. This is very helpful in providing better tracking.

#### What Happens After Submitting an Idea

Our support engineer may:

- Ask for additional information.
- Propose an alternative approach or a workaround.
- Find out if the development isn’t already in place.
- Determine that the request cannot be accommodated.

After the support team confirms the proposed idea is valid, the original support ticket is closed.

#### How We Prioritize Feature Ideas

We take a number of factors into consideration when prioritizing future development, including:

- Product strategy - ideas need to be aligned with our long-term strategic vision.
- Demand - are there other customers who proposed the idea or would benefit from similar functionality?
- Level of effort - simple ideas have shorter implementation time than complex features.
- Availability of our team and resources.

#### How to Track What Is Happening to a Proposed Idea

After the proposed idea is prioritized by the product team, its status changes to Planned. Depending on the complexity of the implementation, it may take between one to three quarters to complete it. The status of the post will be updated to Completed once the feature is released to production.

Follow our [release notes](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/categories/4930539748124) and [product news](https://phrase.com/news/) pages to stay up to date.

### Language Quality Assessment (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709599557020-Language-Quality-Assessment-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-09-08T06:14:05Z  
> Labels: Administration, 2BTr, ar_tms

#### Available for

- Team, Professional, Business, Enterprise and Software UI/UX plans

Get in touch with [Sales](https://phrase.com/demo/) for licensing questions.

#### Available for

- Ultimate and Enterprise plans (Legacy)

Get in touch with [Sales](https://phrase.com/demo/) for licensing questions.

Language Quality Assessment (LQA) provides visibility on translation quality based on pre-configured criteria. LQA can be added as a [workflow](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709717879324#UUID-3d4fec12-4a9f-ace5-cd20-a1575786a6b7) step to help Linguists review translations (i.e. human translations, [machine translations](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709692009884#UUID-5ee4d7fd-b6eb-a722-73da-3fdcb23390b0) or machine translations with edits) according to predefined error categories applied in the [project](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709748435484#UUID-fd006a60-d1b0-dc4b-8681-00d5464cd76e).

The LQA workflow typically involves three main steps:

1. Definition and customization of LQA error categories.
2. Translation review to identify and evaluate LQA errors.

   1. Automatic calculation of an [LQA score](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/27529737766044#UUID-8c8a9e28-99dd-f432-f780-331192127c69) to assess the translation quality.

#### LQA Profiles

When assessing content quality, different rules may be required for different content types or clients. Some content may need to have precise terminology and others may need to follow locale convention or be precise with target length and markup. Errors may also require different severities or assigned weights.

LQA profiles are assigned when setting up the workflow for a project.

**Use Case:**

- Marketing texts don’t require literal translation while legal texts should be very precise. Marketing content could be assigned an 0.5 weight to *Omission* errors but legal text could have a 2.0 weight assigned to the same error.

#### Create an LQA Profile

Administrators and Project Managers with unlimited user rights can customize which types of [language quality assessment](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/27529737766044#UUID-8c8a9e28-99dd-f432-f780-331192127c69) error categories are applied in projects.

To create an LQA profile, follow these steps:

1. From the Settings ![Setup_gear.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682310460316) page, scroll down to the Quality section and click on Language quality assessment (LQA).

   The Language quality assessment page opens to display existing profiles.
2. Click Add profile.

   The Errors and their importance page opens.
3. Provide a Profile name.
4. Select error categories/subcategories based on [MQM Core typology](https://themqm.org/the-mqm-typology/) and indicate importance by adjusting weights . The default weight is 1.0.
5. Assign Penalty points per severity.

   These are used in scoring translations and are multiplied according to the error's weight. Recommended penalty values are 0 - Neutral, 1 - Minor, 5 - Major and 10 - Critical.
6. Provide a Pass/Fail threshold.
7. Click Create profile.

   Profile is added to the LQA profiles table.

Profiles can be edited, assigned as default, deleted or duplicated from the ![ellipses.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682310502428)menu to the right of the profile name.

Once a workflow step is created and becomes active in a project, its assigned LQA profile cannot be changed. To apply a different LQA profile, create a new workflow step with a position number higher than all existing steps in the project. From Settings, go to Workflow steps and click New workflow step, then assign a higher order number, enable LQA, and select the correct profile. This new step is created globally and becomes available for selection in the project's workflow steps after being added.

### Specifying Completed File Names and Export Paths (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709608269980-Specifying-Completed-File-Names-and-Export-Paths-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-08-27T06:13:11Z  
> Labels: Administration, 2BTr, ar_tms

Automate the renaming and target of downloaded (translated) files.

Follow these steps:

1. From the Settings ![Setup_gear.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682342092316) page, scroll down to the Project settings section and click on Completed file name and export path.

   The Completed file name and export path page opens.
2. Apply Rename completed files to macro if required. Macro names are case-sensitive.

   Supported macros:

   - `{path}`

     Only for files imported in ZIP format with a folder structure.
   - `{fileName}`

     Characters can be removed from the original file name by using a character position (starting from 0) to select part of the name. Examples:

     - `{fileName[2:6]}` to keep the 3rd to the 7th characters of the file name
     - `{fileName[0:-3]}` to cut off the last 2 characters.
   - `{sourceLang}`

     Adds source language
   - Use these macros to represent target language

     Target language macros for multilingual files are a concatenation of all target language codes (e.g. `./cs-de-zh_cn`):

     - `{targetLang}` Based on [language codes](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709608511516#UUID-20af2b09-6aa5-bdd3-57d5-7939abfb65ca "Supported Languages (TMS)").
     - `{targetLangName}` Based on [language names](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709608511516#UUID-20af2b09-6aa5-bdd3-57d5-7939abfb65ca "Supported Languages (TMS)").
     - `{targetLangRFC}`

       - Examples: `es`, `en-US`, `az-Latn-AZ`
       - Based on [RFC 5646](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5646)
     - `{targetLangRFCLower}`

       - Examples: `de-de`, `en-us`
     - `{targetLangIso}`

       - Examples: `de`, `en`
     - `{targetLangLocale}`

       - Examples: `de_DE`
     - `{targetLangJavaResourceBundle}`

       - This macro follows legacy Java resource bundle naming conventions. For some languages, the resulting code differs from the standard locale code produced by `{targetLangLocale}`. Indonesian resolves to `in_ID` instead of `id_ID`, Hebrew resolves to `iw_IL` instead of `he_IL`, and Yiddish resolves to `ji` instead of `yi`.
     - `{targetLangAndroid}`

       - Examples: `es`, `en-rUS`
     - `{targetLangAndroidBCP}`

       - Examples: `b+es`, `b+en+US`
   - `{workflow}`
   - `{status}`
   - `{date}`

     Date of file download in the PM's timezone
   - `{time}`

     Time of file download in the PM's timezone
   - `{userName}`

     Adds username of the assigned Linguist or Vendor. If multiple Linguists are assigned, the name will be empty.
   - `{replaceExt[xx]}`

     The file extension is replaced by that specified within [ ] brackets.

     - Example:

       If `{replaceExt[txt]}` is specified, the file *test.POT* is downloaded as *test.txt*.
     - Changing extensions does not change the format itself; renaming '.docx' to '.xlsx' does not change a text file into a spreadsheet file.
3. Provide macro for Export online repository files to.

   - If specific files are monitored, then select Target language subfolder for Export completed files to.

     Specify the folder name in the Target Subfolder Path:

     - Use these macros to represent target language.

       - `{targetLang}` Based on [language codes](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709608511516#UUID-20af2b09-6aa5-bdd3-57d5-7939abfb65ca "Supported Languages (TMS)").
       - `{targetLangName}` Based on [language names](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709608511516#UUID-20af2b09-6aa5-bdd3-57d5-7939abfb65ca "Supported Languages (TMS)").
       - `{targetLangRFC}`

         - Examples: `es`, `en-US`, `az-Latn-AZ`
         - Based on [RFC 5646](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5646)
       - `{targetLangRFCLower}`

         - Examples: `de-de`, `en-us`
       - `{targetLangIso}`

         - Examples: `de`, `en`
       - `{targetLangLocale}`

         - Examples: `de_DE`
       - `{targetLangAndroid}`

         - Examples: `es`, `en-rUS`
       - `{targetLangAndroidBCP}`

         - Examples: `b+es`, `b+en+US`
         - Subfolders can be created within the source folder.

           Available for [Amazon S3](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709642462364#UUID-d11cf532-a08e-5226-3c63-83a69235c61f), [Azure](https://support.phrase.com/document/preview/363#UUID-3cec285f-02cf-93d5-085f-7e8b6c2b2174), [FTP](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709668060444#UUID-f561b4aa-8ce6-f53a-d498-4a0e4aa189cc), [SFTP](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709654587164#UUID-91f2d662-b47b-927f-ca1b-1f67b721237d), [Dropbox](https://support.phrase.com/document/preview/376#UUID-888ecb58-fac4-b192-1374-19bc385940f0), [Google Drive](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709642759708#UUID-b7ae67ad-cda3-7eb3-907e-6bcd8ce47e2d), [Box](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709656600348#UUID-86845105-8abd-dd47-86bf-ff721ab2e745), [OneDrive](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709654491548#UUID-eacfb97c-96bc-4498-5bbe-60dc3e074676), [Git](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709654170780#UUID-54d80814-1f84-4dd2-39df-cb2370f55de8), [GitHub](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709656771356#UUID-59be0e6b-918d-2c99-67d5-9ead10cab859), [GitLab](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709668128796#UUID-9080c15e-f184-4520-1c33-257442b37bd2), and [Bitbucket Cloud](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709653950492#UUID-5150c835-7b8a-2f82-bf92-51418bdb7b10).
     - For some repositories, an absolute path is available. Begin your path with / to indicate the absolute path.

       Available for Amazon S3, Azure, FTP, SFTP, Dropbox, Google Drive, Box, OneDrive, Git, GitHub, GitLab, and [SharePoint](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709638401820#UUID-112cc49b-fc38-e797-40eb-e30a02780fd0). When using Git connector, the leading / is followed by the branch name, and then by the root of the repository where .git folder is located. If the branch doesn’t exist, it will be created. When using other Git-based connectors (e.g. GitLab), the leading slash is followed by the root of the repository where .git folder is located.
     - Use `..` to refer to the parent folder.

     ### Tip

     **Examples**

     If the source file is `/files/loc/ui.properties` and the target language is German (Germany):

     - `translations/{targetLang}` will create */files/loc/translations/de\_de*
     - `/files-{targetLang}/loc` will create */files-de\_de/loc/<filename>*
     - `../{targetLang}` will create */files/de\_de/<filename>*
   - Use `.` to export a file to the same folder as the source file.

     Available for FTP and SFTP connectors.
   - If Rename completed files to includes folder segments, such as `{path}` or a target language macro used as a folder (for example `{targetLangRFC}/{fileName}`), Export online repository files to must also specify a matching path. If Export online repository files to is left empty in that case, the export fails.
4. Click Save.

   Specified macros are applied to downloaded files.

If the naming rule specified in Rename completed files to includes folder segments (for example `{path}`, or target language macros used to imply a folder structure), the Export online repository files to field must also be populated with a corresponding path. If the naming rule contains folder segments and the export path field is left empty, the export fails silently: no progress bar appears, no entry is added to the export history, and no error message is shown.

Use one of the following pairings:

- Naming rule `{fileName}` paired with export path `translated/{targetLangRFC}`
- Naming rule `{path}/{fileName}` paired with an empty export path field

The export path field only needs to be populated when the naming rule includes folder segments. If the export path field is left empty, the naming rule must not contain any folder segments and should consist of `{fileName}` only.

### Phrase TMS Limits

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5784117234972-Phrase-TMS-Limits  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-08-24T06:14:05Z  
> Labels: 2BTr, File size

Users are expected to use Phrase responsibly, reasonably (especially with regards to our [fair use policy](https://phrase.com/terms/)) and to comply with our [data storage](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/17019781874076#UUID-99ae6922-df28-38ae-ea89-7f7fac88a538) policy.

- The free **Developer** edition is limited to a maximum of two [jobs](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709686763420#UUID-33f88350-daa8-2ab2-e7ce-e35300ec60f8), and the maximum size of any uploaded file is 1 MB.
- Numbers of users is dependant on [user management](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5793349215900#UUID-09f99b48-09c7-b144-42bb-a1bfd2e7d452).

#### File Size Import Limits

- **Maximum import size:** 1 GB (for a file or a batch of files [imported](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709686763420#UUID-33f88350-daa8-2ab2-e7ce-e35300ec60f8) in one request).
- **.ZIP**: 100 MB
- **Plain .PDF** (not via TransPDF): 100 MB
- **XML inside MS Office documents**: 100 MB
- **.IDML files**: 200 MB per file and 100 MB for embedded XML files.
- **.RTF files**: 30 MB
- **.YAML files**: 20 MB
- **.JSON** and **.YAML**: the Context Note, Context Key, and Max. target length are processed only for files 10MB and smaller.
- **Custom logo**: Image cannot be larger than 180x65px.
- **Preview package size limit**: 50 MB

#### File Import Limits

- **File naming**: Filename and *original file directory* length is limited to 255 chars. Both properties are truncated on save, so information may be lost on save if names are too long.
- **Number of segments** in one job: 500,000
- **Tag metadata** content in a segment: 20,480 characters (calculated separately for source and target)
- **Number of characters per segment**: 10,240 characters (calculated separately for source and target)
- **Number of characters per context key/context note**: 10,240 characters.
- **MS Word paragraphs**: 20,000 characters
- **.DOC files**: 80 pictures per file
- **MS Excel**:

  - 200,000 cells per file
  - 500 styles for files imported as MS Excel with the HTML subfilter, regex to Convert to Phrase tags or as Multilingual MS Excel.
  - Spreadsheet documents containing more than 10,000 cells with conditional formatting and are processed with Multilingual Excel, Excel with html (Process HTML code) or Excel with Convert to Phrase TMS tags filters will be rejected as too large/complex.
- **MS Excel sheet names**: 31 characters, table names: 255 characters
- **.XML**: the Context Note, Context Key, and Max. target length are processed only for files with a maximum of 10,000 XML elements.
- **MT Glossaries**: Up to 10 glossaries can be attached to a Phrase Language AI profile (or activated in Phrase Language AI if profiles are not used) with a maximum of 50,000 entries in total.
- [**Update source**](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709686763420#UUID-33f88350-daa8-2ab2-e7ce-e35300ec60f8): A new version of the source file can only be uploaded to an existing job once every 30 minutes.
- [**References**](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/10825091188252#UUID-6c709408-1d38-28ad-b042-4b54558b29dd): Any type of file can be added as a reference with a 1Gb size limit.

#### API Limits: Async Requests

The most resource demanding actions in Phrase are called *Async Requests* as they are executed asynchronously. This includes [creation of new jobs](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709686763420#UUID-33f88350-daa8-2ab2-e7ce-e35300ec60f8), [pre-translation](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709717749788#UUID-a982e5f9-9aa2-434f-116c-17b822d35343), [analysis](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709712007708#UUID-7ed2ed16-6064-f667-bb86-7d971d7004c9), TM [exports and imports](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709739829532#UUID-1d5509ec-f537-4aff-cede-ce93f80b713c), [QA](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709703799324#UUID-83632035-0d65-f957-b0dd-ad00704f8d25), etc.

Limits for the maximum number of concurrently running (submitted and not yet completed) async requests in each plan:

| Plan | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Developer | 50 |
| Teamstart | 100 |
| Academic | 100 |
| Team | 200 |
| Ultimate | 500 |
| Enterprise Starter | 2000 |
| Enterprise | 2000 |

If limits are exceeded when submitting a new async request, the 429 HTTP response will be returned. The `async/status` API [endpoint](https://cloud.memsource.com/web/docs/api#operation/getCurrentLimitStatus) is available to monitor the current number of running async requests and their limits.

##### Limits for new Phrase Platform pricing plans

| Plan | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Starter/Freelancer (LSP) | N/A |
| Team/Professional (LSP) | 200 |
| Business/Business (LSP) | 500 |
| Enterprise/Enterprise (LSP) | 2000 |

#### Request Rate Limiter

The request rate limiter is common to all Phrase services. This limiter allows a fixed number of requests to be submitted within a fixed time frame (minute) by a user.

Access to Phrase Services via the API is subject to usage limits. The number of permitted calls is:

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Logged-in users | 6,000 per minute |
| Users who are not logged in | 2,000 per minute |

#### Concurrent Request Limiter

The concurrent request limiter only allows a certain number of requests to be processed concurrently for one user. This limiter works as an add-on to the request rate limiter to protect the system from resource exhaustion in the following scenarios:

- Resource-intensive APIs being heavily called by a single user.
- APIs called at extreme rates within a very short period of time. This can be caused by a malfunctioning script.

The concurrent request rate limiter has two limits: the *global* limit tracks the number of concurrent requests being processed across the whole system and the *local* limit tracks the number of concurrent requests being processed at one backend processing unit. The requests are evenly distributed to many backend processing units so it very rarely occurs that a local limit is hit. An example of limits being hit may be the submission of hundreds of requests in just a few milliseconds over a single HTTP connection resulting in many requests directed to a single backend processing unit. Under normal circumstances the global limit is the only number to be aware of.

The default limits are as follows and may be increased upon request:

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Global concurrent limit | 100 |
| Local concurrent limit | 50 |

If the limit is hit, the Phrase TMS API will return a HTTP 429 status code in the response. To prevent this from happening, track the number of concurrent requests and submit new requests only if there is free capacity. To make it easier, the following HTTP headers are returned in all API responses:

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Ratelimit-Limit | Maximum number of permitted concurrent requests |
| Ratelimit-Remaining | Remaining number of concurrent requests that can be made |

#### Jobs in a Project

- The maximum number of jobs that can be in a project (all target languages) is 50,000 including jobs imported via API. The recommended volume for simultaneous import is up to 500 jobs per 1 target language.
- Assigning providers from a template will only allow 100 jobs to be selected at a time.
- The maximum number of segments which CAT web editor can open (applicable to both a single file and joined files) is 150,000 segments.
- The maximum number of joined jobs that can be processed in QA is 500.
- A maximum of 260 job parts in joined jobs can be opened at a time in the CAT web editor.
- A maximum of 1,000 job parts in joined jobs can be opened at a time in the CAT desktop editor.
- If the number of job parts exceeds 500, comments and LQA are disabled in the CAT desktop editor.

Opening a large number of files at one time can have a negative impact on performance or cause difficulties with loading all files. To avoid problems, it is recommended that you do not join more than 100 files or more than 150,000 segments.

#### Analytics

- The maximum number of rows that can be downloaded from a chart or report is 10K.
- Data retention period is limited to the past 12 months.

#### In-context Preview

- The in-context preview in CAT editors for MS Excel or Multilingual MS Excel has a limit of 200 columns or 5000 rows in the original file. This limit excludes hidden columns or rows.
- [Office Open XML](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_Open_XML) Word documents (default format of MS Office documents since 2007) with any XML zipped inside larger than 20 MB, will not generate in-context preview. This restriction also applies to older formats as Phrase converts them to Office Open XML upon import.
- In-context preview cannot be generated for .PPTX or .DOCX files of over 100 MB.
- In-context preview for .PPTX files is limited to files with a maximum of 100 slides.
- In-context preview for .PPTX files fails to generate when embedded images inside the presentation exceed internal size thresholds: 500 KB per individual image and 10 MB total across all images combined.

  To check embedded image sizes, rename the file extension from .pptx to .zip, open the archive, and inspect the images in the ppt/media/ folder. Resize any image exceeding 500 KB, or reduce the total combined image size below 10 MB, then re-import the file. Cleaning the file metadata before re-importing can also help: in PowerPoint on Windows, go to File > Info > Check for Issues > Inspect Document > Inspect, then click Remove All next to \"Document Properties and Personal Information\". On Mac, open the Review tab and select Check Document to access the same inspector.
- CMS in-context preview has a limit of 5,000 segments.

#### Editor Limits

There is no ability to switch [organizations](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/6091807042076#UUID-3b204035-bb79-8662-cb38-a08bb599962b) within the desktop editor; if a user is a member of multiple organizations, they will only be able to use the desktop editor under the default organization.

Side panel display limitations:

- **Cat tab results**

  - Unlimited term base results
  - 5 translation memory results
  - 5 subsegment results
- **Search tab results**

  - 15 term bases results
  - 50 translation memories results
- **Translation table**

  - In any segment, no more than 999 splits or joins (or combination of these) can be performed.
  - Maximum number of characters per segment: 8,196

#### Auto LQA Limits

Auto LQA can be run on:

- A maximum of 1800 segments per job.
- A maximum of 200 jobs per day.

#### Default Analysis

The results of a default analysis of files that contain more than 100,000 segments is only approximate.

Analysis results are calculated independently for each target language against that language's own translation memory content. Even when multiple target languages in a project share the same TM, each language pair maintains its own translation units, so a source segment can score differently in each language pair. As a result, match percentages and net rates can differ across target languages in the same project even when the analysis settings are identical for all of them.

#### Translation Memory Limits

- Original imported values of text attributes are truncated to max. 32,766 UTF-8 bytes (calculated separately for source and target units).
- [Segment key](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/9386879839900#UUID-3b275425-0cc2-6b63-2971-619cb40d1636) values longer than ~32kb cannot be indexed.

#### Automated Project Creation (APC)

- A maximum of 10 monitored folders can be set per APC.
- Monitoring more than 10,000 files per APC can cause file import errors and performance issues. If an error occurs in the UI, it is recommended to reduce the number of monitored files and manually trigger APC monitoring to retry the import.

### Bidirectional Text (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709562365980-Bidirectional-Text-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-06-29T08:00:38Z  
> Labels: 2BTr, ar_tms

Text in a document that goes both left-to-right (LTR) and right-to-left (RTL) is considered bidirectional.

Example:

The inclusion of English language words in an otherwise Arabic text; English words being read left to right with the remaining text reading right to left.

- Right-to-left languages are fully supported as translation targets. Bidirectional text support applies to segments with an RTL target locale (e.g. translating into Arabic or Hebrew). It does not apply when the source language is RTL and the target is LTR.
- Strong directional characters, such as Arabic or Hebrew letters, and Latin letters, are recognized automatically by the editor. Neutral characters (numbers, spaces, punctuation) are not automatically assigned a direction; they inherit direction from context, which can produce incorrect rendering. For these characters, directional marks must be inserted manually.
- To mark neutral text (numbers, spaces, dots, etc.) as RTL or LTR, follow these steps:

  1. In the editor, select the text to be marked.
  2. From the Edit menu, select Insert symbol.
  3. Select Left-to-Right Mark (**CTRL+ALT+SHIFT+L**) or Right-to-Left Mark (**CTRL+ALT+SHIFT+R**).

     The selected text is marked as specified and the marking can be viewed in the target with the Display hidden characters toggled on under the Format menu.

### Access and Security (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709585565980-Access-and-Security-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-07-29T06:12:45Z  
> Labels: Administration, Security, 2BTr

To access options for managing security environment and data access, follow these steps:

1. From the Settings ![Setup_gear.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682339949724) page, scroll down to the Project settings section and click on Access and security.

   The Access and security page opens.
2. Select required options:

   - Receive webhooks and Orchestrator triggers for this project
   - Display usernames in LQA scorecard

     When disabled, all names are replaced with the user id and organization name.
   - Use vendors

     Allow the use of Vendors that facilitate the [sharing and collaboration](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709703948444#UUID-2fb330ab-e5ad-e017-5972-a9a75c1e0360) of files across organizations.
   - Grant access to Phrase technical support

     [Phrase technical support](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5784099168284#UUID-e4850ff4-2767-84b5-3d18-4f0f40e3072d) has access to your profile to help resolve technical issues.
   - Activate/Deactivate linguists automatically

     If enabled, [Linguist](https://support.phrase.com/document/preview/10095#UUID-cbf40c4c-9130-9844-ff10-25bc2b982151) profiles are automatically deactivated once they have no jobs in progress. As soon as a new job is assigned, profiles are automatically reactivated.
   - Use secure HTTPS for [Webhooks](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709693398812#UUID-6a1bd917-264f-438d-8d66-2e32504779ec)
   - Set Session timeout value
   - Email notifications

     Users or vendors assigned to the project will receive notifications concerning assigned work, status changes comments or LQA mentions, newly added reference materials, and other project updates. If not selected, no notifications are sent.

     Does not override Notify providers settings when [creating a job](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709686763420#UUID-33f88350-daa8-2ab2-e7ce-e35300ec60f8).
   - Notify [job owner](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709756503196#UUID-f5990e2a-6aa9-ce27-fe52-bdad461726e6) when job status is changed
   - [Notify](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709702543260#UUID-1f822e95-39f1-cc57-0234-5532047c453d) users when [mentioned](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/7681232807708#UUID-0801f553-9b35-4ba4-4a38-46d3fc1e8a34) in comments or LQA
   - Notify specific user groups when reference materials are added

     Notifications are triggered to the selected user group only when a new reference is added manually to a project. Notifications are not sent for references added from project templates, automated imports or updates, or deletions.

     A dedicated email template can be selected for this notification.

     Projects with many assigned users or vendors may send notifications to a large audience.
   - Set Trusted IP addresses or ranges (Business and Enterprise editions only)

     If specified, users are not able to log in from other addresses. Select Advanced to set access options based on [user roles](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5793349215900#UUID-09f99b48-09c7-b144-42bb-a1bfd2e7d452). Ranges are specified with a [CIDR suffix](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Help:Range_blocks).

     ### Note

     Only IPv4 addresses are supported.
   - Allow users to:

     - turn on/off auto-propagation of repetitions in CAT editor

       Permits Linguists and Vendors the option of enabling or disabling the auto-propagation of [repetitions](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709708706460#UUID-b94ef2c1-e8fa-b9ce-e18e-242b5873bd1b) feature in the editor.
     - turn on/ off [instant QA](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709703799324#UUID-83632035-0d65-f957-b0dd-ad00704f8d25) in CAT editor
   - Allow linguists to:

     - download their translation jobs

       [Linguists](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709735838492#UUID-911ee8d4-ecc1-0c38-8f71-7c22f1646545) (including Vendor's Linguists) may download bilingual content for translation outside of Phrase. Bilingual MXLIFF files, bilingual DOCX files, and TMX files may be downloaded for translation in the [CAT desktop editor](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709683873052#UUID-92b9886a-e3a5-6975-8c35-246200ac54ef) or other external editor.

       This setting applies to both shared projects and jobs. If disabled, Vendor project managers or administrators can still download and manage the job.
     - download the [LQA Scorecard](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/27529737766044#UUID-8c8a9e28-99dd-f432-f780-331192127c69)
     - access the CAT web editor

       Project managers can control in which environments Linguists (including Vendor's Linguists) may work. With this box checked, translators can click on file names and open them in the [CAT web editor](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709683890204#UUID-b7f5d899-ec2b-4352-a151-d45f6cfb5cd8).

       This setting applies to both shared projects and jobs. If disabled, Vendor's project managers or administrators can still open the job in the CAT editor.
     - view user metadata in CAT editor

       Linguists and Vendors may see the names of others who translated identified [TM](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709688865692#UUID-9e5b1c50-0408-738b-59b5-baa05a312eea) matches. Deselect this option to ensure anonymity, privacy and prevent providers from seeing each other's names.

       If disabled, [mentions](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/7681232807708#UUID-0801f553-9b35-4ba4-4a38-46d3fc1e8a34) in the CAT editor and in-app notifications continue to work even when Linguist users cannot see other users' names in the CAT editor. Mentioned users are shown by UID instead.
     - only begin [workflow steps](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709717879324#UUID-3d4fec12-4a9f-ace5-cd20-a1575786a6b7) if the preceding step is **'completed'**

       Restrict or allow translators and reviewers to work simultaneously on one job in multiple workflow steps or not until the job is set to *Complete*.
     - edit locked segments

       Linguists are permitted to edit locked segments by clicking F2.
     - edit tag content
     - edit source

       Linguists are permitted to edit source texts including the [splitting and joining of segments](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709678012828#UUID-753af50b-27d0-e386-418a-452ed30e0083).

       If not selected, Linguists are not permitted to:

       - Edit the source language in the editor. Pressing F2, triggers the message Source edits disabled by project owner.
       - Upload bilingual MXLIFF or DOCX files with edits in the source segments including modification in the UI, API, or editor. Attempts trigger the message Source edits prohibited by project owner. Upload failed.
       - Join or split segments.
   - Allow vendors (of shared jobs) to:

     - upload references
     - change due date
   - Allow loading of:

     - external content in CAT editor
     - iframes in CAT web editor
3. Click Save.

   Preferences are applied.

### Supported Languages (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709608511516-Supported-Languages-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-08-19T06:13:28Z  
> Labels: Administration, 2BTr, ar_tms

Phrase TMS is a language-independent system. Practically any standard language can be supported with various writing scripts.

#### Active languages

If a supported language is not available, it may not be activated. [Administrators](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709753812124#UUID-c512e8a2-c3ee-7321-9b76-81f0dd72517f) may activate or deactivate languages as required by an organization.

To activate or deactivate a language, follow these steps:

1. From the Settings ![Setup_gear.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682342177308) page, scroll down to the Administration section and click on Active languages.

   The Active languages page opens.
2. Move required languages to the Inactive or Active columns.
3. Click Save.

   Selected languages are now activated or deactivated.

#### Bidirectional Text (TMS)

Text in a document that goes both left-to-right (LTR) and right-to-left (RTL) is considered bidirectional.

Example:

The inclusion of English language words in an otherwise Arabic text; English words being read left to right with the remaining text reading right to left.

- Right-to-left languages are fully supported as translation targets. Bidirectional text support applies to segments with an RTL target locale (e.g. translating into Arabic or Hebrew). It does not apply when the source language is RTL and the target is LTR.
- Strong directional characters, such as Arabic or Hebrew letters, and Latin letters, are recognized automatically by the editor. Neutral characters (numbers, spaces, punctuation) are not automatically assigned a direction; they inherit direction from context, which can produce incorrect rendering. For these characters, directional marks must be inserted manually.
- To mark neutral text (numbers, spaces, dots, etc.) as RTL or LTR, follow these steps:

  1. In the editor, select the text to be marked.
  2. From the Edit menu, select Insert symbol.
  3. Select Left-to-Right Mark (**CTRL+ALT+SHIFT+L**) or Right-to-Left Mark (**CTRL+ALT+SHIFT+R**).

     The selected text is marked as specified and the marking can be viewed in the target with the Display hidden characters toggled on under the Format menu.

### Analytics Dashboards (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/6554447243036-Analytics-Dashboards-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-09-30T06:14:31Z  
> Labels: 2BTr, ar_tms, edited_at

Analytics dashboards provide ready-made dashboards for standard metrics, including MT usage, cost, volume, leverage, savings, time, quality, quotes, and TM threshold, each with its own filters. Use [Advanced Analytics](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/7756614696988#UUID-4cac50d9-b52a-30fb-ba52-2e1dd66b9989 "Advanced Analytics (TMS)") to build a chart for a metric, breakdown, or combination that none of the predefined dashboards covers.

Analytics dashboards are accessed from the Phrase Analytics button on the navigation panel.

In line with our internal [data storage](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/17019781874076#UUID-99ae6922-df28-38ae-ea89-7f7fac88a538) policy, any customer-input text (e.g. project names, file names, domains) from permanently deleted content does not appear in Phrase Analytics. Permanently deleted content is replaced with Deleted. All numerical values, dates, timestamps, boolean data types from permanently deleted content remain available. This ensures that historical KPIs, trends, and forecasting aggregations remain consistent over time.

- Charts showing *by provider* include both linguists and vendors.
- Language pairs are shown as a concatenation of source to target language.
- Charts showing *by project* only display the first 10,000 projects while the full project list is included when downloaded.
- Dashboards show data in UTC timezone.
- Dashboards are refreshed twice daily:

  - 12:00am and 12:00pm UTC for the EU instance
  - 07:00am and 19:00pm UTC for the US instance

  Each dashboard shows the time of the last data refresh completion. It is important to note that the displayed timestamp may not include data generated up to 3 hours prior. This is because transactions may not be captured in time when the data refresh process is triggered.
- Data reports are available for the past 12 full months, allowing users to have a full year at any point in time.

A video review of the dashboards:

|  |
| --- |
| [Eingebettetes Video/Inhalt](https://www.youtube.com/embed/Zn7VE8yGnys) |

##### Note

Due to continuous improvements, the user interface may not be exactly the same as presented in the video.

An administrator sets each project manager's Analytics access level in [user](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5793349215900#UUID-09f99b48-09c7-b144-42bb-a1bfd2e7d452) settings. Three levels are available:

- View all organization data.
- View only data from projects the project manager owns.
- No dashboard access.

Every dashboard supports different filters to display selected data in the charts. In particular, the Job state filter takes into account the following job states:

- Available job.
- Job in recycle bin.

  When a job or a project is deleted, the job is marked with this state as long as it sits in the recycle bin.
- Deleted job.

  A job removed by manually or automatically emptying the recycle bin.
- Archived job.

  ### Note

  When a job is archived, its state changes to *archived*. When a project is archived, the state of the job does not change.

It is recommended that the date filter is not run for more than one year in time, as performance may degrade and chart may no longer preserve definition.

Every chart can be downloaded in .csv, .xlsx, .json and .png file formats. Click on the 3-dots button at the top right of the chart and select ![Download Results](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682327041564) Download results:

- To download formatted results including a comma separator in large numbers, select the desired file format from the Download full results window.
- To download unformatted results, hold the **Shift** (Windows) or **Option** (Mac) key and select the desired file format from the Download full results window.

#### Shared Content

Data from [shared](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709703948444#UUID-2fb330ab-e5ad-e017-5972-a9a75c1e0360) content is supported in all dashboards.

Shared content that has been deleted is not guaranteed to remain visible for any organization other than the content owner.

Several dashboards include ownership filters to help distinguish between data owned by the organization and data shared across organizations:

- The Job ownership filter identifies whether the organization is the creator of the job or not.

  - Own content

    Jobs created by the organization (which may or may not be shared).
  - Shared content

    Jobs that are shared with or by the organization, regardless of who created them.
- The LQA ownership filter identifies whether the organization is the creator of the LQA assessment or not.

  The review provider is considered the owner, so the organization’s view will show the assessment as Own Content. Users from other organizations (such as the translation provider, project buyer, or vendor) will see the same assessment listed under Shared Content.

  If the provider is from your organization, their username and full name are displayed. If the provider is from a different organization, their user ID and organization name are shown, as seen in the scorecard.
- The Quote ownership filter identifies whether the organization is the creator of the quote or not.
- The Analysis ownership filter identifies whether the organization is the creator of the analysis or not.

#### Cost Dashboard

##### Available for

- Team, Professional, Business and Enterprise plans

Get in touch with [Sales](https://phrase.com/demo/) for licensing questions.

The charts show the actual spend of an organization calculated on a pricing metric (e.g. word count, character count, pages or hours) and multiplied by a [price list](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709625473436#UUID-95ab5b98-50d1-a2e5-ca91-e80e85131cbc).

The cost dashboard is based on:

- [Quotes](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709635877020#UUID-317de099-f8f9-9c94-dde1-36018cb96947) for all the workflow steps in the project.

  ### Note

  Creating a new quote for the same workflow step overwrites the data for the previously created quote.
- All hourly quotes for the project and the latest quote for the standard quotes for each job.

In [shared projects](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709703948444#UUID-2fb330ab-e5ad-e017-5972-a9a75c1e0360) (or quotes with assigned provider), the quote is visible to all users but the latest quote may be different for each user.

When assigning a provider to a job, consider:

- If a provider is assigned during job creation, their price list overwrites the project’s price list.
- If a provider is assigned later, the cost is not re-calculated automatically.

  Generate a quote for the assigned user to update the data accordingly.
- If multiple providers are assigned to a job part, the first listed provider's data is used.

  Generate a new quote to use any other user’s pricing information.

#### MT Usage Dashboard

The MT usage tab presents insight on MT units and translated character consumption across Phrase TMS and Strings, [Phrase Portal](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/12949538303516#UUID-0af9ae02-cbd1-1c17-aec5-541956f27282), and [Phrase Language AI via API](https://eu.phrase.com/smt/api/docs/index.html). It provides an overview of consumption over time, locale pair, MT engine, and MT profile, by project and workflow step.

Upon access, it defaults to Phrase TMS but users can also see consumption across all/specific Phrase products by adjusting the Phrase product dashboard filter.

The TMS MT origin filter shows the split of MT units across Phrase TMS:

- TMS pre-translation
- TMS analysis
- TMS CAT editor

#### Leverage Dashboard

The charts display how translation memories (TM), machine translation (MT), repetitions, and non-translatables (NT) are leveraged across jobs.

Leverage is computed as the difference between the word count in the specific match category before applying any net rate scheme and the word count in the same match category after applying the net rate scheme.

The dashboard is based on:

- Data from default [analysis](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709712007708#UUID-7ed2ed16-6064-f667-bb86-7d971d7004c9).
- Data from the last run analysis for any given job.

Data are generated only when a [net rate scheme](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709665578908#UUID-271da169-10bc-f829-9b5d-421d21407b8f) is added to the project or to the provider assigned to a job before the analysis is created. If the net rate scheme is changed in the project or analysis, the analysis displays up-to-date information.

The charts display no data in the following scenarios:

- Projects and jobs without a net rate scheme.
- Analyses with 0 leverage (e.g. for projects, language pairs, etc.).
- Analyses with internal fuzzies.
- Deleted analyses.

Only analyses created by a user belonging to the viewer's organization are included in the computation of the dashboard. Therefore, when a Buyer [shares a job](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709703948444#UUID-2fb330ab-e5ad-e017-5972-a9a75c1e0360) with a Vendor and the Vendor creates the analyses:

- The buyer does not see the data related to the analyses in the dashboard.
- Since the vendor is the creator of the analyses, they are able to see pertinent data in the dashboard.

#### QPS Insights Dashboard

##### Available for

- Team, Professional, Business, Enterprise and Software UI/UX plans

Get in touch with [Sales](https://phrase.com/demo/) for licensing questions.

Quality performance score (QPS) estimates MT translation quality at the segment level to determine which segments are good enough for auto-confirmation. QPS is generated automatically by [Language AI](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709660879516#UUID-b0d64b4f-fa01-f7c3-006a-40e0ee0dedd2) and is distinct from [Language Quality Assessment](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709599557020-Language-Quality-Assessment-TMS) (LQA) scores, which reflect human reviewer assessments and are tracked separately in the [Quality Dashboard](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/6554447243036-Analytics-Dashboards-TMS#quality-dashboard-0-12).

[Pre-translated](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709717749788#UUID-a982e5f9-9aa2-434f-116c-17b822d35343) segments can be automatically confirmed based on the [QPS](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709672289180#UUID-054981cd-9a0e-32bf-79b7-cd6167ebf444) thresholds set in Pre-translation settings. QPS is only available for MT segments translated via [Language AI](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709660879516#UUID-b0d64b4f-fa01-f7c3-006a-40e0ee0dedd2).

For MT quality data, use the QPS Insights Dashboard. For human review scores, use the Quality Dashboard.

The dashboard helps find the optimal QPS threshold to balance cost savings and quality risks.

Filters in the dashboard help find the best values for different content categories, as technical, legal, and marketing texts may have varying quality requirements.

These insights are based on segment-level metrics. Custom insights can be unlocked with [Phrase Data Premium](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709668525468#UUID-1a55946b-a29f-e7e8-c124-443108351c75 "Phrase Data (TMS)") that provides access to raw segment-level data.

##### Included data

- Last 6 months, starting January 1, 2025 (when tracking began)
- Language AI only, since QPS is only available for MT translations processed via Language AI
- All Language AI segments, regardless of the source (pre-translation or editor suggestions)
- QPS scores are the original scores given after translation via Language AI, not after edit by linguist.
- Buyers (not vendors) see data for shared projects

###### Filtering long editing times

Occasionally, segments have unusually long editing times. This can be due to distractions (e.g., checking a phone or taking a break). To maintain data accuracy, the average editing time is ~20 seconds. A 50% buffer is applied and excludes segments with editing times longer than 30 seconds.

While some long edits may be legitimate, most are outliers and introduce noise.

Impact of filtering:

- On large datasets, filtering these long segments has minimal impact.
- On smaller datasets, the effect is more pronounced since a single prolonged edit can disproportionately affect total editing time.

This filtering ensures cleaner and more reliable time tracking data.

##### Chart descriptions

- Chart 1: MT segments by QPS

  Displays the distribution of segment volumes based on their QPS score within the selected timeframe.
- Chart 2: Percentage of edited MT segments by QPS

  Shows the percentage of segments that were edited by linguists. Higher QPS scores are expected to have fewer edits.
- Chart 3: Average [editing time](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/18931688168476#UUID-b6c94775-512f-1559-dde5-a757368e29f9) by QPS for edited MT segments

  Shows how much time linguists spend editing segments.
- Chart 4: Average editing time by QPS across all MT segments

  Includes both edited and unedited segments (segments with 0 editing time). This provides a clearer picture of the overall effort spent on all processed segments, combining insights from the previous two charts.
- Chart 5: Words not needing human review by reducing the QPS threshold

  Estimates the number of auto-approved words that won’t require human verification if the QPS threshold is lowered. For example, if the QPS threshold decreases from 95 to 90, the average number of auto-approved words may increase from 950 to 1,750.

  ![QPS Dashboard Threshold Example](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682327071260)
- Chart 6: Editing time saved by reducing the QPS threshold

  Shows how much editing time could be saved if the QPS threshold is reduced.
- Chart 7: Percentage of auto-confirmed, auto-locked, and edited MT segments over time

  Tracks the reduction in edited segments over time by comparing the percentage of automated segments (auto-confirmed or auto-locked) with that of edited MT segments. It shows how automation is improving efficiency by reducing the number of segments that require manual editing.

#### Quality Dashboard

##### Available for

- Business and Enterprise plans

Get in touch with [Sales](https://phrase.com/demo/) for licensing questions.

##### Available for

- Ultimate and Enterprise plans (Legacy)

Get in touch with [Sales](https://phrase.com/demo/) for licensing questions.

The dashboard focuses on [LQA](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709599557020#UUID-57c78462-458b-cc16-fd64-bf052b015217 "Language Quality Assessment (TMS)") features and includes results from finished assessments presented in their own row. The assessment result may or may not include issues and the charts are based on the job creation date .

Dashboard provides insights on:

- Average quality score across an organization and the number of errors over time.
- Which categories have the highest severity LQA errors.
- Which providers maintain a high quality score.
- Number of errors by severity for each project.
- How the quality score is performing by language pair and client over time.

The LQA error counts include repeated issues. Repeated and non-repeated issues are displayed separately in by project and by provider tables.

There is a toggle between LQA and Auto LQA insights.

The "Average LQA score" shown in the dashboard is calculated as a plain average of the LQA score across all included assessments: the sum of the individual assessment scores divided by the number of assessments. The calculation does not apply any weighting based on word count, segment count, or any other factor. Assessments with no score are excluded from the calculation. All finished assessments with a score are included in the average, regardless of whether the assessment passed or failed.

#### Quotes Dashboard

##### Available for

- Team, Professional, Business and Enterprise plans

Get in touch with [Sales](https://phrase.com/demo/) for licensing questions.

The dashboard shows Vendor quotation information for job payments and includes all [quotes](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709635877020#UUID-317de099-f8f9-9c94-dde1-36018cb96947) in new, approved, for approval, and declined status.

Quotes of deleted projects are excluded from the dashboard.

- Minimum Price is the minimum price set for all the jobs within the quote.
- Price is the price incurred for each job within the quote.
- Actual Price shows the actual cost paid, split equally between all the job workflow steps, language pairs, etc.

Included in the dashboard (and [quotes table](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/27529207288476#UUID-7b47aa44-56e2-41ff-9613-555128eb6a75 "Phrase Data: Table Definitions")):

- Quotes for jobs split equally across all workflow steps. This includes quotes for split jobs with just one workflow step.
- Quotes created before the splitting.

Not included in the dashboard (and quotes table):

- Quotes for jobs split unequally across all workflow steps.

#### Savings Dashboard

##### Available for

- Team, Professional, Business and Enterprise plans

Get in touch with [Sales](https://phrase.com/demo/) for licensing questions.

This dashboard compares the raw and net price from a [quote](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709635877020#UUID-317de099-f8f9-9c94-dde1-36018cb96947) to calculate relevant savings.

When the minimum price is higher than the calculated price, the minimum price is used in the quote. In this case, the savings equal zero, as the [net rate scheme](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709665578908#UUID-271da169-10bc-f829-9b5d-421d21407b8f) is not relevant for the minimum price.

If a minimum charge fee exists, the word count calculation is no longer applied.

##### Note

In the legacy Savings dashboard, when the minimum price is 0, savings are considered as the difference between raw and net price.

#### Time Dashboard

This dashboard focuses on on-time vs overdue job delivery based on the job date created and job due date. The Time dashboard includes all on-time and overdue jobs which have a due date, and whose last status is not *cancelled*, *declined* or *rejected by linguist*.

If the job is not yet marked as completed, then the job due date is compared with the current date.

There are two prerequisites for data to be visualized in this dashboard:

- Jobs require a due date.
- With the exception for the Average job duration chart, jobs need to follow the correct status order - new, emailed, accepted, and completed:

  - Date/time of job emailed is less or equal to the date/time of job accepted by provider.
  - Date/time of job accepted by provider is less than or equal to the date/time of job delivered or job completed by provider.

As a job can go through the same status multiple times, calculation is based on the first instance of assignment and the last instance of acceptance and completion.

##### Note

All job workflow steps are counted in the Jobs by status chart. For example, if the job has a *translation* step and a *revision* step, each of them is counted with their separate status (which may or may not be different).

The dashboard provides insight on:

- The number of on-time and overdue jobs over time.
- Tracking of job delivery based on metadata - i.e., clients and domains.
- Which projects are on-track and which are not.
- Which clients and providers tending to perform well.
- The average time taken for jobs to be assigned, accepted, and completed split by language pair. This provides an understanding of the languages that typically take more or less time in each state.
- The average editing time per workflow step.

If using [Phrase Data](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709668525468#UUID-1a55946b-a29f-e7e8-c124-443108351c75 "Phrase Data (TMS)"), the status naming is different and correlates as:

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **In Phrase Data** | **In TMS application** |
| emailed | Emailed to provider |
| assigned | Accepted by provider |
| completed, completed\_by\_linguist | Delivered,  Completed by provider |

#### TM Threshold Dashboard

##### Available for

- Team, Professional, Business and Enterprise plans

Get in touch with [Sales](https://phrase.com/demo/) for licensing questions.

##### Available for

- Team, Ultimate and Enterprise plans (Legacy)

Get in touch with [Sales](https://phrase.com/demo/) for licensing questions.

The following criteria is applied to the data:

- Segments pre-translated by TM or MT are included. Segments pre-translated by TM must be confirmed.
- A segment with multiple job parts is considered and counted as one segment. The sum of editing time is taken from segments across all job parts, and takes into account the [thinking time](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/18931688168476#UUID-b6c94775-512f-1559-dde5-a757368e29f9).
- Segments with more than 30 seconds of editing time are not included in the editing time averages, but are included in the count of the pre-translated segments chart.
- Segments from jobs where all job parts were at some point completed or completed\_by\_linguist are included.
- Segments that were created in the previous 6 calendar months and within the current month are included.

Charts highlight:

- Average editing time by TM match category

  This chart shows the average editing time of a pre-translated segment. For segments pre-translated by TM, it shows the editing time by TM match category score. For segments pre-translated by MT, the horizontal line shows the average editing time of MT segments. This should help to indicate the optimal value to set the threshold.

  - Segments that are not edited are included with 0 editing time.
  - TM match scores are grouped into categories (0-69%, 70-74%,..., 95-99%, 100-101%) in order to better present the data.
- Average editing time by month

  This chart shows the overall average editing time of a pre-translated segment from all sources. This could be used to check if the changes of the threshold have an impact. Adjusting the threshold value should result in a lower editing time.
- TM segments by TM match category

  This chart shows how many segments are going through pre-translation and the match category score returned by the TM.

Filters include:

- Date - which is the date the segment is created.

  - It is set to 6 months by default, to align with the criteria used for the [Phrase TM threshold](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/16057517629852#UUID-22373687-0c7d-80bf-7a0a-f0fd7a3508b0) value recommendation.
- Project template
- Domain ([project metadata](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709748435484#UUID-30234837-9796-c6f2-1a21-a623b67ac6cc))
- Subdomain (project metadata)
- Target locale (project metadata)

These charts provide insights to help minimize linguistic effort by identifying the optimal TM threshold, and should serve as a starting point for capitalizing on automation. Setting several filter combinations may result in displaying a small subset of segments which may not contain enough data to provide conclusive insights.

#### Volume Dashboard

The word count takes into account all source words processed (uploaded) in TMS such as when a submission has been made, a job is created or when the continuous localization and update source have been done. Adjust the dashboard filter to include trashed or deleted jobs. With continuous jobs, calculation is based on all the source words in the last version.

The dashboard provides insight on processed word count:

- Words used up throughout subscription.
- Word consumption month on month.
- How words are distributed between providers.
- Which language pairs occupy the highest word volume.
- Word volume split by metadata such as clients and domains.

Word count by project creators or job creators can be displayed through customizable charts available in [advanced analytics](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/7756614696988#UUID-4cac50d9-b52a-30fb-ba52-2e1dd66b9989 "Advanced Analytics (TMS)").

If required, it is possible to view charts based on *character* or [billed word](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/14409846225308#UUID-c7fcec5b-77fb-1cd1-ecc4-f40318292402 "Cost-Effective Word Management (TMS)") count instead of word count. Select the desired metric through the Unit count toggle to display relevant data in the charts.

#### Word Count

Due to different counting methods across different languages, word count as presented may not be the same as word counts produced by other applications.

Word count for analysis is different from the character count used for [MT calculation](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/11530492252444#UUID-3c8ba1b3-290a-5451-ba45-71797af5a755) and from the number of [TMS processed words](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/14409846225308#UUID-c7fcec5b-77fb-1cd1-ecc4-f40318292402 "Cost-Effective Word Management (TMS)") used for subscription billing.

- Each join tag is replaced with one space.
- Other tags are removed.

In languages using a [whitespace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitespace_character) for separating words (e.g., English):

- Each number sequence including `+-,.` is replaced with one character (using [regex](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709636670364#UUID-fecec79b-8d0e-daaa-3327-8435094210ec) expression `[+-]?[0-9]+([., -]?[0-9]++)*+`).
- Each sequence of whitespaces is replaced with one space.
- Whitespaces at the beginning and the end of segment are removed.
- Each sequence of characters different from space is counted as one word.

In Languages not using whitespace for separating words (e.g., Japanese):

- Some punctuation marks are removed from the text (using regex expression `[\u2000-\u206F\u2E00-\u2E7F\u3000-\u3004\u3006-\u301F\\p{P}]`).
- Segment is split into sequences of characters belonging to non whitespace (NWS) Han, Hiragana, Katakana, and Thai scripts and sequences of characters not belonging to those scripts (WS).
- Total number of words = (number of words from NWS) + (number of words from WS).
- Number of words from WS is computed as for English.
- Number of words for NWS is number of characters without whitespaces.
- For Thai, the number of words is number of characters without whitespaces divided by 2.

If other dashboard criteria are required, a [feature request](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/community/topics/6254476117020-TMS-Analytics) is welcomed.

### Advanced Analytics (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/7756614696988-Advanced-Analytics-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-09-17T06:14:43Z  
> Labels: 2BTr

#### Available for

- Business and Enterprise plans

Get in touch with [Sales](https://phrase.com/demo/) for licensing questions.

#### Available for

- Ultimate and Enterprise plans (Legacy)

Get in touch with [Sales](https://phrase.com/demo/) for licensing questions.

Advanced Analytics provide a self-service reporting solution with customizable charts and dashboards to create analytics reports according to business needs.

In line with our internal [data storage](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/17019781874076#UUID-99ae6922-df28-38ae-ea89-7f7fac88a538) policy, any customer-input text (e.g. project names, file names, domains) from permanently deleted content does not appear in Phrase Advanced Analytics. Permanently deleted content is replaced with “Deleted”. All numerical values, dates, timestamps, boolean data types from permanently deleted content remain available. This ensures that historical KPIs, trends, and forecasting aggregations remain consistent over time.

Data reports are available for the past 12 full months, allowing users to have a full year at any point in time.

Shared content that has been deleted is not guaranteed to remain visible for any organization other than the content owner.

- Data is shown in UTC timezone.
- Dashboards are refreshed twice daily:

  - 12:00am and 12:00pm UTC for the EU instance
  - 07:00am and 19:00pm UTC for the US instance

  Each dashboard shows the time of the last data refresh completion. It is important to note that the displayed timestamp may not include data generated up to 3 hours prior. This is because transactions may not be captured in time when the data refresh process is triggered.

**Use cases**

Use cases focus on optimizing throughput, performance, cost, timeliness, and quality. Use the data to:

- Monitor translation volumes by project, language, and vendor
- Track on-time vs. overdue deliveries at each workflow step
- Measure leverage and savings from Translation Memory (TM) and Machine Translation (MT)
- Evaluate quality scores and error types by language and vendor, and more
- Analyze cost breakdowns by project, language, and vendor, and more
- Review vendor performance, including cost, word volume processed, and editing time

##### Tip

Ready-made dashboards for standard metrics, including MT usage, cost, volume, leverage, savings, time, quality, quotes, and TM threshold, each with its own filters, are available through [Analytics dashboards](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/6554447243036#UUID-4135ba9f-d25a-d679-73a7-ae473cd19a36 "Analytics Dashboards (TMS)").

|  |
| --- |
| [Eingebettetes Video/Inhalt](https://www.youtube.com/embed/eymkY0qgtFo) |

##### Note

Due to continuous improvements, the user interface may not be exactly the same as presented in the video.

Advanced Analytics is accessed from the Phrase Analytics button on the navigation panel. From the [analytics](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/6554447243036#UUID-4135ba9f-d25a-d679-73a7-ae473cd19a36 "Analytics Dashboards (TMS)") page, select the Advanced tab to display the Self-service reporting page.

|  |
| --- |
| adv_analytics__2_.jpeg |

The Self-service reporting page shows an embedded version of [Metabase](https://www.metabase.com/), an open-source business intelligence platform, with a homepage including:

- A navigation sidebar with the following sections:

  - COLLECTIONS, where all personal or shared charts and dashboards are stored.
  - DATA, which lists available data sources.

    To learn more about available tables and relevant fields, follow these steps:

    1. Select Databases/ANALYTICS.
    2. Hover over the desired table.
    3. Click on the book icon ![Table Details](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682374344476).

       The table's details page is displayed.
    4. Select Fields on this table.

       A list of all the fields within the chosen table is displayed, including their description and data type.
- Bookmarks displayed at the top of the navigation sidebar, if any.
- New button at the top right, enabling users to [create a chart](https://www.metabase.com/learn/metabase-basics/querying-and-dashboards/questions) (Question), [create a dashboard](https://www.metabase.com/learn/metabase-basics/querying-and-dashboards/dashboards) or a new folder (Collection).

Personal charts and dashboards are visible only to the user who created them, and can be edited and saved without affecting other users. Charts and dashboards saved in the Shared Collection can be accessed and edited by other users within the same organization. As this content is shared, do not include personal data in the naming of charts, dashboards and labels in the shared collection.

Customize charts and dashboards by selecting filters, sorting and aggregating data upon creation or edit. Different [visualization](https://www.metabase.com/learn/metabase-basics/querying-and-dashboards/visualization) types (e.g. line, pie, funnel, bar, etc.) can be also applied to charts and dashboards.

##### Note

Metabase application's version and functionalities available in Phrase Analytics may differ from the latest version and features released by Metabase.

Full documentation about how to use Metabase features available in Advanced Analytics can be found [here](https://www.metabase.com/learn/getting-started/getting-started).

##### User permissions

An administrator sets each project manager's Analytics access level in [user](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5793349215900#UUID-09f99b48-09c7-b144-42bb-a1bfd2e7d452) settings. Three levels are available:

- View all organization data.
- View only data from projects the project manager owns.
- No dashboard access.

Phrase Advanced Analytics does not include the native SQL query editor in Metabase. Build charts and dashboards using the visual query builder (Join Data, Filter, and Summarize steps) against the same underlying tables. Creating, editing, or automating charts and dashboards in Advanced Analytics via API is not supported.

Public link sharing for dashboards and questions is not available in Advanced Analytics. This applies to all users, including Admins and the creator of the dashboard or question, since Admin access to the underlying Metabase instance is managed only by Phrase.

##### Tip

Deleted jobs are moved to the recycle bin for 30 days, during which they remain visible in Advanced Analytics. After 30 days — or if the recycle bin is emptied manually — customer-input text is replaced with "Deleted"; numerical values, dates, timestamps and boolean data types remain available.
