### Phrase Data (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709668525468-Phrase-Data-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-07-01T06:12:53Z  
> Labels: 2BTr, ar_tms

Phrase Data is available in two tiers:

- Basic

  #### Available for

  - Team, Professional, Business, Enterprise and Software UI/UX plans

  Get in touch with [Sales](https://phrase.com/demo/) for licensing questions.
- Premium

  The Premium tier offers the same access as the Basic tier, plus access to segment-level data.

  #### Available for

  - Business and Enterprise plans

  Get in touch with [Sales](https://phrase.com/demo/) for licensing questions.

  #### Available for

  - Enterprise plan (Legacy)

  Get in touch with [Sales](https://phrase.com/demo/) for licensing questions.

Cloud data warehouses (such as [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/)) enable customers to securely access their data through an SQL interface.

Phrase Data displays data relevant to the customer's usage of TMS from the date the customer first subscribed to Phrase to the present date. Phrase reserves the right to change the period for which the data is displayed, upon notice to the customer.

Full [technical documentation](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/27529207288476#UUID-7b47aa44-56e2-41ff-9613-555128eb6a75 "Phrase Data: Table Definitions") of the Phrase Data integration.

Phrase Data aids strategic decision-making, demonstrates business impact and can justify investments. Data can be combined with broader company metrics to reveal impact on revenue, market penetration, and customer satisfaction:

- Web traffic, such as page views, bounce rates, user demographics.
- Marketing data, such as click-through rates, conversion rates, social media engagement
- Customer support data, analyze whether localized support materials lead to faster issue resolution and higher customer satisfaction.
- Sales figures, comparing the costs with revenue generated from localized content.

Insights help to understand the reach and reputation of global content globally and ensures a company’s message succeeds across languages.

- **Return on Investment (ROI) of Localization Efforts**

  Used to support maintaining or increasing budgets by proving that investments in translation drives returns. It also points out cost savings such as how using machine translation saved money over time contributes to overall ROI.
- **Content Adaptation, Efficacy, and User Engagement**

  Understand how localized content performs with audiences. Tracking customer retention in each locale suggests that the translations are meeting user needs. This feedback can influence a team’s quality strategy or how to adjust style to better resonate with local users. A customer use case correlates content adaptations with engagement metrics. By using different prompts with AutoAdapt to personalize content based on demographics (e.g. age, gender, region, language), this would then track performance uplift at a local or campaign level.
- **Market and Language Prioritization**

  Helps decide which languages or regions to focus on for maximum impact. It ensures the team allocates resources to translations that yield the greatest business return. May also guide the sequence of new language rollouts or justify localization for markets where they want to grow.
- **Process Optimization & Technology Strategy**

  Evaluating workflow duration and automation impact leads to continuous process improvements and helping choose the right technology. Measuring how increased use of machine translation in terms of quality and speed (e.g. post-editing time and quality scores) quantifies productivity gains.
- **Internal Performance Benchmarking**

  Over time, internal benchmarks such as average cost per word, average turnaround for a given content type, and average quality score become strategic targets for improvement. It reveals the results of smart practices and efficiency gains which further justify localization programs.

Connect Phrase Data with Orchestrator workflows to run heavy queries and advanced automations more efficiently. The [Orchestrator integration](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/22646379858716#UUID-b04ba7af-e13a-2a67-a347-567d81e4522e) also helps streamline quality checks and process optimization by sampling projects or identifying jobs that match specific criteria more quickly.

#### Basic Tier Use Cases

In any industry that relies on translation and linguistic localization, teams need robust data insights to guide decisions. However, analytics reporting and insights differ by team needs (Localization, Content, Executive Stakeholder) who require operational metrics (day-to-day efficiency, throughput, costs) and strategic insights (long-term ROI, user impact, market growth).

Operational analytics help localization managers streamline workflows and manage costs on a daily basis.

- Volume (also known as throughput)

  Tracking the amount of content translated over time (e.g. words per week/month) indicates the team’s capacity. This helps with resource planning.
- Timeliness (also known as turnaround time)

  Turnaround time measures how long it takes to translate content from start to finish. Localization teams track whether translations are delivered on schedule or face delays. This is crucial for meeting product launch dates, SLAs, and investigating delays.
- Vendor and linguist performance

  If external translation vendors or freelance linguists are used, the localization team will want to evaluate their performance. Metrics like turnaround time per vendor, on-time delivery per vendor and quality scores per linguist are tracked.
- Quality metrics ([Linguistic Quality Assurance](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/27529737766044#UUID-8c8a9e28-99dd-f432-f780-331192127c69))

  Measure the percentage of translations that pass QA checks on the first attempt (no rework needed), indicating effective initial translation. Similarly, detailing the category and severity of the error issues found e.g. terminology, accuracy, etc.
- Cost and efficiency metrics

  Typically teams track cost per word and total spend by project, language, or department to ensure budgets are met. As well as savings to compare raw translation cost vs. discounted cost after applying a net rate scheme highlighting the value of maintaining TM matches and repetitions.  For example, if 30% of words in a new project were translated via 100% TM matches, the team can quantify the cost saved by not retranslating those segments.
- Leverage of Automation (MT and TM)

  - Post-editing effort, such as the average edits or time needed on MT outputs, to help evaluate MT.
  - TM leverage rate by looking at the % of content by TM matches, which indicates TM reuse efficiency and cost savings.
  - MT usage rate such as  the % of segments initially translated by MT. This presents automation coverage and opportunities for cost/time reduction – Premium only.

#### Premium Tier Use Cases

##### Translation Memory (TM) utilization

Track when a TM was last used and how many segments were reused over time. This helps assess TM freshness, value contribution, and whether outdated TMs are still worth maintaining.

Suggested analysis:

- Use segment\_statistic\_v2 and filter on `translation_origin = TM`.

  - A TM can be identified using the `translation_memory_id`.
  - Aggregate segments by TM, and use the `date_created` field to see when the TM was used. It is also good to calculate and see the average `editing_time_ms` and `score`.
- Join with job\_v2 using the `job_id` to extract language information e.g. `target_locale`.
- Join with project\_v2 using the `project_id` to contextualize usage by domain, client, business unit, etc.

Benefits:

- **Cost savings:** Helps sunset unused or low-performing TMs to reduce maintenance overhead.
- **Quality:** Identifies aging TMs with high post-editing effort, and flags suitable action.
- **Efficiency:** Use high-performing TMs that reduce edit time and increase auto-confirmation. Look into adjusting the TM threshold accordingly.

##### Machine Translation (MT) engine optimization

Compare MT engines by QPS (quality score per segment) and post-editing time, allowing for a more intelligent routing of content to the right MT engine.

Suggested analysis:

- Use  segment\_statistic\_v2 with filter on `translation_origin = MT`.
- Join with machine\_translate\_setting\_v2 using the `machine_translate_setting_id`.

  - An MT engine can be identified using the `machine_translate_setting_name`.
  - Aggregate segments by MT engine and calculate the sum of `segment_id`, the average QPS, and the average `editing_time_ms`.
- Join with job\_v2 using the `job_id` to extract language information e.g. `target_locale`.
- Join with project\_v2 for different content types like domain, client, business unit, etc.

Benefits:

- **Lower Cost:** Identify and use the right engines for the job that are most suitable for content type and language with historically low edit rates.
- **Quantify turnaround time:** By looking into the editing times per language pair, content type, etc.

##### Maximize auto-confirm segments (i.e. no touch content)

Identify the most efficient point where high QPS and no editing time is eligible for auto-confirmation so to separate as much content as possible from requiring human review.

Suggested analysis:

- Use  segment\_statistic\_v2:

  - Filter where segment `translation_origin = MT`, `is_confirmed = true`, `editing_time_ms = 0`, and `confirmation_source = MT`.
  - Aggregate segment count (`segment_id`),word count (`words_processed`) by `QPS`.
  - Join with job\_v2 using the `job_id` to extract language information e.g. `target_locale`.
  - Join with project\_v2 using the `project_id` to extract content metadata.

Benefits:

- **Cost Savings:** Find the optimal QPS threshold to increase auto-confirmation and reduce editing time where the quality is already good enough.
- **Reduce turnaround time:** Avoid content being unnecessarily reviewed.

#### Query templates

Sample queries to use as a guide to help get started with the relevant tables:

##### Pre-translated MT output from month to month

```
SELECT
    ssv.qps
    ,DATE(DATE_TRUNC('month', ssv.date_created)) AS date_month
    ,COUNT(DISTINCT segment_id) AS mt_segments
FROM segment_statistic_v2 ssv
WHERE
    ssv.date_created >= DATEADD('day', -365, CURRENT_DATE)
    AND ssv.date_created < CURRENT_DATE
    AND ssv.translation_origin = 'mt' -- segments pre-translated by MT
GROUP BY
    ssv.qps
    ,DATE(DATE_TRUNC('month', ssv.date_created));
```

##### Pre-translated MT quality variation across custom project metadata

```
SELECT
    ssv.qps
    ,pcmv.custom_field_name
    ,pcmv.custom_field_values
    ,COUNT(DISTINCT segment_id) AS mt_segments
FROM segment_statistic_v2 ssv
JOIN job_v2 jv
    ON ssv.job_id = jv.job_id
JOIN project_custom_metadata_v2 pcmv
    ON jv.project_id = pcmv.project_id
WHERE
    ssv.date_created >= DATEADD('day', -28, CURRENT_DATE)
    AND ssv.date_created < CURRENT_DATE
    AND ssv.translation_origin = 'mt' -- segments pre-translated by MT
GROUP BY
    ssv.qps
    ,pcmv.custom_field_name
    ,pcmv.custom_field_values;
```

##### Pre-translated MT quality variation across locales

```
SELECT
    ssv.qps
    ,jv.locale_pair
    ,COUNT(DISTINCT segment_id) AS mt_segments
FROM segment_statistic_v2 ssv
JOIN job_v2 jv
    ON ssv.job_id = jv.job_id
WHERE
    ssv.date_created >= DATEADD('day', -28, CURRENT_DATE)
    AND ssv.date_created < CURRENT_DATE
    AND ssv.translation_origin = 'mt' -- segments pre-translated by MT
GROUP BY
    ssv.qps
    ,jv.locale_pair;
```

##### Pre-translated MT volume and quality

```
SELECT
    ssv.qps
    ,mtsv.machine_translate_setting_type
    ,COUNT(DISTINCT segment_id) AS mt_segments
FROM segment_statistic_v2 ssv
JOIN machine_translate_setting_v2 mtsv
    ON ssv.machine_translate_setting_id = mtsv.machine_translate_setting_id
WHERE
    ssv.date_created >= DATEADD('day', -28, CURRENT_DATE)
    AND ssv.date_created < CURRENT_DATE
    AND ssv.translation_origin = 'mt' -- segments pre-translated by MT
GROUP BY
    ssv.qps
    ,mtsv.machine_translate_setting_type;
```

##### Quantity of pre-translated MT segments auto-confirmed by QPS

```
SELECT
    qps
    ,COUNT(DISTINCT segment_id) AS mt_segments
    ,COUNT(DISTINCT IFF(LOWER(confirmation_source) IN ('mt', 'tm', 'nt', 'ir', 'ut'), segment_id, NULL)) AS mt_segments_autoconfirmed
FROM segment_statistic_v2
WHERE
    date_created >= DATEADD('day', -28, CURRENT_DATE)
    AND date_created < CURRENT_DATE
    AND translation_origin = 'mt' -- segments pre-translated by MT
GROUP BY
    qps;
```

##### Quantity of pre-translated MT segments edited by QPS

```
SELECT
    qps
    ,COUNT(DISTINCT segment_id) AS mt_segments
    ,COUNT(DISTINCT IFF(COALESCE(editing_time_ms, 0) > 0, segment_id, NULL)) AS mt_segments_edited
FROM segment_statistic_v2
WHERE
    date_created >= DATEADD('day', -28, CURRENT_DATE)
    AND date_created < CURRENT_DATE
    AND translation_origin = 'mt' -- segments pre-translated by MT
GROUP BY
    Qps;
```

##### Quantity of words saved from human review by reducing the QPS threshold

```
WITH qps_segments AS (
    SELECT
        ssv.qps
        ,SUM(words_processed) AS words_processed
    FROM segment_statistic_v2 ssv
    WHERE
        ssv.date_created >= DATEADD('day', -28, CURRENT_DATE)
        AND ssv.date_created < CURRENT_DATE
        AND ssv.translation_origin = 'mt' -- segments pre-translated by MT
    GROUP BY
        ssv.qps
)

SELECT
    qps AS new_qps_threshold
    ,SUM(words_processed) OVER (ORDER BY qps DESC) AS words_saved
FROM qps_segments;
```

### Phrase Data: Table Definitions

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/27529207288476-Phrase-Data-Table-Definitions  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-09-01T06:13:53Z

- Host: dx66025.eu-west-1.snowflakecomputing.com
- Database: CUSTOMER\_SHARES
- Database Management System: Snowflake

###### Timezone

Data is displayed in the user’s local timezone.

###### Refresh rate

- V2: Once a day at 07:00 UTC for both EU and US
- V1: Daily by 9:00 CET

Data generated up to 3 hours before this timestamp may be excluded.

###### Data retention

Phrase Data displays data relevant to the customer’s usage of TMS from the date the customer first subscribed to the present date. Phrase reserves the right to change the period for which the data is displayed, upon notice to customer.

In line with our internal [data storage](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/17019781874076#UUID-99ae6922-df28-38ae-ea89-7f7fac88a538) policy, any customer-input text (e.g. project names, file names, domains) from permanently deleted content does not appear in Phrase Data. Permanently deleted content is anonymized and replaced with “Deleted” after 14 days. All numerical values, dates, timestamps, boolean data types from permanently deleted content remain available and table connections are maintained. This ensures that historical KPIs, trends, and forecasting aggregations remain consistent over time.

These fields are available in all Phrase Data tables:

- `is_historical` identifies whether the main entity represented by the table was permanently removed from the Phrase Platform.
- `is_anonymized` tracks whether customer-input text tied to the main entity represented by the table was permanently deleted and replaced with Deleted.

#### Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD) (TMS)

This ERD provides a clear overview of the data structure and how the tables are connected to one another in Phrase Strings. The visual serves as a representation to help understand the data relationships.

![Phrase Data Relationships](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682340257308)

#### analysis\_compare\_job\_part\_v2 (TMS)

View ANALYSIS\_COMPARE\_JOB\_PART\_V2 provides data from compare [analyses](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709712007708) run on job parts. Analysis results are split into standard Phrase match categories:

- Comparison 100, 95, 85, 75, 50, 0
- Repetitions
- Total

For each match category, we provide counts of

- Characters · Characters with spaces
- Pages (norm pages)
- Segments
- Words
- Percentages

Data for Pre- and Post- analysis are stored in a separate view `ANALYSIS_JOB_PART_V2`.

For each job part, data for all analyses are stored. If an analysis is recalculated, only the last version is kept. To include data for regular project only, it is necessary to join the table with table `PROJECT_V2` and filter the data by `PROJECT_CLASS_TYPE` and select only the value `Standard`.

#### job\_mt\_metrics\_v1 (TMS)

This table is only available to the Phrase Data EU instance.

The JOB\_MT\_METRICS\_V1 contains MT metrics for each relevant job. There are multiple conditions that a job must meet in order to be included here, and for the feedback score to be non-zero:

- The document translation must be finished (all segments have been confirmed, level &gt; 0).
- At least 10 seconds must be spent in the document on post-editing.
- Segments are only included if their editing time exceeds 250 ms.
- If Phrase Translate is not used in the project, your default MT profile must have at least one engine enabled.

| Column Name | Column Type | Column Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BLEU | FLOAT | BLEU MT metric |
| CHRF3 | FLOAT | chrf3 MT metric |
| DOMAIN\_LABEL | TEXT | Name of the domain our automated system gave to the job by analyzing its content. |
| JOB\_ID | NUMBER | The ID of the job, you can join this to the id column in the job\_v1 table. |
| MACHINE\_TRANSLATE\_SETTINGS\_ID | NUMBER | The ID of the MT setting, identifying the MT engine that contributed the most to the scores (usually there should be only one). You can join to the ID column in the machine\_translate\_setting\_v2 table to get more info about the MT engine. |
| MT\_SEGMENT\_COUNT | NUMBER | The number of segments which were taken into account when calculating the 3 metrics. If this is zero, it means the MT metrics for this job are irrelevant/do not apply. |
| ORGANIZATION\_ID | NUMBER | Organization ID |
| TER | FLOAT | TER MT metric capped to 1 |
| WORKFLOW\_STEP\_ID | NUMBER | The ID of the workflow step the metrics were calculated on/for |
| DOCUMENT\_STATUS | TEXT | Status of the document and can  contain one of the following values:  - NEW: Represents a newly added document where a recommendation has been made, but none of the segments have been confirmed yet. - SKIPPED\_UNCONFIRMED: Indicates that some segments of the document have been confirmed, but not the entire document. Such documents are skipped when computing MT metrics. - SKIPPED\_LOW\_EDITING\_TIME: Denotes a confirmed document with low overall editing time. Such documents are skipped when computing MT metrics. - CONFIRMED: Represents a confirmed document where machine translation (MT) metrics have been calculated. This is the typical final state when the document is post-edited, and metrics should be present. - UPDATE\_ERROR: Signifies an error that occurred during the update process, possibly preventing the document from being properly updated or processed. |

#### lqa\_v2 (TMS)

`job_id`, `job_uid`, `workflow_step_level`, and `job_part_inner_id` fields enable reliable joins between LQA data and job-related tables.

- Project buyer/project vendor

  They have access to all workflow steps, so `job_part_v2` contains one record per workflow step. To avoid duplicated assessment results, joins must include `workflow_step_level`.
- Job provider

  They typically see a single record in `job_part_v2`. Do not use `workflow_step_level` when joining assessments, as the LQA may have been created on a different workflow step and the join would fail.

  **Exceptions**

  - If acting as a provider on multiple workflow steps (e.g. translation and review), multiple records may exist. In this case, select the correct job part or use `workflow_step_level` if the applicable one is known.
  - If a job is split unevenly across workflow steps, the `job_part_inner_id` may differ between steps, and joins may not work. Handling this depends on the specific setup.

| Column Name | Column Type | Column Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ORGANIZATION\_ID | NUMBER | Organization ID |
| ASSESSMENT\_ID | NUMBER | Assessment ID |
| JOB\_PART\_ID | NUMBER | Job part ID |
| JOB\_PART\_UID | VARCHAR | Unique alphanumeric that identifies the workflow step |
| SCORE | NUMBER | LQA Score |
| CATEGORY | TEXT | Category of the issue |
| CATEGORY\_COUNT | NUMBER | Number of issues for the category |
| SUBCATEGORY | TEXT | Subcategory of the issue |
| SUBCATEGORY\_COUNT | NUMBER | Number of issues for the subcategory |
| SEVERITY | TEXT | Severity of the issue |

#### segment\_statistic\_v2 (TMS)

**Available with Phrase Data Premium**

The `segment_statistic_v2` table provides information where the translation is coming from, and its quality score generated at segment-level. It also indicates locked and confirmed segments along with their word/character count and editing time, if any. The insights from this table help to drive and increase automation in your translation processes.

For more detailed context, the table can be linked;

- to the `machine_translate_setting_v2` table, with the `machine_translate_setting_id` to include data on the MT engine
- to the `job_part_v2` table, with the `job_part_id` to include data such as workflow step status and workflow step level.
- to the `job_v2` table, with the `job_id` to include data such as file names and languages.
- and further to the `project_v2` table to include data such domain, subdomain, business unit and other metadata.
- And other tables such as `job_part_statistic_v2` and `vendor_v2` tables.

All this data leads users to take the data-backed actions, such as to;

- Optimize their workflows, weighing the value of each workflow step in terms of improved quality vs cost
- Utilize the MT engines that return higher scores, whilst balancing the ratio of quality vs MTU cost.
- Validate the most effective translation memories.
- Maximize no-touch segments for auto-confirmation and minimize linguistic effort by identifying the optimal QPS and TM threshold respectively.

Data is available for the past 12 full months including current month, allowing users to have a full year at any point in time.

| Column Name | Column Type | Column Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SEGMENT\_ID | TEXT | A unique number that identifies the segment. |
| JOB\_ID | NUMBER | A unique number that identifies the job. |
| JOB\_PART\_ID | NUMBER | A unique number that identifies the workflow step. |
| JOB\_PART\_UID | TEXT | A unique alphanumeric that identifies the workflow step. |
| DATE\_CREATED | TIMESTAMP\_LTZ | The date the segment is created. This value is read from MXLIFF. |
| DATE\_MODIFIED | TIMESTAMP\_LTZ | The date when any field is updated for the segment. This value is read from MXLIFF. |
| TRANSLATION\_ORIGIN | TEXT | Indicates whether the translation is coming from TM, MT, or NT. |
| TRANSLATION\_MEMORY\_ID | TEXT | The ID of the translation memory if the translation is coming from TM. Data available from 20th August 2024 onwards. |
| MACHINE\_TRANSLATE\_SETTING\_ID | TEXT | A unique number that identifies the machine translation engine if the translation is coming from MT, and is provided for confirmed segments only. |
| QPS | FLOAT | The Quality Performance Score (QPS) for machine translations via Phrase Language AI.  The QPS of a current version of source:target remains the same if the source and target are unchanged.  If a segment is edited, the field is set to null.  If pre-translation runs multiple times on the same workflow step, QPS is updated to reflect the most recent result. |
| SCORE | FLOAT | The score of a segment for which the target is chosen from the suggested translation coming from TM/MT/NT. |
| HIGHEST\_CONFIRMED\_WORKFLOW\_STEP\_LEVEL | NUMBER | The highest workflow step level where the segment is confirmed. |
| IS\_CONFIRMED | BOOLEAN | Indicates if the segment is confirmed or not. |
| IS\_LOCKED | BOOLEAN | Indicates if the segment is locked or not. |
| CONFIRMATION\_SOURCE | TEXT | Indicates how the segment is confirmed, whether it is from pre-translation rules (TM, MT, NT), (IR) import rules, (UT) update target, or (EX) external, which refers to manual. If NULL, then the segment is not confirmed. |
| WORKFLOW\_STEP\_LEVEL | NUMBER | A numerical value indicating the order sequence of the workflow step of the job. |
| CHARS\_PROCESSED | NUMBER | The number of source characters in a segment. |
| WORDS\_PROCESSED | NUMBER | The number of source words in a segment. |
| EDITING\_TIME\_MS | NUMBER | The time taken to edit a segment, which also includes the thinking time. |
| THINKING\_TIME\_MS | NUMBER | The time spent thinking about the translation for a segment. |
| ORGANIZATION\_ID | NUMBER |  |
| LATEST\_EDITING\_SOURCE | VARCHAR | Identifies which segments were processed by Phrase post-editing AI features or a partner integration service. |
| LOCKING\_SOURCE | VARCHAR | Identifies who/what has locked the segment. Possible values:  - `mt` - machine translation, set only by pre-translation - `tm` - translation memory, set only by pre-translation - `nt` - non-translatable, set only by pre-translation - `ir` - import rule, set during import for some file formats, by import settings - `ex` - external, set in all other cases - especially when locked via import xliff/mxlif |
| LOCKING\_SOURCE\_DETAIL | VARCHAR | Identifies the service for cases when the locked by value is `ex` - external |
| QUALITY\_ESTIMATION\_SCORE | FLOAT | This is tied to `latest_editing_source` field. It represents the QPS score generated via Phrase AI features, or the score provided by a partner service integration.  Whenever `latest_editing_source` is cleared or updated, this field (if present) should follow the same behaviour. If a later enhancement (e.g. Auto Adapt) happens afterwards, the value in this field is removed since it no longer applies. |

#### tms\_curated\_analysis\_detail\_v2 (TMS)

View TMS\_CURATED\_ANALYSIS\_DETAIL\_V2 includes data from both default and post-editing analyses, covering raw and net values. It displays information on segments, words, percentages, and editing time. It also indicates whether the analysis was created by your organization or by another organization—for example, in the case of a shared job or project. Additionally, it tracks whether the analysis is the latest one generated by your organization. Includes data for up to 12 calendar months.

| Column Name | Column Type | Column Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ORGANIZATION\_ID | NUMBER | Organization ID |
| LANGUAGE\_PAIR | TEXT | A concatenation of the source and target languages |
| LOCALE\_PAIR | TEXT | A concatenation of the source and target locales |
| WORKFLOW\_STEP\_LEVEL | NUMBER | A numerical value indicating the order sequence of the workflow step of the job |
| PROJECT\_ID | NUMBER | A unique number that identifies the project |
| PROJECT\_NAME | TEXT | The name of the project |
| PROJECT\_OWNER\_ID | NUMBER | A unique number that identifies the project owner |
| CLIENT\_NAME | TEXT | The client name |
| DOMAIN\_NAME | TEXT | The domain name |
| JOB\_STATE | TEXT | Indicates if the job is available, deleted, archived, or in the recycle bin |
| JOB\_PROVIDER | TEXT | Linguist or vendor assigned to the workflow step |

#### tms\_curated\_job\_detail\_v2 (TMS)

View TMS\_CURATED\_JOB\_DETAIL\_V2 includes data related to jobs, and a new record with a version number is created each time a job source content is updated. Includes data for up to 12 calendar months.

| Column Name | Column Type | Column Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ORGANIZATION\_ID | NUMBER | Organization ID |
| DATE\_JOB\_CREATED | TIMESTAMP\_LTZ | The date when a job was created (i.e. file uploaded with some processed words) |
| LANGUAGE\_PAIR | TEXT | A concatenation of the source and target languages |
| LOCALE\_PAIR | TEXT | A concatenation of the source and target locales |
| WORKFLOW\_STEP\_LEVEL | NUMBER | A numerical value indicating the order sequence of the workflow step of the job |
| PROJECT\_ID | NUMBER | A unique number that identifies the project |
| PROJECT\_NAME | TEXT | The name of the project |
| PROJECT\_OWNER\_ID | NUMBER | A unique number that identifies the project owner |
| CLIENT\_NAME | TEXT | The client name |
| DOMAIN\_NAME | TEXT | The domain name |
| JOB\_STATE | TEXT | Indicates if the job is available, deleted, archived, or in the recycle bin |
| PROVIDER | TEXT | Linguist or vendor assigned to the workflow step |
| UNIQUE\_ID | TEXT | Unique identifier of a provider which allows to distinguish between providers with the same name |
| WORDS\_PROCESSED | NUMBER | The number of source words uploaded and processed. If a job has several workflow steps, it only includes the count of the first workflow step. |
| PROJECT\_OWNER\_USERNAME | TEXT | The username of the project owner |
| WORKFLOW\_STEP\_DUE | TEXT | Indicates whether the workflow step is on-time or overdue in delivery. A workflow step is marked as overdue if the due date is lower than the lowest date between the highest date of completion and the highest date of delivery. |
| WORKFLOW\_STEP\_NAME | TEXT | The workflow step name of the job |
| WORDS\_COMPLETED | NUMBER | The number of source words in a segment that is marked as locked, confirmed, or both, either manually in the editor or automatically. |
| EDITING\_TIME\_S | NUMBER | The time in seconds that the provider spent editing the segments of a job |
| THINKING\_TIME\_S | NUMBER | This field tracks the time a user clicks within a target segment from the CAT editor pane and stops when the user starts editing that segment. When a user re-enters that same segment, the time continues to add to the previous value. |
| BUSINESS\_UNIT\_NAME | TEXT | The business unit name |
| COST\_CENTER\_NAME | TEXT | The cost center name |
| SUBDOMAIN\_NAME | TEXT | The subdomain name |
| PROVIDER\_FULL\_NAME | TEXT | The name and surname of the provider |
| SOURCE\_LANGUAGE | TEXT | The source language |
| TARGET\_LANGUAGE | TEXT | The target language |
| SOURCE\_LOCALE | TEXT | The source language locale |
| TARGET\_LOCALE | TEXT | The target language locale |
| PROJECT\_OWNER\_FULL\_NAME | TEXT | The name and surname of the project owner |
| PROJECT\_STATUS | TEXT | The status of the project |
| JOB\_CREATOR\_FULL\_NAME | TEXT | The name and surname of the job creator |
| WORKFLOW\_STEP\_STATUS | TEXT | The status of the workflow step |
| DATE\_DUE\_PROJECT | TIMESTAMP\_LTZ | The due date of the project |
| JOB\_CREATOR\_USERNAME | TEXT | The username of the job creator |
| JOB\_CREATOR\_ID | NUMBER | A unique number that identifies the job creator |
| PROJECT\_DUE | TEXT | Indicates whether the project is on-time or overdue in delivery |
| JOB\_ID | NUMBER | A unique number that identifies the job |
| FILE\_NAME | TEXT | The name of the uploaded file for which a job is created. This field is empty for hourly quotes. |
| FILE\_EXTENSION | TEXT | The file extension of the uploaded document |
| DATE\_COMPLETED\_PROJECT | TIMESTAMP\_LTZ | The date the project is marked as completed |
| DATE\_COMPLETED\_WORKFLOW\_STEP | TIMESTAMP\_LTZ | The date the workflow step is marked as completed |

### Cost-Effective Word Management (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/14409846225308-Cost-Effective-Word-Management-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-09-29T06:14:57Z  
> Labels: Administration, 2BTr, edited_at

##### Note

This article applies to organizations on [capacity-based plans](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/13872357395228#UUID-77729fa2-a37d-6ee7-c3a0-cba548b0384d). For organizations on credit-based plans, refer to [credit-based pricing](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/30624146191260#UUID-94ce26d4-ef00-691c-2926-13bbf8448bd1).

Managing translation resources efficiently and optimizing the usage of processed words ensures cost-effectiveness.

As soon as a file is uploaded to Phrase TMS, the number of TMS processed words is calculated as follows:

`A x B` = TMS processed words

*Where*:

- `A` is the total number of words in the source language in the uploaded content.

  - If the source language is a character-based language (e.g. Japanese, Korean, Simplified or Traditional Chinese), `A` is the total number of uploaded characters divided by two.
- `B` is the total number of languages into which the source language is translated.

Processed words are only consumed when content is imported as a job in Phrase TMS. No other additional processed words are consumed in any other function (locking segments, analysis, using translation memory matches, etc.) nor do these functions reduce the number of processed words.

**Example**

A customer has a document with 5,000 source language words `(A)` which are being translated into 5 languages `(B)`. Therefore, the total amount of processed words equals:

5,000 words `(A)` x 5 target languages `(B)` = 25,000 processed words

Platform [owners and administrators](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5793349215900#UUID-09f99b48-09c7-b144-42bb-a1bfd2e7d452) can monitor capacity usage in the Subscription overview tab of the Organization settings page.

Detailed information on consumption for specific projects or time periods is available in the Volume tab of [Phrase Analytics](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/6554447243036#UUID-4135ba9f-d25a-d679-73a7-ae473cd19a36 "Analytics Dashboards (TMS)"), where the per billed word unit count can be used.

##### Note

Use of [Job Sync](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709647502620#UUID-776d5a52-a0f8-d5c1-10b7-60bb343ef950) (adding languages) will impact total number of managed words.

**[Continuous jobs](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709711922972#UUID-ec063437-ae86-bb7b-9358-19bb3087a3c5), projects, and update of source**

If a source file is changed in continuous jobs, all words in new or altered source segments are counted as new and included in the TMS processed words count. Unchanged source segments within the same job are not included in the count, regardless of any updates to the target segments.

**[Shared scenarios](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709703948444#UUID-2fb330ab-e5ad-e017-5972-a9a75c1e0360)**

TMS processed words are deducted from the [organization](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/6091807042076#UUID-3b204035-bb79-8662-cb38-a08bb599962b) that imports the job.

If a buyer shares a project with a vendor from a different organization, the words count against the buyer's limits. The words only count towards the vendor's limits if they import additional jobs to the project. This applies to shared jobs as well.

A vendor will not see any words counted towards their TMS processed words limits when assigned to jobs shared by their buyers.

#### Best Practices for TMS Word Management

To optimize the usage of processed words in TMS, the following strategies are recommended:

- *Regular audits to optimize content*

  Regularly review and remove unused or obsolete source content from within monitored repositories. Remove languages from project templates or content repositories monitored by [Automated Project Creation](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709647363356#UUID-3fb1230d-d6b0-83ce-cb52-98b96688b553) and other integrations to avoid accidental translation.
- *Use continuous projects and jobs*

  Continuous projects and jobs provide significant savings compared to creating new projects and jobs each time.
- *Remove and avoid duplications*

  Ensure the content management system or processes do not inadvertently duplicate text across projects or departments. Be careful when importing overlapping sets of files.
- *Use Update source instead of re-importing files as new jobs*

  If files manually uploaded to create a job change slightly afterward, select the jobs and use [Tools](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/10825557848220#UUID-1601e4ba-40df-d962-11d4-e2ef301430f1)/Update source to update only the edited segments. This is also available via [API](https://cloud.memsource.com/web/docs/api).
- *Estimate Where Possible*

  When unsure if a large project will proceed, consider the following:

  - Avoid processing the documents and provide high-level cost estimates before uploading.
  - If translation memories are missing or offer minimal leverage, create jobs for one target language and use the respective [analysis](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709712007708#UUID-7ed2ed16-6064-f667-bb86-7d971d7004c9) to estimate the rest.
  - Analyze a representative subset of files, extrapolate the results, and import the remaining files only after receiving the order.
- *Use [Phrase Portal](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/12949538303516#UUID-0af9ae02-cbd1-1c17-aec5-541956f27282)*

  Phrase Portal consumes [Machine Translation Units (MTUs)](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/11530492252444#UUID-3c8ba1b3-290a-5451-ba45-71797af5a755). It only consumes TMS processed words when content is sent for human review to Phrase TMS.
- *Use technical tips to save words*

  - When importing files, upload a truncated version of the files first.
  - Instead of uploading multilingual XML, Excel, or CSV files with custom [import settings](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/sections/5709618056604) to create jobs and populate a translation memory, it is advisable to pre-process legacy content externally. This approach will produce a multilingual Excel file or ordered document pairs (in the same format) suitable for alignment.
  - For XML files, use [XML profiles](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/11560308549404#UUID-9b69b021-14c3-6a79-ecf2-10a4d4954c17) instead of a trial and error. AI assistants can help generate complex XPaths to test in the XPath tab of the XML profile in TMS.
  - To test regular expressions ([regex](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709636670364#UUID-fecec79b-8d0e-daaa-3327-8435094210ec)) on short samples, use [regexr.com](http://regexr.com), [regex101.com](http://regex101.com), or text editor plugins. For practical tutorials, visit [rexegg.com](http://rexegg.com).
  - For files processed with OCR, verify the contents and layout before import to prevent the need for reimporting corrected versions.

## Automation

### Automation (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709631713820-Automation-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-07-21T10:13:44Z  
> Labels: Automation, 2BTr

Automation is based on customized templates set for service types, project types, and due date schemes. Texts submitted through either the submitter portal or automated project creation have these templates applied to them to generate pre-configured projects. This removes the need for project managers to manually define each project.

|  |
| --- |
| Automation Workflow |

Automation workflow

To prepare for Automation, follow these steps:

1. Create a [Service](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709616197788#UUID-f021f3f3-3659-b700-c1a6-421cf8ce5b5b "Services (TMS)").
2. Create a [Project template](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709647439772#UUID-0d4861e8-5219-9b5f-3a49-4fe65f7bd211 "Project Templates (TMS)").
3. Create a [Due date scheme](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709647457308#UUID-0e2570ac-5170-51a4-945c-c5352ba81621 "Due Date Schemes (TMS)").
4. Set up [automated project creation](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709647363356#UUID-2558de58-eb7e-d298-f22a-d41dd17b1de6 "Automated Project Creation - APC (TMS)") and/or the [submitter portal](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709602111132#UUID-895c1049-1178-6c17-109b-55bc8b33a361 "Submitter Portal (TMS)").

### Choosing between AI Translation Agent and Machine Translation

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/22644545336732-Choosing-between-AI-Translation-Agent-and-Machine-Translation  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-09-29T06:13:38Z  
> Labels: Machine Translation, Automation, 2BTr, edited_at

When automating translations, either the [AI translation agent](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/20660272640284#UUID-d2f83c62-3868-1bfe-75ae-b32b718706c9) or machine translation ([Phrase Language AI](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709660879516#UUID-b0d64b4f-fa01-f7c3-006a-40e0ee0dedd2)) can be selected. Both solutions yield fast, high quality translation, but are built for different use cases.

##### AI Translation Agent

A translation service that enables zero-touch translation workflows. Unlike machine translation services, it works with project [term bases](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709733372188#UUID-ca45e09b-442e-336f-3257-2983bccd0503) and combines a context-aware AI agent that reviews and translates. The result is an accurate and refined translation.

**Recommended for:**

- Teams needing high-quality, ready-to-use output without configuring multiple MT engines.
- Content that benefits from contextual understanding like full sentences, paragraphs, or domain-specific material.
- Workflows where reducing or avoiding post-editing effort is a priority.

##### Machine Translation (Phrase Language AI)

A fast translation service that connects to leading MT engines. Choose from providers like Phrase, Google, or Amazon, or train customized engines via [Phrase Custom AI](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/7683093364508#UUID-7e94a40d-cd95-9388-1d29-cb05cb65a32f). The MT output can be improved further with human post-editing or automated workflows such as [MT Optimize](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/20397396468508#UUID-b0ff2f2f-60e8-95fa-7166-1cbfaa9e853a) (configured separately in Orchestrator).

**Recommended for:**

- Teams that want control over MT engine selection.
- High-volume or time-sensitive content where fast delivery is key.
- Workflows that include human post-editing or a custom MT setup.

##### Comparison table

|  | Choose AI translation agent | Choose Phrase Language AI |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Setup | Ready to use | Requires configuring [MT profiles](https://support.phrase.com/document/preview/21505#UUID-8139f165-9c79-2540-f81a-e117c38aad03) or adding MT engines |
| Terminology support | Term base support | [MT Glossary](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709675486876#UUID-7e625233-8ae7-ac05-e4b6-a82056604355) support |
| Specific MT engine support | Not available | Configurable MT profiles |
| Quality | Automated refinement included via AI Translation Agent's own built-in review step performed as part of producing the translation | Relies on human review or additional setup (e.g. via MT Optimize) |
| Capacity used | AI units ([AIU](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/14032731809052#UUID-cc9cfa45-5b73-500c-edfc-a3b77c44713f)s)/credits consumed | Machine translations units ([MTU](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/11530492252444#UUID-3c8ba1b3-290a-5451-ba45-71797af5a755)s)/credits consumed |

### Automated Project Creation - APC (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709647363356-Automated-Project-Creation-APC-TMS

Get in touch with [Sales](https://phrase.com/demo/) for licensing questions.

|  |

| [Eingebettetes Video/Inhalt](https://www.youtube.com/embed/zVhki1kE1Kg) |

Due to continuous improvements, the user interface may not be exactly the same as presented in the video.

#### Set Up Automated Project Creation

Automated project creation rules allow the configuration of how Phrase monitors specific folders via an [integration](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709656492572#UUID-98e00ebc-37ac-490b-1577-e8f108fa5a9b) connector and creates new projects if new or updated content is detected within them.

**[Project templates:](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709647439772#UUID-0d4861e8-5219-9b5f-3a49-4fe65f7bd211 "Project Templates (TMS)")**

- Most APC settings are handled in project templates. The project template defines file destinations, source and target languages and workflow steps. Process and financial details are also defined in the project template such as providers and the generation of quotes and analyses.
- Separate APCs can share the same project template, but each APC still creates its own project. Jobs from files or folders monitored by different APCs are not combined into a single project.
- APC-created projects are exclusive to that APC. APC can only import jobs into TMS projects that the APC itself created; they cannot import a job into a separate, pre-existing TMS project that was created manually or by another process.

**Exporting translations back to the repository:**

- Jobs are exported when the project status is set to Completed.
- Jobs can be manually exported by choosing Download > Export to online repository. Even unchanged files will be exported.
- Each target file is stored in a target path specified in APC settings.

**Re-importing:**

- Jobs can be re-imported from the Download menu on the [jobs table](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/10825571430172#UUID-f3d84af4-6f87-460d-3d81-594a257660ac).

##### APC Setup

**Prerequisites:**

- At least one [connector](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709656492572#UUID-2aebdc84-c474-f68d-92e3-a50eb8966572) and a [project template](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709647439772#UUID-0d4861e8-5219-9b5f-3a49-4fe65f7bd211 "Project Templates (TMS)") in a profile.
- (Optional) An [email template](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709617392540#UUID-ab9ad063-eb5e-9a11-a4b4-78c673051419 "Email Templates and Submitter Portal Macros (TMS)") with either New Project via Automated Project Creation or Source update via Automated Project Creation selected as the type.
- If using [Job Sync](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709647502620#UUID-776d5a52-a0f8-d5c1-10b7-60bb343ef950) (Phrase Strings connector), multiple folders or files can be set for monitoring.

  For the Job Sync, the options to mark the job locale and the job as completed upon export can be enabled in the Phrase Strings connector settings. These settings mark an exported job locale, and eventually the whole job, as Completed in Strings once the corresponding TMS job is exported, so the APC stops monitoring that content. If these options are not enabled, the Strings job remains in progress, and a source update to that content can be detected by the APC and trigger a reimport.

##### Important

Monitoring more than 10,000 files per APC can cause file import errors and performance issues. If an error occurs in the UI, it is recommended to reduce the number of monitored files and manually trigger APC monitoring to retry the import.

A maximum of 10 monitored folders can be set per APC.

Follow these steps:

1. Create a new APC

   1. From the Settings ![Setup_gear.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682321905436) page, click Automated project creation.

      The Automated project creation page opens.
   2. Click New.

      The Creation page opens.
   3. Provide a name for the APC (top left).
   4. Select a [project template](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709647439772#UUID-0d4861e8-5219-9b5f-3a49-4fe65f7bd211 "Project Templates (TMS)") if required.
   5. Set active/inactive status (top left).

      The Save button is active once all mandatory fields are filled.
2. Set creation & export

   1. Choose how project is to be created.
   2. Select whether:

      - The APC is to be a continuous project.
      - Select from the dropdown list how a new project is created based on when and where changes are detected.
   3. Select a project template from the dropdown list.

      - Source language is defined in the project template and either all or a subset of target languages can be selected. Target languages selected for an APC apply to all files and folders that APC monitors. An APC cannot assign a different set of target languages to different files or subfolders within the same rule. To create jobs with different target language sets for different files or subfolders (for example, one file requiring only German and another requiring German, Spanish, and French), set up a separate APC for each file or folder, with each APC pointed at only the relevant files or folders and configured with only the target languages required for that content.
      - Select View project template details to preview the settings of the selected project template.
      - File selection in Monitoring (step 2) displays the entries in the default source locale (source locale as configured in the connector). If a project template is selected, the entries are displayed for that template’s source locale. Regardless of the settings and potential discrepancies between the project template and a connector’s source locales, the project template’s source locale is followed and jobs are created correctly.
   4. Select criteria for exporting translations.

      Export translations from is what [workflow](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709717879324#UUID-3d4fec12-4a9f-ace5-cd20-a1575786a6b7) state translations are in when they are to be exported. User can decide which content to export; examples being translations from the final workflow step or a step before that.

      Up to 5 exports per can be defined. Configure which content should be exported (from which workflow step) and when the export is triggered.

      When completing provides the event that triggers the export.

      - The translations will be exported when a selected workflow step is completed; when a specified workflow step is completed for one target language, this triggers the export for that language without waiting for the rest of the target languages to be completed
      - The translations will be exported when the whole project is completed - i.e. when all the jobs from all the workflow steps are complete.
3. Monitoring

   1. Click Monitor folder or file to choose a folder to monitor for new or updated content.

      The Connectors windows opens with a list of all connectors configured for the account.

      If the required connector is not listed, it can be added by clicking the plus button ![Plus_connector.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682254992796) at the top left of the window.
   2. Click a connector to open the folder list.
   3. Select specific folder or file to be monitored.

      Not all options are available on all [connectors](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709656492572#UUID-98e00ebc-37ac-490b-1577-e8f108fa5a9b)

      - If none are selected, the entire folder is monitored for a change or for new files.
      - Include subfolders to enable the monitoring of the selected folder and its subfolders.
      - Move processed files to specified folder can be used for file-based connectors to indicate which files were already used for translation.

      Filter by filename pattern (regex) lets customers define a [regular expression](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709636670364#UUID-fecec79b-8d0e-daaa-3327-8435094210ec) to filter out files to be monitored within the folder. This cannot be used to filter out folders.
   4. Click Confirm.

      The selected folder or file is listed with name and type of connector and path to the monitored entity. Click Browse to change the selection.

      For some connectors, more folders or files can be added to the list by clicking Monitor folder or file again. This is currently available for the following integrations: [Strings](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709647502620#UUID-776d5a52-a0f8-d5c1-10b7-60bb343ef950), [Contentful](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709656617628#UUID-c120e0c5-0b42-84ef-29e0-858e7a52a34e), [WordPress](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709657294620#UUID-63aa2730-0d12-1bbd-2955-224b36b30b81), [Kontent.ai](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709668269340#UUID-4f7ef7f1-571b-c2f0-440d-76760e2bfe40), [Git](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709654170780#UUID-54d80814-1f84-4dd2-39df-cb2370f55de8), [GitHub](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709656771356#UUID-59be0e6b-918d-2c99-67d5-9ead10cab859), [GitLab](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709668128796#UUID-9080c15e-f184-4520-1c33-257442b37bd2), and [Zendesk Guide](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709654717980#UUID-cac3e3c0-74a9-316f-6f14-5c19e4226aa1).

      - Multiple folders or files can only be monitored within one connector.
      - If changes are made to the monitored connector, previously saved settings are deleted.

      Click Save to confirm folder and file selection.
   5. Click Add monitor to select either a Schedule-based or Webhook-based trigger.

      Provide webhook or schedule (or both) in the monitoring window.

      Webhook-based monitoring:

      - The webhook token is generated automatically when selecting Webhook-based monitoring and clicking Add during APC setup.
      - Each APC receives its own unique token. The token is not shared and cannot be reused across other APCs.
      - Calling the webhook URL triggers change detection immediately on that specific APC. If an APC is already running a check when the webhook fires again, Phrase queues one additional run. Further calls while a run is already queued do not create additional runs; they confirm that the single pending run will proceed.

      ### Note

      This webhook is a separate mechanism from Phrase Strings' general-purpose [Webhooks](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5784125630620#UUID-27f6a836-3420-6087-e990-9ecbf6f85e68) feature, which sends outbound event notifications to a specified URL and neither supplies nor accepts the APC webhook token. Configure a webhook-triggered APC through the APC setup steps, not through a manually created Strings webhook.

      When using the [Job Sync](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709647502620#UUID-776d5a52-a0f8-d5c1-10b7-60bb343ef950) connector, configure a webhook-triggered APC through the APC setup steps, not through a manually created Strings webhook.
4. Set optional automations

   1. Select required automations.

      - Assign providers from template
      - Analyses and quotes options
      - [Due date schemes](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709647457308#UUID-0e2570ac-5170-51a4-945c-c5352ba81621 "Due Date Schemes (TMS)")
      - Notifications

        [Email templates](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709617392540#UUID-ab9ad063-eb5e-9a11-a4b4-78c673051419 "Email Templates and Submitter Portal Macros (TMS)") with the New Project via Automated Project Creation or Source update via Automated Project Creation will be available in this dropdown.
   2. Select source update options (only enabled for [continuous projects](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709703661468#UUID-2bd6e968-44df-ca0a-4eec-583c56016cba)).

      - If Create a new project everytime has been selected in the Creation & Export part of the APC setup, the APC monitors remote folders for source updates, but a detailed configuration is not necessary, because a new project is created every time a change is detected.
      - For a continuous project, specify which workflow steps require reopening when a source update is detected, if new analyses and quotes are to generated, and if project owners are to be notified about a source update.

        - If [Continuous analyses](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/17246425155996#UUID-85cececb-0f67-521a-ad84-53b8128d91a1 "Continuous Analysis (TMS)") is selected to generate new analyses with every source update, specify what to exclude from the [analysis](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709712007708#UUID-7ed2ed16-6064-f667-bb86-7d971d7004c9) (confirmed segments, locked segments, numbers) and how to group the word count (by provider, by language).

          ### Note

          Default settings of the continuous analyses are a combination of the default, mandatory settings of the Post-Editing Analysis and the Default Analysis.

          If required, enable the Macro-Assisted Analyses naming to enter a naming pattern for continuous analyses by using available [macros](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709720465948#UUID-28ae6783-5abf-f16a-f320-0a46b315dc23).
   3. Select target update options (only enabled for [Phrase Strings connector](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709647502620#UUID-776d5a52-a0f8-d5c1-10b7-60bb343ef950) if Create a new project everytime is selected).

      User can monitor the remote online repository for target updates. Any changes made to the target copy in the online repository will automatically update the translation memory.
   4. Click Save.

      The Import files from monitored folders opens.

      If Only new and updated files is selected, a dry run of the automation creates a baseline on the first iteration and imports only new/updated files after that baseline to reduce unnecessary usage. This option is only available on the first iteration.
   5. Click Confirm.

      The APC is added to the list on the Automated project creation page.

With the automation rules set, content can now be created in the designated folders. Based on frequency checks, Phrase looks into the specified folder and identifies new or updated content (based on file names, metadata, size, etc.).

##### Change Detection

APC uses two change detection strategies depending on the connector type and its configuration.

###### File History–Based Detection

This is used by most connectors. On each detection run, APC lists the files in the monitored folder and compares each file against a stored record from the previous run. The following fields are compared:

- Hash
- File size
- Last modified
- Due date

Which fields are actually available depends on what the connector provides as not all connectors expose all fields. All available (non-null) fields are compared.

A file is considered **changed** when any available field in the incoming file differs from the stored record. If the set of available fields changes between runs, for example, a hash becoming available where it was not before, the file is treated as metadata-modified and an import is triggered.

The stored record updates after each successful detection cycle.

###### Diff-Based Detection

Used when a **Git-based connector** has **subfolder monitoring enabled**. For Git connectors without subfolder monitoring, file history–based detection is used instead.

Instead of comparing file metadata, APC queries the connector for the list of files that changed since the last processed commit.

- On the first run, APC fetches all files in the folder and treats them all as changed.
- On subsequent runs, APC requests only files changed since the last known commit.

The last processed commit ID is stored and used as the starting point for the next detection run.

###### When an Import or Update Is Skipped

APC skips triggering an import or update under the following conditions:

- **No matching files found**

  If the monitored folder returns no files, or no files match the configured filename filter, the run is skipped with no action taken.
- **File was uploaded by this APC**

  If a file in the monitored folder was previously uploaded by the same APC instance (for example, a translated file written back to the source folder), it is excluded from change detection to prevent re-importing APC output.
- **No content change detected** (file history–based connectors)

  If all available fields for a file match the stored record, the file is treated as unchanged and skipped.
- **Selective import** (file not in the selected set)

  When a run is configured to import specific files only, files outside the selected set are excluded from the current run and evaluated in the next detection cycle.

###### When Multiple Folders Are Monitored

When an APC monitors multiple folders, each monitored folder runs its own independent detection. Results are collected and merged before triggering the downstream import.

A folder using a Git-based connector with subfolder monitoring enabled uses diff detection; all other folders use file history–based detection.

For Job Sync connectors monitoring Phrase Strings jobs, change detection checks every active job in the monitored folder on each run. A large number of active jobs in a watched folder can significantly increase the time an APC run takes to complete, even when only a few jobs need to be imported. To keep change detection fast, mark a job or job locale as Completed in Phrase Strings once it is finished, and keep the number of active jobs in a monitored folder low.

##### Set Target File Pathnames

Each target file is exported to a folder specified in [project settings](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709748435484#UUID-fd006a60-d1b0-dc4b-8681-00d5464cd76e).

##### Disable Automated Project Creation

There are three ways to disable APC:

- Manually disabled in settings.
- Automatically disables after 90 days of inactivity.
- Automatically after the organization profile has been deactivated (at the end of the subscription).

When a connector used as part of the Automated Project Creation rules detects three or more consecutive instances of a project not being created when it should be, notification is sent to affected users.

##### Zip File Support

- Multiple ZIP files can be imported to one project.
- Translated files are exported back to ZIP files.
- If one ZIP file is imported to multiple targets, the translated files will be exported to multiple ZIP files—one ZIP for each target language—using the target locale code in the ZIP name (for example *Pack18.en\_us.ZIP*).

#### APC Overview Page

The Automated project creation page provides an overview of currently available APCs.

APCs can be filtered by Type, Status, Last triggered, Next scheduled and APC version.

If a specific APC is selected:

- Edit

  Opens the selected APC for editing.
- Clone

  Makes a copy of the selected APC.
- Trigger monitor

  Manually checks source files for updates and updates the Last triggered date and time.
- Force import

  Imports all the files from the remote folder monitored by the selected APC, bypassing change detection.

  When force import is enabled, all files matching the folder filter are treated as changed regardless of their stored history. This is useful for reprocessing files after configuration changes or when a re-import is needed.

  - Selective Force Import

    Select which files from the monitored folder(s) to import. Only the selected files bypass change detection. The remaining files in the folder are not affected and are evaluated normally on the next scheduled detection run.
- Delete

  APCs associated with active projects cannot be deleted.

  Deleting APC is permanent. A deleted APC cannot be restored from the recycle bin or recreated automatically; it must be set up again from scratch if needed. This is distinct from manually disabling an APC (toggling it inactive), which can be re-enabled at any time.

##### APC Settings

Clicking on a specific APC opens the settings page for that APC. From the settings page, it is possible to:

- From the Configuration tab, review and update the APC settings.
- From the History log tab, track operations executed by the APC and their status.
- From the Financials tab, view and download existing [continuous analyses](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/17246425155996#UUID-85cececb-0f67-521a-ad84-53b8128d91a1 "Continuous Analysis (TMS)") generated for the APC.

###### History Log

APC history log details all the operations performed by an APC. It enables localization managers to view all APC events, search and filter them, and troubleshoot problems with a specific APC.

##### Note

The search bar only works for enquiries in English. All data is stored in English so that the logs are useful for Phrase’s engineers and technical support / customer success teams.

The log tracks these events:

- Project

  - Create
  - Status change
- Job

  - Import
  - Export
  - Source update
  - Target update
  - Status change
- Monitoring

  - Folder monitoring
- APC

  - Create
  - Deactivate

The log does not track:

- Manual operations (manual file imports)
- Operations that do not have impact on APC functioning (e.g. updates of project template settings that do not affect the APC)
- Non-APC-related operations
- Quote and analysis creation
- TM updates
- Sent notifications
- APC configuration changes

##### APC Status

The status of an APC is presented on the APC Overview page.

- Active

  APC is running without any issues
- Inactive

  APC has been made intentionally inactive
- Running

  APC is processing content from the monitored repository. Processing time depends on the size of the monitored content.

  To keep APC processing times short:

  - Trigger imports more frequently, in smaller batches, rather than allowing large batches of files to accumulate.
  - Split monitoring of large folders or paths across multiple APCs (for example, by folder or product area) so each APC processes fewer files.
  - Create a new APC instead of reactivating one that has been inactive for a long time to avoid importing a large backlog of eligible jobs at once.
- Needs attention

  APC is running but requires user’s attention due to possible changes or minor errors which might affect the APC.

  Error and warning statuses on an APC reflect the outcome of the most recent run only. These statuses are not updated in real time. A Needs attention or error state will remain visible until the APC runs again successfully. If an underlying issue has been resolved, trigger the APC manually to clear the outdated status.

  | Reason | Details |
  | --- | --- |
  | APC check was successful but the file import failed. | File import from connector failed. Check the monitored file configuration on the APC edit page.  Once file monitoring is fixed, trigger Force Import (or Selective Force Import) to re-import the previously failed files. |
  | Multiple folders monitored in one APC: some of the monitored folders failed. | APC is only monitoring changes for successfully monitored folders. Check if all monitored folders still exist.  Once monitored folders are fixed, trigger monitoring to process new/missed changes. |
  | One folder monitored in an APC: monitored folder failed. | Check if the monitored folder still exists.  Once the monitored folders are fixed, trigger monitoring to process new/missed changes. |
  | Multiple folders monitored in one APC: all folders have some issues, but in the APC check failed only once or twice, | Validate the folder monitoring settings on the APC edit page. Once the monitored folders are fixed, trigger monitoring to process new/missed changes. |
  | Connector failure | Check the connector configuration. |
  | Workflow step configured for export no longer exists. | APC is still running but won’t execute any exports. Ensure the project template is correct and APC export settings are correct. |
  | Workflow step configured for export has been modified. | APC is still running and will be executing exports from the workflow step which has a number corresponding with the workflow step number configured for the APC. Ensure the project template is correct and APC export settings are correct. |
  | Some target languages got removed from the project template. | APC won’t use removed languages in newly created projects. |
  | File export from APC failed. | Export the files manually. |
- Stopped

  APC has been deactivated by the system due to breaking errors/failures.

  | Reason | Details |
  | --- | --- |
  | All source and/or target languages were removed from the project template. | No source and/or target languages. Add at least one source and at least one target language in the project template, then set the APC status to Active. Once the APC is re-activated, newly created projects will use the updated source/target locales. |
  | APC check failed three times for all monitored folders. | Validate the monitoring configuration and connector settings, then re-activate the APC and trigger monitoring. |

#### Translation with Pivot Languages through APC

In multilingual localization, a [pivot language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pivot_language) can be used as a bridge language to enable translation from the source language to any required number of target languages. The pivot language approach is especially valid when there are limited translation resources available in the source language.

Translation with pivot languages is a APC use case to automate the translation process. The example below summarizes required steps to follow:

1. Create a folder in the desired online repository to store the source language content.

   In this example, source files in French language are added to a Google Drive folder.
2. [Set up APC](https://support.phrase.com#UUID-2558de58-eb7e-d298-f22a-d41dd17b1de6 "Automated Project Creation - APC (TMS)") monitoring options to monitor content updates in the desired online repository.
3. Set up APC to create a project with the required source language and the chosen pivot language to use as target language.

   In this example, the APC is set up to create a project with French as source language and English as pivot target language.
4. Configure the APC export settings to export translated content into the corresponding target language folder on the same online repository.

   In this example, the APC is set up to export the English translations into a target folder on the same Google Drive.
5. Once the project is completed, the export triggers APC to create another project for translating content from the pivot language into the desired target language.

   In this example, the export triggers APC to create another project for translating content from English into German.

##### Note

Required [connectors](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709656492572#UUID-98e00ebc-37ac-490b-1577-e8f108fa5a9b)and [project templates](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709647439772#UUID-0d4861e8-5219-9b5f-3a49-4fe65f7bd211 "Project Templates (TMS)") must be set up to apply the use case.

For large scale projects, translation with pivot languages can also be achieved by custom scripting via [APIs](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709706916124#UUID-e66c3c22-e3d3-ade2-9f14-e1800c773c58).
