### Quality Assurance Pane - QA (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709694857372-Quality-Assurance-Pane-QA-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-08-04T06:05:17Z  
> Labels: Linguist, Quality Assurance, 2BTr

[Quality assurance](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709703799324#UUID-83632035-0d65-f957-b0dd-ad00704f8d25) (QA) is a feature built into the editor. It detects translation issues by comparing source and target segments, checking the term base, spelling, content of the tags, and other configured checks. It helps translators detect formal errors and improve overall translation quality and consistency.

If set by a project manager, QA checks may be mandatory for projects. If mandatory, QA warnings must be mitigated before the jobs can be set to *Completed*. QA checks are also run on locked segments unless excluded by the project manager. The project's QA settings apply to all jobs it contains.

[QA warnings](https://support.phrase.com#UUID-1865a53c-d82a-4b2e-6209-aa12c86b50d3_UUID-d9cc738f-e997-be83-27b5-ca536b7b75b3 "Mitigating QA Warnings") for segments with potential problems are displayed in the quality assurance pane (QA) ![QA_pane.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682184005916) in the editor. If [Quality profiles](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/25865045974300#UUID-7b57e446-f5e2-e696-aaf1-8713b94eab34) are enabled for the project, AI check issues are also displayed in the QA pane under the [AI checks](https://support.phrase.com#UUID-1865a53c-d82a-4b2e-6209-aa12c86b50d3_UUID-7cd37781-f22f-39d4-f160-11d5af14010b "AI Checks") tab.

QA can be performed instantly upon segment confirmation, or manually.

To sort the QA warning list, click on the column headings.

#### Instant QA

When attempting to confirm a segment, Instant QA check is run on that segment. In the case of an issue, a yellow warning triangle ![yellow_warning.jpg](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682184032284) is displayed instead of a green check ![QA Confirmed Segment](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682197685148), and the QA pane with the warnings is opened. The Linguist must mitigate all issues or set false positive warnings to ignored in order to confirm the segment.

Instant QA can be disabled if the linguist is [given permission](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709585565980#UUID-424b8fbe-2d60-48eb-891a-a4f1c5004c82) by the Project manager. If permission is not given, the option to disable will not be available.

To enable/disable Instant QA, follow these steps:

1. In the editor, go to the menu ![Open Menu](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682151975324) and select Preferences.

   The Preferences window open.
2. Click the Misc tab.

   Translation table options are presented.
3. Select/Deselect Instant QA.
4. Click Save.

   Preferences are applied and the window closes.

#### Manual QA

Manual QA does not affect ability to confirm segments, but if issues are identified and cannot be ignored due to project settings, the job can not be set to *Complete*.

To run a manual QA, follow these steps:

1. Open the QA pane.
2. Select QA issues to be scanned for from the dropdown menu.
3. Click Run job QA.

   The QA is run and results presented in the QA pane.

#### Mitigating QA Warnings

Click a QA warning to highlight the segment where the problem has been detected.

Quality assurance warnings are resolved in one of two ways:

- Correcting the translation and confirming it.
- Clicking in the far right Ignore column, the inline or the context menu to mark the QA warning as ignored if it is a false alarm.

  Multiple warnings can be grouped for ignoring by holding down **Shift** while selecting as a group or **CTRL** for individual lines. Clicking the top of the column can also be used to sort the warnings.

After mitigation, warnings are displayed in gray.

To remove ignored warning from the list:

- In the web editor, deselect Show ignored issues from the filter menu ![Menu_Triangle.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682184132380).
- In the desktop editor, select Hide ignored.

Warning types may be set to *Unignorable* by Project Managers. These warnings *must* be corrected in the target segments before proceeding to confirmation.

##### Note

Words identified as misspelled during QA may be set to Ignore in the QA pane but will still be marked as spelling errors in the target segment.

#### AI Checks

If a Quality profile is applied during [pre-translation](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709717749788#UUID-a982e5f9-9aa2-434f-116c-17b822d35343), an additional AI checks tab appears in the QA pane.

The AI checks tab displays issues detected based on the AI checks defined in the applied Quality profile and the corresponding segments. Selecting an issue highlights the affected text in the translation table.

At the top of the tab, select Show AI checks to display the AI checks used for the job and a preview of their criteria. Clicking any check name in the Issue table opens the AI checks window with the full criteria. For joined jobs, AI checks from all included job parts are combined into one list. Users with access to the job part can view the available AI check details.

If a segment is [split or joined](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709678012828#UUID-0d65fa6f-a518-11dc-7467-b46c79496b52 "Segments (TMS)") in the editor, the associated AI check issues are removed. This action is not reversible. Even if the split or join is undone, the AI check issue is not restored.

### In-Context Preview (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709664002076-In-Context-Preview-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-09-24T06:07:05Z  
> Labels: 2BTr

The In-context preview feature offers a real-time preview of original or translated text directly in the [editors](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709683847964#UUID-1da30c04-11f8-6314-17a0-f4948f4cfed6 "CAT Editor (TMS)") and can be switched between source and target views.

The preview can be switched on and off from the Tools menu in both the web and desktop editors.

Click ![seperate_window.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682200241948) to open the in-context preview in a separate window. Closing the separate window restores the preview to the bottom panel.

Clicking on a [segment](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709678012828#UUID-0d65fa6f-a518-11dc-7467-b46c79496b52 "Segments (TMS)") to be translated highlights the respective text in the preview window and displays the position of the translated segment within the document.

Clicking on text within the preview causes the translation grid to indicate the corresponding segment for editing.

During [QA](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709703799324#UUID-83632035-0d65-f957-b0dd-ad00704f8d25), clicking on a warning navigates the linguist to the position of the warning within the document.

Tables, columns, various graphics, formatting, and fonts (if installed by users) are supported. The feature is meant to provide context when translating and is not a perfect representation of the original or completed document; some visual differences are expected. It can also be influenced by enabling/disabling *Allow loading of external content in editors* option in Access and Security settings.

The preview also has zoom functionality as well as a right-click context menu.

##### Note

The in-context preview in the web browser may be affected by the editor having only a portion of segments loaded at a given time; skipping over large groups of segments can lead to an incomplete preview.

Scrolling through the translation table and loading segments from the beginning of a major section (e.g. a chapter) or from the beginning of a job improves the preview.

#### Supported CMS

- AEM
- Contentful
- Drupal
- Marketo
- Sitecore
- WordPress

For certain file types (e.g. .HTML files), the preview is generated directly.

In all other cases, Phrase downloads the .HTML from the third-party system and saves it as a preview template. When importing and processing the content for translation in the CAT editors, the .HTML preview template is matched with information from the .MXLIFF file to generate the In-context preview of the segments.

In-context preview for CSM content can be generated without building a custom CSM connector by using the preview package, which supports rich .HTML and .SVG preview formats. The preview is generated during [job creation](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/10825587738268#UUID-f34b2b7c-0b92-e115-cfee-f436ba5e5445) by importing an .HTML (optionally with contextual assets) or .SVG preview template.

#### Supported file types

- AsciiDoc
- .DITA
- Google Docs, Sheets and Slides
- .HTML
- .IDML
- Markdown
- Microsoft Excel (including multilingual files)
- Microsoft PowerPoint
- Microsoft Word
- .RTF
- .SVG
- .XML with style sheets (including multilingual files)

Previews are not generated for unsupported file types.

If a preview can not be generated due to unsupported file type or preview [limits](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5784117234972#UUID-c318163f-0b7f-cb70-4773-980cb156bf43) are exceeded, a preview can be downloaded from the Document menu but will not be in the original file type.

##### Tip

Microsoft Excel file previews are downloaded in [SpreadsheetML (.XML)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpreadsheetML) format, which can be opened in any compatible spreadsheet editor. If MSOffice is installed, they typically open in Excel automatically; if not, use the Open with action from the file [context menu](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/file-explorer-in-windows-ef370130-1cca-9dc5-e0df-2f7416fe1cb1#windowsversion=windows_11) to select an application.

#### Preview for InDesign Files

The in-context preview for .IDML files supports all in-context preview functions: source and target preview, real-time changes, navigation between the translation table and the preview window, and zoom. The preview displays a wide range of InDesign components.

To make the preview more accurate, upload a PDF that matches the .IDML file when creating the job. Uploading a PDF adds page background images and renders text and formatting more reliably in large documents.

The preview provides context for translation and is not a pixel-perfect representation of the InDesign document.

**Limitations**

- Images are displayed for imported .IDML files with embedded images.

#### Preview for Figma Files

A live in-context preview is available for [jobs synced](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709647502620#UUID-776d5a52-a0f8-d5c1-10b7-60bb343ef950) from Phrase Strings that were created with the [Strings Figma plugin](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5819515701916#UUID-c9c6bc21-3921-38e5-4339-93578f6782d7).

The preview supports all TMS in-context preview functions (source and target preview, real-time changes, navigating from the translation table to the preview window and the other way round, and zoom) and the following Figma elements:

- Text
- Frames
- Groups
- Components
- Shapes and images

**End-to-end workflow overview**

1. Push from Figma to Strings

   Use the [Figma plugin](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5819515701916#UUID-c9c6bc21-3921-38e5-4339-93578f6782d7) to select design content and send it to a [Strings project](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5784094677404#UUID-67ae68da-d206-0281-f708-35cfdfb52252).

   A preview (up to 50 MB) is attached automatically. If a preview exceeds the 50 MB limit, a notification appears and the keys will still be pushed to Strings but a job with keys for [JobSync](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709647502620#UUID-776d5a52-a0f8-d5c1-10b7-60bb343ef950) will be not be created.

   When uploading multiple frames in bulk, frames with previews larger than 50 MB are excluded from upload with an error message displaying the frame name and node ID.

   Required plugin settings:

   - Enable the Upload Figma preview option.
   - Enable smart key naming and use the following macro to ensure that segments are sent to TMS in the same order as they appear in the plugin:

     `{ulid}`

     This setting is remembered per Figma file only, not on new files.
   - Regenerate keys before each push to ensure updated naming.
   - If rich formatting is required in the TMS in-context preview, enable the Preserve content formatting & styling option. This allows bold, italics, lists, and links to be displayed correctly in the preview using HTML formatting tags.
2. Jobs are created in the Strings project

   [Jobs](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5784100517788#UUID-92182692-6284-4968-7e2d-56d1a1dee812) are created automatically from pushed content and include all defined target languages.
3. Translate in TMS CAT editor

   Sync the job(s) via the [Phrase Strings connector](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709647502620#UUID-776d5a52-a0f8-d5c1-10b7-60bb343ef950) and open them in the CAT editor to translate content with the Figma in-context preview.
4. Pull back to Figma

   Completed translations are synced back to Strings and can be pulled into Figma via the Strings plugin.

### Resources Pane (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/28913499477532-Resources-Pane-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-08-25T06:06:10Z

The resources pane is accessible through the right sidebar and displays resources attached to the project.

The following resources are displayed:

- References
- Style guides
- Term bases
- Translation memories

Only term bases and translation memories belonging to the current user’s organization can be accessed.

##### Downloading and Viewing References

Project reference files can be downloaded directly from the editor and some reference files can be viewed in a new browser tab:

1. Clicking the filename downloads the file.
2. Clicking the ![seperate_window.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682200336284) icon opens the file in a new browser tab.

   This option is available for file types such as .PDF, image, .TXT, audio, video, and .HTML files. The icon does not appear if the browser cannot render the file type, for example .DOCX files. For files capable of running scripts, for example .SVG or .HTML files, a trust warning appears, prompting confirmation before the file opens.

### Context Information (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709700187292-Context-Information-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-09-07T06:06:44Z  
> Labels: 2BTr

Some file formats contain contextual information that aids in the understanding and translation of those files. Phrase cannot separate contextual information from the original file.

The editor displays this information in the Context note pane. If the file format is not fully supported, such as PDF, the pane may not be visible.

Context note display can be turned on or off from the Tools menu with the Show context note option or the keyboard shortcut (**Ctrl-N** for desktop editor, **Alt-N** for the web editor).

Contextual information can be presented in plain text or rich text formats. Autoselect allows the editor to heuristically select the format.

There are three types of context information:

sidebar. Context key

- Automatically retrieved from the source file on import or defined manually for supported file types.
- Supported in:

  - Chrome
  - .CSV
  - Desktop Entry
  - .DTD
  - .INI
  - Joomla
  - .JSON ([limits](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5784117234972#UUID-c318163f-0b7f-cb70-4773-980cb156bf43))
  - Mac strings
  - .MIF
  - Mozilla properties
  - Multilingual MS Excel
  - .PO
  - .properties
  - .RESJSON
  - .SRT
  - .TS
  - Windows RC
  - .XLIFF
  - .XML ([limits](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5784117234972#UUID-c318163f-0b7f-cb70-4773-980cb156bf43))
  - .YAML ([limits](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5784117234972#UUID-c318163f-0b7f-cb70-4773-980cb156bf43))

sidebar. Context note

- The context note allows users to specify sections of source documents where additional information relevant for translation is stored.
- Set by the user in by clicking the File Import Settings in the Project Settings section.
- Supported in:

  - Chrome
  - .CSV
  - .JSON ([limits](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5784117234972#UUID-c318163f-0b7f-cb70-4773-980cb156bf43))
  - Mac Strings
  - .PO
  - .RESJSON
  - .RESX
  - .SBV
  - .SRT
  - .TS
  - Windows RC
  - .XLIFF
  - .XML ([limits](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5784117234972#UUID-c318163f-0b7f-cb70-4773-980cb156bf43))
  - .YAML ([limits](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5784117234972#UUID-c318163f-0b7f-cb70-4773-980cb156bf43))

Segments can be [filtered](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709720416796#UUID-11936659-047d-2507-3e91-ab2208f2ef73) by Context key and Context note.

sidebar. Context origin

- Retrieved from the original file on import. It includes information on the origin of the current segment.

  **Example:**

  *footer* will appear for a segment originating from the footer of a .DOCX file.
- Supported in:

  - Desktop Entry
  - .MIF
  - .TS
  - MS Office

[**Plural forms**](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709718013980#UUID-a45be532-450a-fdf8-bc5f-52a000050e3c)

In file formats supporting the plural form, some segments can be designated as plural variants.

When detected, the Context pane automatically opens and information about the plural segment is displayed:

- Additional text if present in the original file

  **Example**:

  *msgctxt* in a PO Gettext file may be added to the Note field.
- Plural category (depending on the target language)
- Plural examples

### Segments (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709678012828-Segments-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-09-07T06:06:45Z  
> Labels: 2BTr

#### Segmentation

Segmentation is the splitting of source texts into smaller parts. This improves the retrieval of previously translated text from a [translation memory](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709688865692#UUID-c58dd835-39ea-1a94-02d1-9f2517fd6d75). Segments are presented in the [editor](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709683847964#UUID-1da30c04-11f8-6314-17a0-f4948f4cfed6 "CAT Editor (TMS)") and can be [filtered](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709720416796#UUID-11936659-047d-2507-3e91-ab2208f2ef73). If a project has workflow steps, changes in segments are presented in the [translation changes pane](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709700120476#UUID-5bf661bf-3e7f-4a72-4ff6-350a4aa4eb1a "Translation Changes Pane (TMS)").

Default segmentation rules correspond with specifics of each supported language and can be customized.

[Jobs](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709686763420#UUID-33f88350-daa8-2ab2-e7ce-e35300ec60f8) imported with bad segmentation such as poorly formatted document files or the application of inappropriate segmentation customization can affect TM match values. It is recommended that some time is spent reviewing and preparing the source file before importation; a common problem is the incorrect use of line breaks versus paragraph breaks.

**Example**:

Good segmentation:

- *Translation memories with multilingual target languages are supported and can be used bidirectionally.*

  Match value of 100%.

Poor segmentation

- *Translation memories with multilingual target languages are supported.*

  Match value of 100%.
- *and can be used bidirectionally.*

  Match value of 63%.

#### Joining and Splitting Segments

Segments can not be joined or split if a Linguist does not have editing rights on the source text or the segment is part of the [plural form](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709718013980#UUID-a45be532-450a-fdf8-bc5f-52a000050e3c).

Segment splitting and joining is done only virtually, and therefore is not taken into account when splitting jobs. When splitting a job after a segment that had been split in the Editor, the whole original segment is considered, not its parts.

To join segments, follow these steps:

1. Select a segment.
2. Click join segments ![Join Segment](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682184477980) or **Ctrl/Cmd+J**.

   The selected segment and that below are joined. The joining point is indicated with the {j} tag. The {j} tag is a visual representation of the whitespace mark which exists and is applied between the two joined segments. Do not remove this tag even if previously joined segments are split again as it will corrupt the formatting.

To split segments, follow these steps:

1. Place the cursor at a point in the source segment that requires splitting.
2. Click split segments ![split_segment.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682217208988) or **Ctrl/Cmd+E**.

   The segment is separated at the specified point.

   Split segments cannot be searched or filtered for after the fact. Splitting a segment creates no status, tag, or metadata to identify it later.

##### Caution

Ensure leading and trailing spaces are added to the target side based on the source text.

When splitting segments in a job where the source is a space-less CJK language and the target is a language that uses spaces as a word delimiter, ensure leading or trailing spaces are added to the target to delimit words in the translation. This is normally automatically applied to segments formed by the default segmentation rules as no spaces are added in manually split segments or those formed by additional custom [segmentation rules](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709712126876#UUID-24c008d6-ce1d-0432-6b76-384de441b063).

#### Confirming Segments

All segments (unless locked by a Project manager) in a job must be confirmed before a job can be set as Complete. Confirmation can be performed via [keyboard shortcuts](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709700557468#UUID-303b0e1c-0be1-e356-2455-42c1518ab1e8 "Editor Keyboard Shortcuts (TMS)"), menu or clicking on ![Red_X.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682184549788) in the table.

To confirm a segment, follow these steps:

1. Open a job in an editor.

   Segments are presented as unconfirmed ![Red_X.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682184549788).

   If confirmed in a previous workflow step, segments are presented with a gray checkmark ![Confirmed Segment](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682184590748).
2. Click on a segment to review.

   Matches are presented in the CAT pane.
3. Review matches for accuracy and either accept or change.
4. Confirm the segment by clicking the ![Red_X.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682184549788).

   Segment is presented as confirmed ![QA Confirmed Segment](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682184626332).

   Editing a segment removes confirmation status from that segment.
5. If required, run a [QA check](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709694857372#UUID-1865a53c-d82a-4b2e-6209-aa12c86b50d3 "Quality Assurance Pane - QA (TMS)").

Select segment numbers to highlight multiple segments:

- Hold down **Shift** while selecting multiple segments as a group.
- Hold down **CTRL** (Windows) or **Cmd** (macOS) while selecting multiple individual segments.

To confirm all segments at once, select the menu options Edit/Select all and Edit/Confirm segment, or use the relevant keyboard shortcuts.

Confirmation behavior can be modified in [CAT preferences](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709683926812#UUID-4c833ac1-32c2-c1cb-2d80-b6411f03a8be_UUID-7a7fb24c-ee23-057b-8444-adb74d532665 "CAT Pane Preferences").

##### Locked segments

Only Project managers and Administrators can lock and unlock segments (Ctrl+L or from the Edit menu) and may [restrict](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709585565980#UUID-424b8fbe-2d60-48eb-891a-a4f1c5004c82) Linguists and Vendors from being able to edit them. Locked segments don't require confirmation before a linguist sets the job to *Completed*. Locked segments can be excluded from the QA.

If a segment is locked and available for editing, click F2 to access the content.

#### Saving Segments to a Translation Memory

Saving segments to a [translation memory](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709688865692#UUID-9e5b1c50-0408-738b-59b5-baa05a312eea) ensures that translation work performed can be reused in future translation projects.

Segments *can not* be saved to a translation memory if:

- Working offline in the CAT desktop editor.
- When a job is pre-translated with the Set segment status to confirmed for... option selected.

  If confirmed segments are locked during pre-translation and then unlocked in the editor, unlocked segments will be saved into the TM.
- When importing an .XLIFF file as a new job with the Set segment status to confirmed for... option selected.

Linguists and Vendors can save segments to translation memories in projects set as writable by a Project Manager.

Segments are saved in two ways:

- Automatically saved to the TM when confirmed during the translation process.
- Upload of translated bilingual file via the desktop editor or the tools menu in the linguist portal.

Project managers can save segments to translation memories in three ways:

- Upload via the tools menu on the Job page.
- Import a standard [.XLIFF](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709613119516#UUID-e95395fa-bc12-6247-0a1a-9b79950fc242) file as a new job with the Save confirmed segments to TM on import option selected in file import settings.
- Directly [import a bilingual .MXLIFF](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709739829532#UUID-1d5509ec-f537-4aff-cede-ce93f80b713c) file into the TM.

### Repetitions (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709708706460-Repetitions-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-06-23T12:55:26Z  
> Labels: 2BTr

Segments repeated within a job are labeled as repetitions. The first instance of a repetition is identified with a heavy arrow ![Repetition_heavy.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682231902748)and subsequent repetitions with a lighter arrow ![Repetition_light.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682231931932).

Segments are considered repetitions if:

- *Segment 1* and *Segment 2* contain identical texts.

If Ignore tag metadata is unselected in file import settings:

1. *Segment 1* and *Segment 2* contain identical texts with tags of the same type at the same places with the same tag metadata regardless of tag ids.
2. *Segment 1* and *Segment 2* contain identical texts with at most one formatting tag (may consisted of multiple formats) or a paired number tag surrounding it regardless of the surrounding tag; they may differ in that tag. Note that no other formatting or tags may be present within the text.

Segments with [plural form](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709718013980#UUID-a45be532-450a-fdf8-bc5f-52a000050e3c) are not considered repetitions.

If the *Set segment status to 'confirmed' for* the Repetitions option is [enabled](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/10825091328028#UUID-1b4ea28a-d66f-0cf7-6a75-f04f8dc61a3e) in [CAT editor](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709683847964#UUID-1da30c04-11f8-6314-17a0-f4948f4cfed6 "CAT Editor (TMS)") settings, the translation of a repeated segment is automatically propagated to all subsequent repetitions. When a linguist confirms a segment that is repeated later in the document, all repetitions of that segment are confirmed.

Repetition propagation is a CAT editor behavior and is separate from pre-translation. Pre-translation applies translation memory, non-translatables, and machine translation matches in batch before a job is opened in the editor. Repetition propagation runs later, inside the editor, as the linguist works.

#### Repetition exception

Clicking on the repetition icon crosses out the arrow ![Repetition](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682167946524) to indicate an exception from the repetition. This allows the instance to have a different translation. If auto-propagation of repetitions is disabled, the first repetition exception is identified with greyed out ![disabled_rep_new.jpeg](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682152636188) arrows.

##### LQA assessment of repetitions

When flagging an [LQA issue](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/27529737766044#UUID-9bfa4b5c-9bdc-ae9a-51e8-32126336ba05 "LQA Assessments (TMS)") in a repetition, there must be a decision on how other instances of the repetition will be flagged. Select an option from the dropdown menu.

#### Disabling auto-propagation of repetitions

To disable/enable the auto-propagation of repetitions, follow these steps:

1. From the Settings ![Setup_gear.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682152663068) page, scroll down to the Project settings section and click on CAT editor.

   The CAT editor page opens.

   Or

   From the Edit Project page, open the CAT editor menu.
2. Select Auto-propagate repetitions.
3. Click Save.

   Settings are saved and repetitions are identified in the editors with greyed out ![Disabled Repetition](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682232037020) and ![Disabled Repetition](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682200954012) arrows.

Unless the option is disabled by a project manager in [Access and Security](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709585565980#UUID-424b8fbe-2d60-48eb-891a-a4f1c5004c82) settings, Linguists can disable/enable the auto-propagation of repetitions in the [CAT pane preferences](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709683926812#UUID-4c833ac1-32c2-c1cb-2d80-b6411f03a8be_UUID-7a7fb24c-ee23-057b-8444-adb74d532665 "CAT Pane Preferences").

#### Repetition Use Case

##### Prevent linguists from editing already confirmed repetitions

After the first repetition is confirmed, segments with subsequent repetitions are auto-propagated and locked so as to be uneditable by Linguists.

To set up this use case, follow these steps:

1. From the Settings ![Setup_gear.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682152663068) page, scroll down to the Project settings section and select CAT editor.

   The CAT editor page opens.
2. Under Repetitions, select Auto-propagate repetitions, Auto-propagate to locked repetitions and Lock subsequent repetitions.
3. Click Save.

When Allow linguists to edit locked segments is enabled in [Access and Security](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709585565980-Access-and-Security-TMS) settings, Linguists can edit a locked segment by pressing F2 in the CAT editor. To prevent Linguists from editing locked segments, keep this option disabled.

### Regex in Web Editor (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/20889691339164-Regex-in-Web-Editor-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-04-18T13:33:15Z  
> Labels: 2BTr

Regex support in the web editor is limited by the implementation of the [Lucene Regex](https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/query-languages/query-dsl/regexp-syntax) engine.

To use regex, enabled Match using regex in filter settings. A green checkmark in the filter input field indicates the successful validation of a valid regex.

Queries are by default case insensitive. Enable Match case in filter settings to make them case sensitive.

Match words (ensuring matching only complete words and not substrings within longer words) is not available.

The query `^abc$` will work as expected, i.e. matching the whole segment, while abc will match substring *abc* in any text.

#### Limitations

The correct replacement of partially formatted queries is not supported, e.g. searching for `"Jméno: $1, Příjmení: $2."` in text "{b>First name<}: Bob, {biu>Last name<biu}: Dylan." will be replaced as “{>Jméno: Bob, Příjmení: Dylan<b}”

#### Unsupported patterns

- Word boundary anchor `\b` used to match exact words (works in the desktop editor).
- `\\[1-9]` - Backreferences (\1, \2, etc.), e.g. `(\w+)\s+\1` to match duplicated words like “hello hello”
- `\(\?=|\(\?!|\(\?&lt;=|\(\?&lt;!` - Lookahead and lookbehind, e.g. `cat(?=\.jpg)` to match “cat” only in “cat.jpg”
- `\(\?:` - Non-capturing groups, e.g. (`?:Mr|Mrs|Ms)\. \w+,` but capturing groups `(Mr|Mrs|Ms)\. \w+` are supported and match names like “Mrs. Smith”, “Mr. Brown”
- `\(\?#` - Inline comments, e.g. `\d{4}-(?# year)\d{2}-(?# month)\d{2}(?# day)` to match  “2025-06-25”
- `\(\?P<[^>]+>` - Named capture groups, e.g. (`?P<amount>\d+)\s?(?P<currency>USD|EUR)` to match “150 USD” and “99 EUR”

#### Usage

##### Basic Pattern Matching

Dot (.) as a placeholder for any single character

- `c.at`: Matches: “chat”, “coat”. Does NOT match: “cat”, “cheat”
- `wa.ter`: Matches: “waiter”, “waster”. Does NOT match: “water”
- `s.ip`: Matches: “skip”, “ship”, “slip”. Does NOT match: “sip”, “strip”

##### Quantifiers

`?` - Zero or one occurrence

- `colou?r`: Matches: “color”, “colour”
- `g?rain`: Matches: “grain”, “rain”
- `books?`: Matches: “book”, “books”

`.*` - Any number of characters (including none)

- `h.*y`: Matches: “happy”, “history”, “honey”
- `sa.*d`: Matches: “sad”, “sand”, “satisfied”
- `m.*ing`: Matches: “morning”, “meeting”, “marketing”

`.+` - At least one character must appear

- `pa.+er`: Matches: “paper”, “painter”
- `a.+ed`" Matches: “asked”, “accepted”, “allowed”

`*` - Zero or more occurrences

- `go*al`: Matches: “goal”, “goooooooal”

`+` - One or more occurrences

- `no+`: Matches: “no”, “noooooo”
- `$1+`: Matches: “$1”, “$11”, “$111”

It is recommended to use as specific a pattern as possible as open patterns may cause performance issues in the editor.

##### Important

The editor has a built-in limit on how complex a regex pattern can be. Patterns that are too broad or heavily use wildcards may fail as invalid regex. To avoid this:

- Keep patterns short and specific. `error-[0-9]{3}` is fine; `.*a.*b.*c.*d.*` is not.
- Minimize wildcards. Each `.+` or `.*` multiplies the internal complexity. Prefer character classes like `[A-Z]+` over `.*` where possible.
- Avoid long alternations with repetition. A pattern like `(word1|word2|...|word20){2,}` can exceed the limit quickly. This is amplified when the alternatives include multiple words or punctuation, which adds to the regex complexity.
- Anchor one side when possible. `^prefix.*` is far cheaper than `.*middle.*`.

If the pattern is rejected, try making it more targeted: start with a longer fixed prefix and narrow down from there. Consider reducing the number of alternatives or handling them in separate patterns instead of combining everything into one complex regex.

**Example:**

Filtering for email addresses:

- This pattern will match spaces and all surrounding words with potentially too many results: `.*@.*`
- To limit the results to all email addresses: `[\w.+\-]+@[\w.+\-]+`
- To limit the results to .com emails only:  `[\w.+\-]+@[\w.+\-]\.com`
- To limit the results to those having a digit in the email addresses: `[\w.+\-]*\d+[\w.+\-]*@[\w.\-]+`

##### Alternations (OR operator)

- `cat|dog`: Matches: “cat” and “dog”
- `red|blue|green`: Matches: “red”, “blue”, “green”

##### Character Classes and Ranges

- `[A-Z]+`: Matches one or more uppercase letters in a row (a sequence).
- `[A-Z]{2,}`: Matches any series of uppercase letters (useful for e.g. matching acronyms or strings written in uppercase letters)
- `[0-9]{4}`: Matches four-digit numbers, e.g. "1999", "2003", "1876" (also found within a longer-than-four digit string; to limit the results, the Match words option planned for future should be used)
- `[A-Za-z0-9]+`: Matches any alphanumeric string (hello! → hello would match, but ! is not part of [A-Za-z0-9]; 100% → only 100 would match)
- `([A-Za-z]+\d+|\d+[A-Za-z]+)`: Matches strictly a combination of digits and letters, e.g. “user123”, “Admin99”, “Win11”, “5g”, “1080p”
- `[0-9]{2,4}-[A-Z]{2,3}`: Matches license plates, e.g. “12-XY”, “9999-ABC”

##### Escaping Reserved Characters . ? \* { } [ ] ( ) " \

- `\+[0-9]{1,2}`: Matches “+40”, “+1”
- `\{version: [0-9]+\}`: Matches “{version: 12}”, “{version: 13}”
- `C:\\[A-Za-z]+`: Matches “C:\Users”, C:\Documents, “C:\Desktop”

##### Case-insensitive VS Case-sensitive Filtering

- By default regex filtering will be implemented as case-insensitive. `c.at`: Matches: “chat”, “Chat”, “CHAT” and “coat”, “Coat”, “COAT”
- regex filtering can be combined with Case sensitive UI filter

##### Capturing Groups

Regex capturing groups are recognized and the full query is highlighted, e.g. `s(e)g` will highlight "seg". Capturing groups can be used for replacement, e.g.”Name: Bob” can be searched by `Name: (.*?)` and replaced by using a backreference to `Jméno: $1`”. Missing backreferences are handled graciously, i.e. query `Name: (.*?)` with replacement `Jméno: $1, Title: $2` will be replaced as `Jméno: Bob, Title: $2`.

Examples for replace backreference:

- filter `(\d+),(\d+)` and replace `$1.$2` to normalize decimal separators (e.g. from 5,6 or 35,949 to 5.6 or 35.949)
- filter `(\d+)\.(\d+)` and replace `$1,$2` to normalize decimal separators (e.g. from 5.6 or 35.949 to 5,6 or 35,949)
- filter `(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})` and replace `$3/$2/$1` to reformat date (e.g. from 2025-06-05 to 05/06/2025)
- filter `ID-(\d{3,})` and replace `Ticket #$1` to extract number of the ticket (e.g. from ID-45321 to Ticket #45321)
- filter `(cat|dog)` and replace `$1-$1` to duplicate matched text (e.g. from cat to cat-cat and from dog to dog-dog)
- Optional group: filter `Hello(, (\w+))?` and replace `Hi $1` to transform greetings by replacing "Hello" before names or on its own (e.g. from Hello, John to Hi John and from Hello to Hi)

### Thinking Time and Editing Time (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/18931688168476-Thinking-Time-and-Editing-Time-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-06-11T11:40:52Z

In the editor, two distinct time metrics are tracked.

- Thinking time:

  The duration spent before making any edits after entering a segment.

  This data is visible within the [.MXLIFF](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709739992860#UUID-03e9320f-57b2-e624-e8c7-9b3d2a3da55e) file structure (per segment), in [advanced analytics](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/7756614696988#UUID-6379f0f3-4ab6-8620-4efa-2d6dcd5ed40b) (in the `job_detail` table AA, per job) and in [Phrase Data](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709668525468#UUID-27b73490-9bcd-1f08-fa2c-e3d16be005dd).
- Editing time:

  The entire time spent in a segment (includes Thinking time).

  This data is visible within the .MXLIFF file structure (per segment), in post-editing [analysis](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709712007708#UUID-7ed2ed16-6064-f667-bb86-7d971d7004c9) (per match category), in advanced analytics (in `job_detail` table AA, per job), and in Phrase Data.

  Editing time is displayed in milliseconds when retrieved for post-analysis via API.

Collection of time-tracking stats (in ms) follows these principles:

![Time Tracking](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682232158492)

- User clicks into segment #1:

  - Counting of segment #1 thinking time starts
  - Counting of segment #1 editing time starts
- User starts editing segment #1:

  - Counting of segment #1 thinking time is stopped
  - Counting of segment #1 editing time continues
- User clicks into segment #2:

  - Counting of segment #1 editing time is stopped
- When a user re-enters segment #1, the counting starts again and the new times are added to the previous values. If edited upon re-entering, both times are updated. If there is no editing, times are not updated.
- The thinking and/or editing times are measured for each workflow step separately.
- Re-entering a segment

  If the user returns to a previously edited segment:

  - Time tracking resumes and the new time is added to the previous recorded values.
  - If additional edits occur, both thinking and editing times update.
  - If no edits occur, time values remain unchanged even if the segment is reconfirmed.

### Auto-complete (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709700246940-Auto-complete-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2025-02-18T10:45:43Z  
> Labels: 2BTr

Auto-complete suggests words or phrases while typing in a target segment, improving translation speed. Auto-complete suggestions are based on matches from [TM](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709688865692#UUID-c58dd835-39ea-1a94-02d1-9f2517fd6d75), [TB](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709733372188#UUID-ca45e09b-442e-336f-3257-2983bccd0503) and [MT](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709692009884#UUID-5ee4d7fd-b6eb-a722-73da-3fdcb23390b0) (if applied to the job).

If suggestions are available in the [CAT pane](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709683926812#UUID-4c833ac1-32c2-c1cb-2d80-b6411f03a8be "CAT Pane (TMS)"), they are presented when typing in a target segment. **Tab** applies the suggestion.

Auto-complete can be activated in the editor from the Tools menu or under Preferences on the Misc tab.

##### Note

Auto-complete does not support non-space languages (Japanese, Chinese, Korean).

### Tags (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709695024412-Tags-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-09-18T06:06:31Z  
> Labels: 2BTr

Tags represent non-translatable text; some CAT tools refer to them as placeholders. Non-translatable text can represent variables, special formatting, formal names, code, etc.

Tags must be copied from source to target to ensure formatting and variables are preserved correctly in the exported target file.

##### Important

Issues with [tags](https://support.phrase.com#UUID-53d95c01-b0c5-aae5-dff5-68dcc38c3ea1 "Tags (TMS)") are a common cause of export errors (e.g. File couldn't be generated), especially for file types such as [spreadsheets](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709604373532#UUID-a68697a1-3ac9-5b8d-6497-961d901e4c2e) (MS Excel based) and [.XML](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709623320348#UUID-2dc3473c-ad75-e6d1-6d94-f27d2944443c). Always ensure tags and formatting are correct before exporting files by running [quality assurance](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709703799324#UUID-83632035-0d65-f957-b0dd-ad00704f8d25) checks.

Expand tags with **Ctrl+Shift+E** from the web editor, **Ctrl+Shift+T** from the desktop editor, or from the Edit menu.

#### Tag Types

There are four types of tags:

![tags_overview.jpeg](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682185107612)

1. **Unpaired/single tags**

   Represent, as an example, the position of a footnote in a segment or a joined segment.

   Insert unpaired tags by clicking on a required location in the text and click **F8**.

   Unpaired tags are singular.
2. **Custom tags**

   To insert a custom tag or custom paired tag into the target:

   - From the Edit menu, select Tags , Create Custom Tag or Create Custom Paired Tag.

     The custom tag is displayed as grey instead of blue.

   Custom tags can only be added to file formats supporting tags in the completed file (such as HTML).
3. **Joined Tags**

   [Joined segments](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709678012828#UUID-0d65fa6f-a518-11dc-7467-b46c79496b52 "Segments (TMS)") tags are a special type of unpaired tag. The joining point is indicated with the `{j}` tag.
4. **Paired tags**

   Represent formatting that spans across a section of text. As an example, a section of text in a segment may have a different font or a section of text may be highlighted.

   Paired tags have an opening and a closing.

   Insert paired tags by selecting the text to be tagged and click **F8**.

Tags are not included in the word count when calculating an [analysis](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709712007708#UUID-7ed2ed16-6064-f667-bb86-7d971d7004c9). Each join tag is replaced with one space.

#### Using Tags

Incorrect tagging can lead to improper translations. If tags are missing in the target, Phrase attempts to auto-complete when the completed target file is being generated. If missing or incorrect, add tags manually to the target and in as close a position and order as possible when compared to the source.

##### Tags in Source

If tags are removed from a source, QA can not correctly check it against the target. A Can't download file with missing tags... error is presented on file export with no QA tag warnings.

If this occurs, follow these steps:

1. Export the job to a bilingual .TMX file.
2. Import the .TMX file into a temporary TM.
3. Re-import the original file.
4. Pre-translate the new job using the temporary [TM](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709688865692#UUID-c58dd835-39ea-1a94-02d1-9f2517fd6d75).
5. Check the pre-translation results, and run [QA](https://help.memsource.com/hc/en-us/articles/360012872099) against the new job with Formatting and tags enabled.
6. If successful, the temporary TM can be populated by confirming the segments and it can be imported into the main TM.

##### Inserting Tags to Targets

Tags are inserted through either the Edit menu or keyboard shortcuts **F8** or **CTRL+ALT+**# to specifically number the tag and **Ctrl+,** to insert by section.

##### Editing Tag Content

To edit target tag content, follow these steps:

1. Press **CTRL+SHIFT+E** in the web editor, **Ctrl+Shift+T** in the desktop editor or from the Edit menu, select Tags , Expand Tags.

   Tag content is presented.
2. Click a tag to be edited in the web editor, click a tag and press **F2** in the desktop editor.

   Edited tags are displayed in grey to indicate differences from a source tag.

##### Quality Assurance

The [quality assurance](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709703799324#UUID-83632035-0d65-f957-b0dd-ad00704f8d25) feature can be used to ensure tagging is in place and accurate.

If a project has been set up to check tags by the Project manager, missing or incorrect tags will prevent the export of a valid translated document.

##### Tags in Translation Memories

Phrase stores a translation unit's tags together with the segment when saving the unit to a translation memory (TM). Exported TM files, in both .TMX and .XLSX format, represent inline tags as numbered placeholders, for example `{1}` or `{2}`, rather than the `{1>...<1}` notation shown in the CAT editor.

The `mdata` [property](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/9386879926556#UUID-82a39631-b1e5-ec9e-c57f-497c93f8e6a9) holds the full detail for each placeholder, including its role, for example the start or end of a paired tag, and its underlying content, such as embedded markup or non-translatable text. The `mdata` property is a JSON array of objects with `id`, `type`, and `content` fields, and uses the same structure in both export formats.

###### Tags in MXLIFF Files

Bilingual .MXLIFF files use the same numbered-placeholder notation as TM exports: an inline tag appears in <source> and <target> as `{1}`, `{2}`, and so on (paired tags as `{2>translatable<2}`), rather than the `{1>...<1}` notation shown in the CAT editor.

The full detail for each placeholder, i.e. its type and its underlying content, such as embedded markup, a variable, or a processing instruction from the authoring system, is stored in the `<m:tunit-metadata>` and `<m:tunit-target-metadata>` elements of the same `<trans-unit>`, one `<m:mark>` entry per placeholder, matched by `id`. MXLIFF does not use the XLIFF inline elements `<g>`, `<x>`, `<bpt>` or `<ept>`.

To compare tag placement between source and target, use the numbered placeholders together with their `<m:mark>` entries, or run [Quality Assurance](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709703799324#UUID-83632035-0d65-f957-b0dd-ad00704f8d25) on the job, which reports tag problems per segment.

#### Importing with Tags

As tags are used to mark parts of a text with different formatting most of these format changes are obvious. Common tags are different fonts, font sizes, or colors. Some tags, such as style changes, are minor and may not be as visible.

If a file type has options for how tags are imported, they are defined in [file import settings](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709621471516#UUID-f8f148d5-8914-1eb9-f214-b029d41dbe85) when creating a [job](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709686763420#UUID-33f88350-daa8-2ab2-e7ce-e35300ec60f8).

Imported files containing many unseen tags may generate the TOO\_LARGE\_INPUT: Too large tag metadata of source text of segment no. ... error due to too much metadata. This easily occurs with the import of complex file types such as .PDF that have been converted to text formats.

When importing text files it is suggested:

- If converting a .PDF file using an OCR program, save as plain or unformatted text. Open the file in a text editor to apply required formatting such as adjusting fonts, font size, colors, columns, spacing, etc.
- There are a number of tools available for cleaning text files of extra code. [CodeZapper](http://asap-traduction.com/CodeZapper) is recommended.
- Use the Minimize number of tags option when importing MS Word files, or text files using MS Word file types. This option attempts to remove all tags considered unnecessary from the source text imported for translation. This is an automated process and may remove required formatting. If using this option, compare the completed file with the original document to ensure required formatting is in place.

Imported [slides](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709618524828#UUID-d830a4d4-bb5c-bfe3-7042-554ede7479a6) may show many formatting tags in the [editor](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709683847964#UUID-1da30c04-11f8-6314-17a0-f4948f4cfed6 "CAT Editor (TMS)"). The formatting tags could have been applied during the conversion from the original format (e.g. PDF) to preserve the original appearance as much as possible: wide and narrow text spacing, subscripts and superscripts, different text colors, varying font sizes, etc.

In such case, using online [tag cleaner tools](https://www.translatortools.net/docs/transtools/powerpoint-tag-cleaner) is recommended.

### Comments (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709700374044-Comments-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-09-23T06:07:02Z  
> Labels: 2BTr

While the editors are connected to the server, users can add comments and create conversation threads about an entire segment (using per-segment comments), multiple selected segments (bulk commenting) or a section of a segment (using in-line comments).

The conversation feature allows cooperation between all active users involved in a job (Linguists, Project managers, Guests). A comment made in one step is visible across all steps providing communication throughout the workflow. Project managers can delete and edit comments made by Linguist users. A timestamp is recorded when comments are edited.

Conversations are scoped to a single job. Linguists assigned to different jobs in the same project do not see each other's comments across jobs.

Conversations can be exported to [bilingual .DOCX](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709688974620#UUID-adb08905-9ca5-55e5-3739-95bd935275ea) and opened in a .DOCX editor. Conversations in Bilingual .DOCX are read-only and any changes made in the .DOCX file are not imported back to the job. LQA values are not exported to the Bilingual .DOCX.

#### Add a Comment

To add a comment or start a conversation about a segment or a selected text, follow these steps:

1. Select a segment.

   - To comment about a particular piece of text (an in-line comment), select the text inside the selected segment.
2. Click the speech bubble icon ![speech_bubble.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682232379036) next to the segment or right-click the selected text and select Comment. The keyboard shortcut is **Ctrl+Shift+M**.

   The Comments pane ![Comments Pane](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682232402332) opens and selected text is presented.
3. Enter comment in text field.
4. Optionally, type or select **@** to add a [mention](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/7681232807708#UUID-67965664-7dc3-34ca-9c09-4723e36a1df9 "Mentions (TMS)") in the comment.

   The mentioned user receives in-app notifications. Email notification is sent if enabled in the project.
5. Click the up arrow ![up_arrow.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682232439068) to save the comment.

   Segments with comments are identified with a blue speech bubble icon ![speech_bubble_blue.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682201306012).

#### Add a Reply

Replies can be added to any posted comment. Replies are indented to help navigate the conversation. Replies can not be added as in-line comments.

To add a reply, follow these steps:

1. Click Reply under any comment in the Comments tab.

   A text field opens for the reply.
2. Enter reply text.
3. Optionally, type or select **@** to add a [mention](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/7681232807708#UUID-67965664-7dc3-34ca-9c09-4723e36a1df9 "Mentions (TMS)") in the comment.

   The mentioned user receives in-app notifications. Email notification is sent if enabled in the project.
4. Click Add reply.

   The reply is added to the conversation.

#### Bulk Commenting

Comments can be added to a selection of segments at the same time with a limit of 500 segments. The initial comment is considered the parent ![Parent_comment.jpg](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682232486172) in a selection with the following comments being the children ![Child Comment](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682201370524). Editing, deleting or resolving these selections can then be performed in bulk operations instead of as individual comments.

###### Relations in bulked comments

- Editing or replying to a child comment severs the relation to the parent comment (bulk operations can no longer be performed).
- Editing or replying to a parent comment does not break the relation to children.
- Deleting a parent comment breaks any relation among the children (bulk operations can no longer be performed).
- If the relationship is not severed, resolving a parent comment resolves the children as well.

To add bulk comments, follow these steps:

1. With the Comments pane displayed or by using the **Ctrl+Shift+M** keyboard shortcut, select a number of segments for commentary by clicking on them.

   The selected segments numbers will be indicated in the new comment window at the bottom of the pane.
2. Provide a comment and click Comment or the **Ctrl+Enter** keyboard shortcut.

   The comment is added to the specified segments with the parent comment indicated with ![Parent_comment.jpg](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682232486172) and the child comments indicated with ![Child Comment](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682201370524). Click the child icon to be taken to the parent comment.

Editing or deleting the parent comment gives options for whether the command should be applied to only the parent comment or to all children comments in the selection. Editing or deleting a child comment only applies the command to that selected comment.

Bulk comments are replied to as individual comments and not as a group. Resolving the parent comment resolves the children as well or the children can be resolved independently.

#### Editing comments

Editing and deletion options for comments are in the 3-dot menu ![More Menu](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682232583196) that appears when hovering over a comment in the Comments ![Comments Pane](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682232402332) tab.

#### Resolving comments

The comments in the tab can be filtered ![Menu_Triangle.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682168536732) for selected segments and unresolved comments. Once comments in a conversation have been addressed, mark the conversation as resolved. If the project manager has specified that comments are part of [quality assurance](https://help.memsource.com/hc/en-us/articles/115003484052-Quality-Assurance) checks, unresolved comments are displayed in QA warnings.

### LQA Assessments (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/27529737766044-LQA-Assessments-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-09-22T06:07:41Z  
> Labels: 2BTr

#### Available for

- Team, Professional, Business, Enterprise and Software UI/UX plans

Get in touch with [Sales](https://phrase.com/demo/) for licensing questions.

#### Available for

- Ultimate and Enterprise plans (Legacy)

Get in touch with [Sales](https://phrase.com/demo/) for licensing questions.

[Language Quality Assessment (LQA)](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709599557020#UUID-071f9a72-20ef-1bcd-9169-14a46ebe0449) is performed by reviewers in the [CAT editor](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709683847964#UUID-1da30c04-11f8-6314-17a0-f4948f4cfed6 "CAT Editor (TMS)") to evaluate the quality of translated content based on pre-defined criteria. Issues are flagged segment by segment, categorized by type and severity, and stored in a scorecard that contributes to a final quality score.

While [Quality Assurance (QA)](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709703799324#UUID-83632035-0d65-f957-b0dd-ad00704f8d25) checks are automated and look for technical issues like missing tags or typos, LQA assessments are performed by humans and focus on linguistic quality.

Creating and viewing LQA assessments are only available in [workflow](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709717879324#UUID-3d4fec12-4a9f-ace5-cd20-a1575786a6b7) steps in which LQA is enabled. The LQA pane itself is present in the editor for all workflow steps.

LQA for an LQA enabled step can be enabled only during project creation or when adding the step to a project. If creating a project with an LQA enabled step, but turning it off during project creation, it is not possible to enable it afterwards.

When jobs are shared between a Buyer organization and a Vendor organization, LQA assessment availability depends on whether an assessment is already open and on the scope of sharing. An LQA assessment is locked to whichever side, Buyer or Vendor, starts it first. The other side cannot start a new assessment or add to the existing one on that job or workflow step until the assessment is finished or discarded. While an assessment remains open on one side, the LQA option may not appear for the other side at all.

Permissions on an assessment already started by the other side depend on the sharing scope. When the whole project is shared, the receiving side can open the existing assessment in edit mode and add new issues. When only specific jobs are shared instead of the whole project, the receiving side is limited to reply-only access, without the ability to edit the assessment or add new issues.

When assessing content quality, different rules may be required for different content types or clients. Some content may need to have precise terminology and others may need to follow locale convention or be precise with target length and markup. Errors may also require different severities or assigned weights.

Overall feedback cannot be provided for joined jobs.

#### Add an LQA Issue

To add an LQA issue, follow these steps:

1. In the CAT Editor, select the LQA pane ![LQA_pane.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682232783388) and click Start LQA.
2. Select a segment.

   - To assess a particular piece of text, select the text inside the segment.
3. Click the flag icon ![lqa_flag.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682168655900)next to the segment to open the Error category drop-down list.
4. Select an Error category, Severity, if the issue is a repeated one and an optional description.

   Optionally, type or select **@** to add a [mention](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/7681232807708#UUID-67965664-7dc3-34ca-9c09-4723e36a1df9 "Mentions (TMS)") in the description and select the desired user or group of users from the list. Mentioned user(s) receive an [in-app notification](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709702543260#UUID-1f822e95-39f1-cc57-0234-5532047c453d) and email notification (if enabled in the project).
5. Click Flag issue.

   Once an issue is flagged, it can be edited, replied to or deleted from the ![ellipses.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682232840476) menu.

   - Replying to an LQA issue allows adding a [mention](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/7681232807708#UUID-67965664-7dc3-34ca-9c09-4723e36a1df9 "Mentions (TMS)") by typing or clicking **@** and selecting the desired user or group of users from the list. Mentioned user(s) receive an [in-app notification](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709702543260#UUID-1f822e95-39f1-cc57-0234-5532047c453d) and email notification (if enabled in the project).
6. Repeat the last two steps to flag more issues as needed.
7. Click Finish LQA.

   The LQA results and all flagged issues are listed in the LQA tab.

Segments with LQA issues are identified with a solid flag icon ![solid_lqa_flag.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682218576540). Created LQA issues can be edited or deleted from the ellipses menu of a specific issue ![ellipses.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682232840476) (not available for issues created by others).

#### Add Bulk Issues

Issues can be added to a selection of segments at the same time with a limit of 500 segments. The initial issue is considered the parent ![Parent_comment.jpg](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682201710364) in a selection with the following issues being the children ![Child Comment](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682232913180). Editing or deleting these selections can then be performed in bulk operations instead of on individual issues.

###### Relations in bulked issues

- Editing or replying to a child issue severs the relation to the parent issue (bulk operations can no longer be performed).
- Replying to a parent issue does not break the relation to the children and replies are not propagated to the children.
- Edits to a parent can be optionally applied to only the parent or to the children as well.
- Deleting a parent severs the relation between the children (bulk operations can no longer be performed).

To add bulk issues, follow these steps:

1. With the LQA pane displayed, select a number of segments for flagging with an issue.

   The selected segments' numbers will be indicated in the New issue window.
2. Select an Error category, Severity, if the issue is a repeated one and optionally provide a description.
3. Select how the issue should be flagged in the selected segments:

   - Flag issue in subsequent segments as repeated issue.
   - Flag issue in all segments as non-repeated issue.

     Repeated issues do not have this option.
4. Click Flag issue.

   The issue is added to the specified segments with the parent issue indicated with ![Parent_comment.jpg](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682201710364) and the children indicated with ![Child Comment](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682232913180). Click the child icon to be taken to the parent issue.

Listed issues can be filtered ![Issue Filter](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682218659996). Options can be combined and include filtering by severity or Only repeated issues and Only parent issues.

###### Scoring of bulked assessments

|  | Repeated issue unchecked with Flag issue in subsequent segments as a repeated issue. | Repeated issue unchecked with Flag issue in all segments as non-repeated issue. | Repeated issue checked with Flag issue in subsequent segments as a repeated issue. |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Segment 1 | Unique error - penalty added (parent issue) | Unique error - penalty added | Repeated error - no penalty added |
| Segment 2 | Repeated error - no penalty added | Unique error - penalty added | Repeated error - no penalty added |
| Segment 3 | Repeated error - no penalty added | Unique error - penalty added | Repeated error - no penalty added |

#### Generate LQA Assessments

To generate the LQA assessment, click Finish in the LQA tab. Overall feedback can be optionally applied.

A score will be calculated and a result will be displayed based on the pass/fail threshold set in the [LQA profile](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709599557020#UUID-071f9a72-20ef-1bcd-9169-14a46ebe0449). The score and the result are displayed in the LQA tab and on the [jobs](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709686763420#UUID-33f88350-daa8-2ab2-e7ce-e35300ec60f8) table in the LQA score column if LQA is enabled for that workflow step.

##### Tip

If the LQA score column is not visible, click the ![settings-7648874d097d6f25724f48b0f3da9403.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682201823900) icon on the jobs table and select Customize columns to enable it.

The score is calculated from the job's total word count.

**Scoring example:**

A text of 500 words is set to fail LQA when it contains 1 critical *Accuracy* error and 1 minor *Grammar* error. The *Accuracy* error is given a weight of 2.0 and *Grammar* a weight of 1.0. Critical severity is penalized with 10 points and minor severity with 1 penalty point.

1. Count the number of issues for each error category and multiply by respective severity weight and error weight:

   - Accuracy penalties = number of critical errors x critical error penalty x accuracy weight = 1 x 10 x 2.0 = 20 penalty points
   - Grammar penalties = number of minor errors x minor error penalty x grammar weight = 1 x 1 x 1.0 = 1 penalty point
2. Add up the penalties:

   - Penalty total = Accuracy penalties + Grammar penalties = 20 + 1 = 21
3. Calculate the pass/fail score, using the MQM scoring model [*Score = 1 - Penalty total/Wordcount*]:

   - Score = 1 - Penalty total/Wordcount = 1 - 21/500 = 0.958
4. Present the score result as a percentage:

   - Score % = 0.958 x 100 = 95.8
5. Enter Score % as your pass/fail threshold:

   - Your pass/fail threshold is 95.8 %

Clicking on the results in the jobs table opens a scorecard window with options to send the scorecard by email or export as a spreadsheet (.XLXS) file.

Right-click on more than one selected job to have the option to download multiple scorecards.

Phrase names scorecard files automatically and the name cannot be changed. A single scorecard downloads as `LQA_<project name>_<source language>_<target language>_<job filename>.xlsx`. When a download includes several jobs, the scorecards arrive in one ZIP archive named `LQA_<project name>_<project ID>.zip`, containing one .XLSX file per job. If the name before the extension exceeds 250 characters, Phrase truncates it to 250 characters before adding the extension.

The link to download the LQA scorecard received via email expires after 5 days.

One LQA scorecard email carries a single download link for every job included in the send. When the send includes more than one job, that link downloads a ZIP archive containing one scorecard per job. Keep the `{report.file.url}` [macro](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709617392540#UUID-9344883c-3d65-7641-8b0e-6dfb0aeb17b1) outside the `{jobInfo}` block, as in the default template. Phrase resolves `{jobInfo}` first, then substitutes `{report.file.url}` everywhere it appears, using the same link each time.

By default, the linguist assigned to the job can download their own LQA scorecard. To restrict scorecard downloads to project managers and administrators only, disable Allow linguists to download the LQA Scorecard in Access and security section of project settings. This can also be set as an organization-wide default in Access and Security section of Settings, which new projects will inherit.

The translation provider recorded on an LQA assessment (and shown in [Analytics](https://support.phrase.com/document/preview/76644#UUID-44770dfe-dff0-eaf9-bbfb-0dfb7837342a)) is captured once, when the assessment starts, from whichever provider is assigned as translator on the previous workflow step at that time. If no provider is assigned yet, the reviewer's name is used instead. Reassigning the translator afterward does not update this value on assessments that already exist.

##### Note

[Sharing](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709703948444#UUID-2fb330ab-e5ad-e017-5972-a9a75c1e0360) LQA scorecard download URLs across different organizations (i.e. Buyer and Vendor organizations) is not possible.

##### Edit a Finished LQA Assessment

Once an LQA assessment has been finished, its issues are locked and the scorecard becomes read-only. To make changes:

1. In the CAT Editor, select the LQA pane ![LQA_pane.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682232783388) and click the three-dot menu at the top of the pane.
2. Select Edit LQA.
3. Add, edit, or remove issues as needed.
4. Click Finish LQA again to regenerate the score and scorecard.

This reopens the assessment in place. Existing flagged issues are preserved.

Editing or deleting an individual LQA issue requires the job to be in Accepted status. If the job has moved to Completed or Delivered, the edit and delete options for that issue are no longer available.

#### LQA Score in Workflow Steps

When LQA is enabled in a workflow, all steps display the LQA score.

- If there is only one LQA step, all workflow steps show the same score.
- If there are multiple LQA steps, the score shown depends on the most recent LQA step:

  - Steps before and including an LQA step display that step’s score.
  - Steps after a later LQA step display its updated score.

**Example**

In a 5-step workflow where LQA is enabled in step 2 and step 4:

- Steps 1 and 2 show the LQA score from step 2.
- Steps 3, 4, and 5 show the LQA score from step 4.

As additional LQA steps are completed, the displayed score updates accordingly.

#### Assess a Repetition

Assessments can be added to [repetitions](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709708706460#UUID-4f304f9a-55d3-819c-4bb6-e151c7207dc5 "Repetitions (TMS)") with different flagging options with a limit of 500 segments.

To assess a repetition, follow these steps:

1. With the LQA pane displayed, select a repetition for flagging with an issue.

   Repetitions following the selected one can be flagged together.
2. Select an Error category, Severity, if the issue is a repeated one and optionally provide a description.
3. Select how the repetition is to be flagged:

   - Flag issue in subsequent repetitions as repeated issue
   - Flag issue in all repetitions as non-repeated issue

     If the issue has been indicated as a repeated one, this option is not available.
   - Flag issue in this segment only

     Subsequent or previous repetitions can be flagged independently.
4. Click Flag issue.

   The issue is added to the specified segments with the parent issue indicated with ![Parent_comment.jpg](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682201710364) and the children indicated with ![Child Comment](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682232913180). Click the child icon to be taken to the parent issue.

Listed issues can be filtered ![Issue Filter](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682218659996). Options can be combined and include filtering by severity or Only repeated issues and Only parent issues.

Editing or deleting the parent issue gives options for whether the command should be applied to only the parent issue or to all issues created in bulk, including the children. Editing or deleting a child issue only applies the command to the selected issue.

Repeating LQA issues may require different treatment and may be:

- Flagged as repeating and excepting the parent issue do not add any penalty points to the final LQA score.
- Flagged as a unique issues adding penalty points to the final LQA score with subsequent issues being unique as well and reflected in the score.

###### Scoring of repeated segments

|  | Repeated issue unchecked with Flag issue in subsequent segments as a repeated issue. | Repeated issue unchecked with Flag issue in all segments as non-repeated issue. | Repeated issue unchecked with Flag issue in this segment only | Repeated issue checked with Flag issue in subsequent segments as a repeated issue. | Repeated issue checked with Flag issue in this segment only |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Repetition 1 | Unique error - penalty added (parent issue) | Unique error - penalty added | Unique error - penalty added | Repeated error - no penalty added | Repeated error - no penalty added |
| Repetition 2 | Repeated error - no penalty added | Unique error - penalty added | No error logged | Repeated error - no penalty added | No error logged |
| Repetition 3 | Repeated error - no penalty added | Unique error - penalty added | No error logged | Repeated error - no penalty added | No error logged |
