### Analysis (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709712007708-Analysis-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-09-30T06:04:44Z  
> Labels: Project Manager, 2BTr, ar_tms, edited_at

Analysis calculates the character and word counts in selected files and identifies:

- [Repetitions](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709708706460#UUID-b94ef2c1-e8fa-b9ce-e18e-242b5873bd1b) (including cross-file repetitions)

  Only the first occurrence of a duplicated segment is counted separately, in the regular match-percentage or internal-fuzzy bucket. *Repetitions* counts subsequent occurrences of that same segment. Example: A job with exactly two identical segments shows *Repetitions: 1 segment*, not 2. This reflects the counting rule.

  Repetitions only counts subsequent occurrences of duplicate segments that have no translation memory match or that only have a fuzzy match. Segments that qualify for a 100% or 101% translation memory match take priority over the Repetitions bucket and are counted in the TM match category rather than in Repetitions.
- [Translation memory matches](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709683926812#UUID-fb5d0457-58e7-963b-d4dd-4a069f25139c),
- Non-translatables
- Internal fuzzy matches
- [Machine translation](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709692009884#UUID-5ee4d7fd-b6eb-a722-73da-3fdcb23390b0) suggestions

Analyses can also show the number of revisions made by a reviewer.

Analyses can be created by Project managers or Administrators. Linguists cannot be allowed to run their own analyses. Vendors may create analyses for shared jobs/projects.

Some CAT tools refer to analysis as statistics.

Organizational analytics are provided by the [analytics dashboard](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/6554447243036#UUID-4971a474-63e7-d58f-1e32-4fc570c69320).

Since different billing units are used in different countries, three calculation methods are available:

- **Characters**

  Without spaces.
- **Words**

  For languages that use spaces between words—excluding Chinese, Japanese, and Thai.
- **Pages**

  1800 characters with spaces—unrelated to the actual number of pages in a file.

#### Word Count

Due to different counting methods across different languages, word count as presented may not be the same as word counts produced by other applications.

Word count for analysis is different from the character count used for [MT calculation](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/11530492252444#UUID-3c8ba1b3-290a-5451-ba45-71797af5a755) and from the number of [TMS processed words](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/14409846225308#UUID-686ee438-7db4-5f6f-7f83-ff41950483a2) used for subscription billing.

- Each join tag is replaced with one space.
- Other tags are removed.

In languages using a [whitespace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitespace_character) for separating words (e.g., English):

- Each number sequence including `+-,.` is replaced with one character (using [regex](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709636670364#UUID-fecec79b-8d0e-daaa-3327-8435094210ec) expression `[+-]?[0-9]+([., -]?[0-9]++)*+`).
- Each sequence of whitespaces is replaced with one space.
- Whitespaces at the beginning and the end of segment are removed.
- Each sequence of characters different from space is counted as one word.

In Languages not using whitespace for separating words (e.g., Japanese):

- Some punctuation marks are removed from the text (using regex expression `[\u2000-\u206F\u2E00-\u2E7F\u3000-\u3004\u3006-\u301F\\p{P}]`).
- Segment is split into sequences of characters belonging to non whitespace (NWS) Han, Hiragana, Katakana, and Thai scripts and sequences of characters not belonging to those scripts (WS).
- Total number of words = (number of words from NWS) + (number of words from WS).
- Number of words from WS is computed as for English.
- Number of words for NWS is number of characters without whitespaces.
- For Thai, the number of words is number of characters without whitespaces divided by 2.

##### Note

Characters from CJK languages are counted as both characters and words.

#### Create an Analysis

To create an analysis, follow these steps:

1. From a Project page, select one or more Jobs.
2. Click Analyze.

   The Analyze window opens.
3. Select a Type from the dropdown list.
4. Provide a name if required.

   - Available macros for Analysis naming:

     - `{projectName}`
     - `{sourceLang}`

       Adds source language
     - `{targetLang}`

       Adds target language. If multiple languages are analyzed, the language will be empty.
     - `{userName}`

       Adds username of the assigned Linguist or Vendor. If multiple Linguists are assigned, the name will be empty.
     - `{workflow}`
     - `{innerId}`
     - `{fileName}`

       If more files/jobs are used for analysis, the `{fileName}` will be empty.
5. Select analysis options. In particular:

   - Applying the Exclude numbers option will affect the word count as numbers will not be calculated as words.
   - The Include internal fuzzies option compares segments in the analyzed job for similarities within the file as opposed to only comparing them against a TM.

     If Separate internal fuzzies is checked, internal fuzzies matches are displayed as a separate category in newly created analyses. For example:

     A translation job with 10 source words includes the following segments, where only the last character differs:

     - I bought a new car.
     - I bought a new car!

     In case no matches are found in the TM, a default analysis will display:

     | IF options | TM category: 0%-49% | TM category: 95%-99% | IF category: 95%-99% |
     | --- | --- | --- | --- |
     | *Include IF* disabled | 10 words |  |  |
     | *Include IF* enabled + *Separate IF* disabled | 5 words | 5 words |  |
     | *Include IF* + *Separate IF* enabled | 5 words |  | 5 words |
6. Click Analyze.

   The analysis, or analyses are added to the list.
7. Click on an analysis in the list to view it in the Analysis detail page or download it for rendering in a project management application.

##### Note

Analysis options can be set when creating an analysis, at the [project level](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/10825091328028#UUID-d7b8121c-4488-b077-5493-6ca7d30d48d5 "Project Settings (TMS)"), or globally under Settings ![Setup_gear.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682111265820).

Analysis results are calculated independently for each language pair against that language's own TM. Even when a project uses a shared TM across multiple target languages, each language pair maintains its own set of translation units. The same source segment can score differently in each language, resulting in different match percentages and net rates across target languages within the same project, even when analysis settings are identical.

Three analysis types are provided:

#### Default Analysis

Default analysis is the standard analysis run on source segments *before* translation. It provides the baseline analysis of a job that can be used with the post-editing analysis to determine how much effort was put into translating that job. This baseline is also used as the basis for generating [quotes](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709635877020#UUID-317de099-f8f9-9c94-dde1-36018cb96947) for clients.

The [TM threshold](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/16057517629852#UUID-d9a2d239-b777-2c81-0f7f-8c482950761a "Translation Memory Threshold Optimizer (TMS)") set in [pre-translation](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709717749788#UUID-29b9c1a8-1319-5c47-df68-b0fd50de107c "Pre-translation (TMS)") is used by default but can be changed if required.

A breakdown of segment/word/character counts is produced and if used in a project, TM matches are identified along with non-translatables, internal fuzzy matches and [QPS](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709672289180#UUID-054981cd-9a0e-32bf-79b7-cd6167ebf444) (if enabled).

##### Important

Running a default analysis after translation produces incorrect analyses.

Analysis results are calculated independently for each target language against that language's own translation memory. In a project with multiple target languages, the same source segment can receive different match percentages, or no match at all, in each language pair, since each language pair has its own translation history in the TM. As a result, the word count distribution across match categories, and the resulting net rate, can differ across target languages within the same project even when analysis settings are identical.

#### Post-editing Analysis

Post-editing analysis is run on target segments and indicates editing effort; how much editing the text required from a linguist or proofreader. It is run after post-editing is complete.

When a linguist clicks on an untranslated segment, the current highest translation memory match, machine translation suggestion, and/or non-translatable is saved for that segment and is used in post-editing analysis.

Post-editing analysis can be launched from any workflow step and is calculated as the difference between the text inserted from available source (e.g. TM/MT) and the post-edited result in the segment target.

Post-editing analysis extends the traditional translation memory analysis to include machine translation (MT) and non-translatables (NT). [Third-party MT engines](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709692009884#UUID-5ee4d7fd-b6eb-a722-73da-3fdcb23390b0) are also supported.

##### Important

Disabling Analyze TM post-editing and Analyze NT/MT post-editing does not exclude TM/MT matches from the analysis. In this case, the analysis considers the score of the higher available match instead of the post-editing effort.

A 101% TM result in a post-editing analysis does not necessarily mean the segment was translated from TM.

**Example**

A job translated using MT can still appear as 101% TM if Analyze TM post-editing is disabled and a 101% TM match was available when the segment was opened.

###### Post-analysis options

Post-editing options are used for calculating the post-editing effort required for matches from the translation memory (TM), non-translatables (NT) and machine translation (MT).

**Analyze TM post-editing enabled**

- Intended for low-quality TMs that contain high percent matches that require Linguist editing.
- Indicates post-editing effort for the TM.
- Contains only 100% matches in the analysis. In-context 101% matches from the TM have no effect on the calculation.

**Analyze TM post-editing disabled**

- Intended for high-quality TM where matches should be edited as little as possible to reduce cost.
- Indicates both 101% and 100%.
- Indicates TM matches offered to the Linguist when the segment is opened (not the actual Linguist's post-editing effort).
- Indicates post-editing effort for machine translation and non-translatables.

**Analyze NT/MT post-editing enabled**

- If the MT or NT suggestion was accepted without further editing it is presented as a 100% match in the analysis.
- If Linguist changes the MT, the match rate will be lower. The score-counting algorithm is the same as that used to calculate the score of translation memory fuzzy matches.
- Editing of an NT will cause the segment to be presented as 0-49% NT.

**Analyze NT/MT post-editing disabled**

- Entries from MT/NT without any estimated score will be considered TM 0%-49% matches. They will be indicated as translated by the Linguist with the MT not considered.
- [QPS](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709672289180#UUID-054981cd-9a0e-32bf-79b7-cd6167ebf444) and [Phrase Language AI](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709660879516#UUID-b0d64b4f-fa01-f7c3-006a-40e0ee0dedd2) matches higher than 75% will be in the MT column in their respective matches.
- Indicates NT/MT matches offered to the Linguist when the segment is opened (not the actual Linguist's post-editing effort).

**Automatically generate post-editing analysis before a source update**

- Analysis is created:

  - For each updated job.
  - For each individual provider individually and assigned to that respective provider.
- Analysis is not created if:

  - No linguist or vendor is assigned.
- Analysis counts confirmed and translated segments.
- Analysis follows the naming convention:

  - `UpdateSource #{innerID}{workflow}`
- Analysis will be created with Units counted (source), Analyze NT post-editing, Analyze TM post-editing and Analyze MT post-editing selected.

**Count units of the**

- source/target

  Select which word count will be presented in the analysis. A target word count may be higher than a source word count.

  Does not affect match scoring.

#### Compare Analysis

##### Available for

- Team, Ultimate and Enterprise plans (Legacy)

Get in touch with [Sales](https://phrase.com/demo/) for licensing questions.

The Compare analysis feature is only available in projects with workflow steps. It compares two versions of a file in different Workflow steps on a segment level and analyzes how the two versions differ. If there are no project specific settings for the analysis, default settings are used and may result in incorrect reports.

**Example**

A comparison between the translation and review steps indicates the actual effort of a reviewer by identifying how much the translation changed during the review step.

Analysis can be run on multiple jobs and can be grouped in two ways:

- **Analyze by provider**

  - For a project with many jobs assigned to various Linguists or Vendors. Used to:

    - Create separate analyses containing files assigned to individual Linguists or Vendors.
    - Assign analyses to a provider making the analyses visible to their Linguists/Vendors.

    [Net rate scheme](https://help.memsource.com/hc/en-us/articles/360014250379) will be pre-selected as an option if one is applied to the provider.
- **Analyze by language**

  - If a project contains multiple target languages, the analyses of all files can be run in a batch creating a separate analysis for each individual language.

    To analyze by language, follow these steps:

    1. From a Project page, select all Job files.
    2. Click Analyze.

       The Analyze window opens.
    3. Maintain default settings and select Analyze by language.
    4. Click Analyze.

       Job analysis is prepared by language.

    ### Note

    Unselect this option to create one single analysis for a multilingual project.

#### Analysis Recalculation

When the source file for an analysis is updated, it is marked as outdated ![yellow_warning.jpg](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682159515548) in the analysis table.

Recalculating applies settings used for the original analysis.

[Vendors](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709703948444#UUID-5749c887-b7e0-35b4-0617-8ed9c02e2ecb "Sharing (TMS)") are not allowed to recalculate analyses created by Buyers.

To recalculate using new source file, follow these steps:

1. Select the outdated analysis(es)
2. Click Recalculate.

   The Recalculate analysis window opens until the recalculation is processed. When closed, the recalculation is complete and the outdated indicator is cleared.

###### Customize the Analysis view

Segments, Pages, Words, Characters, and Percents columns can be displayed/hidden in the Analysis table. The Editing time column is also available for post-editing analysis and indicates how many seconds were spent editing a segment.

###### Download an analysis

To download an analysis, follow these steps:

1. Click Download to present the dropdown menu and select:

   - CSV (Comma Separated Values) with or without characters and readable with spreadsheet applications.
   - LOG (Similar to SDL Trados format) and readable with most project management applications.
   - JSON (JavaScript Object Notation), a lightweight data-interchange format.

   Only analysis downloaded in JSON format will include a breakdown of NT, MT, TM and internal fuzzies (IF) data per match type.
2. Selecting a file type triggers the download.

These files can be imported into most project management software systems.

###### Apply a [net rate scheme](https://help.memsource.com/hc/en-us/articles/115003978132-Net-Rate-Schemes)

A discount to words/characters/pages can be applied in an analysis. A discounted translation volume is immediately calculated and displayed directly in the analysis in the Net rate row.

To remove the net rate scheme from the analysis, leave the field next to the Apply net rate button empty.

When a net rate scheme is applied to the analysis, the downloaded file with the analysis shows weighted word counts in each match category.

#### Assign Analysis to a Provider

To assign an analysis to to a provider, follow these steps:

1. Select an analysis from the list and click Edit.

   The editing page opens.
2. Select a Provider from the dropdown list.
3. Click Save.

   The analysis will be available to the assigned provider on the [linguist](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709735838492#UUID-911ee8d4-ecc1-0c38-8f71-7c22f1646545) portal.

---

### Pre-translation (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709717749788-Pre-translation-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-09-18T06:04:24Z  
> Labels: Linguist, Project Manager, 2BTr, ar_tms

Pre-translation is the initial application of non-translatables, [translation memories](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709688865692#UUID-c58dd835-39ea-1a94-02d1-9f2517fd6d75), [machine translation](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709692009884#UUID-5ee4d7fd-b6eb-a722-73da-3fdcb23390b0) and/or [human translation engines](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709681535516#UUID-862b9e0b-dece-a80e-c0ef-7bc4fab87426) against a source text before it is presented to the Linguist in an [editor](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709683847964#UUID-7174fb87-7107-2f32-ce55-5e040de5446c).

Pre-translation settings can be set in [global settings](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/10825091328028#UUID-d7b8121c-4488-b077-5493-6ca7d30d48d5 "Project Settings (TMS)"), when creating or editing a [project](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/10825044285340#UUID-4f1d1f73-fcde-4de9-9259-bf054ae4b696 "Create a Project (TMS)") or when defining a [project template](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709647439772#UUID-94346683-ae2a-16b5-7e16-94a554612687).

They can also be set for individual jobs via the **Pre-translate** button in the [job](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709686763420#UUID-33f88350-daa8-2ab2-e7ce-e35300ec60f8) table but without options for the auto-propagation of [repetitions](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709708706460#UUID-b94ef2c1-e8fa-b9ce-e18e-242b5873bd1b).

#### Pre-translation Options

Pre-translation inserts matches into the target segments, but does not confirm or lock them unless the corresponding Set segment status to 'confirmed' for or Lock segment for options were selected. Unconfirmed segments are not counted as completed, so a job can be fully pre-translated while progress still shows 0%. The job status remains New, unless setting job as completed was selected.

To check pre-translation results, open the job in the editor and review the target segments.

If any of the selected resources (TM/NT/MT) fail when pre-translation is run on a job, the entire process is canceled. No matches from any resource are populated, and an error message is displayed on the [project page](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/10825091188252#UUID-393f1990-2289-4851-99b3-2bdbe8cea0bf "Project Page (TMS)").

- Overwrite existing translations in target segments
- Pre-translate on job creation
- Pre-translate from

  - Translation memory

    Use of a [TM](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709688865692#UUID-c58dd835-39ea-1a94-02d1-9f2517fd6d75) if assigned to the project and pre-translation threshold.

    The pre-translation threshold specifies the minimum score required for insertion of translation memory matches.

    ### Note

    TM match scores can be affected by tags and wrapper-tag structure. Asymmetric wrapper-tag matches are downgraded from 100% to 99% fuzzy matches. If the pre-translation threshold is set to 100%, these matches are not inserted during pre-translation.
  - Non-translatables

    ### Note

    [Non-translatables](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709683926812-CAT-Pane-TMS#non-translatables-0-4) (NT) detection relies on an AI algorithm. Misclassifications can occur, and segments flagged as non-translatable may still require translation. Review NT-filled segments before confirming them.
  - Machine translation

    Use of [MT](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709692009884#UUID-5ee4d7fd-b6eb-a722-73da-3fdcb23390b0) and/or [QPS](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709672289180#UUID-054981cd-9a0e-32bf-79b7-cd6167ebf444) if assigned to a project.

    - Apply MT only when there's no TM match at or above the threshold
    - Compare TM, NT and MT scores and apply the best match

    Available MT is presented in job resources notifications in the [CAT editor](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709683847964#UUID-1da30c04-11f8-6314-17a0-f4948f4cfed6).
- Set [segment](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709678012828#UUID-753af50b-27d0-e386-418a-452ed30e0083) status to 'confirmed' for

  Using this option does not save confirmed [100%/101% matches](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709683926812#UUID-fb5d0457-58e7-963b-d4dd-4a069f25139c) into the project's TM in the write mode.

  - 100% non-translatables
  - Machine translation suggestions (QPS)

    [Project Manager](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709756503196#UUID-f5990e2a-6aa9-ce27-fe52-bdad461726e6) users can define the QPS threshold for automated confirmation of segments pre-translated from MT based on the [QPS](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709672289180#UUID-054981cd-9a0e-32bf-79b7-cd6167ebf444) score.

    Default threshold is set to 100%. Segments confirmed after pre-translation are not saved into the project's TM in the write mode.

    ### Note

    QPS threshold customization is available for Team plans and higher. Get in touch with [Sales](https://phrase.com/demo/) for licensing questions.
- Set job or project to 'completed' options.

  - *Set job to 'completed' once = pre-translated*

    Completes only the job in the workflow step pre-translation was triggered from.
- Lock segment for

  Locking conditions are independent. A segment does not need to meet multiple conditions.

  If multiple locking options are enabled, they are applied sequentially based on the order defined in this section. Once a segment is locked by any step, it is excluded from all subsequent steps and cannot be modified or unlocked by them.

  - Machine translation suggestions (QPS) above the threshold

    [Project Manager](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709756503196#UUID-f5990e2a-6aa9-ce27-fe52-bdad461726e6) (PM) users can define the QPS threshold to automatically lock segments pre-translated from MT above a certain QPS score. Locked segments are visible in the CAT editor but cannot be changed or confirmed by linguists. If required, PMs and Administrators can unlock segments.

    Default threshold is set to 100%.

    This condition is applied in sequence with other locking options and only affects segments that were not locked by previous steps.
  - Meets Quality profile review criteria

    Only available if [Quality profiles](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/25865045974300#UUID-7b57e446-f5e2-e696-aaf1-8713b94eab34) are enabled in the organization.

  ### Note

  Translation memory and other locking conditions are processed first. QPS and Quality profile evaluation are applied only to the remaining unlocked segments. Segments locked by QPS are not evaluated by Quality profiles.

##### Tip

Choose automatic confirmation of MT suggestions when:

- Segments should be marked as completed for workflow tracking purposes.
- It's acceptable for linguists to review and modify the MT suggestions after confirmation.

Choose automatic locking of MT suggestions when:

- Edits must be fully prevented to avoid introducing potentially inaccurate translations into the TM.
- Ensuring TM quality across multiple projects and clients is a priority.

**Use Case**

- Confirm and lock translated segments

  Configure pre-translation settings to prevent duplicated effort by translation providers and ensure the job [analysis](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709712007708#UUID-05eefa40-a781-cd06-519e-724f4379f416 "Analysis (TMS)") accurately reflects the work required:

  1. In the Pre-translate from section, select the Translation memory option.
  2. Set segment status to 'confirmed' for 100/101% TM matches.
  3. In the Lock section, select the 101% translation memory matches and 100% translation memory matches options.

     Confirmed and locked segments will no longer appear as editable in the CAT editor.

     ### Note

     TM matches with asymmetric wrapper tags are scored as 99% instead of 100%. In these cases, the segments will not be auto-confirmed or locked by settings that apply only to 100%/101% TM matches.
  4. If required, navigate to the Analysis project settings and select to exclude confirmed and locked segments from the analysis.

##### Pseudo-translation

Pseudo-translation is used to create dummy text based on the target language. Both ASCII and Non-ASCII characters are supported. The text is used to simulate how a translated text may appear inside a layout based on contraction or expansion due to the translation. Pseudo-translation can also help indicate all translatable text is exported.

##### Pseudo-translation options

- Pseudo-translate using:

  Specified character(s) is added to source text.
- Add to target segment start:

  Specified character(s) is added to the beginning of the segment.
- Add to target segment end:

  Specified character(s) is added to the end of the segment.
- Transliterate:

  A comma separated list of characters can be provided.

  **Example**:

  aá,AÁ,bь,Bβ,cć,CĆ,dđ,DĎ,eé,EÉ
- Segment key hash length (characters):

  For pseudo-translations with a segment key, a pseudo-string to be prepended with a numerical hash value of the segment key can be provided.
- Target segment length (%):

  Specify how much contraction is anticipated.

#### Pre-translating with QPS

Using QPS in pre-translation reduces the amount of content requiring post-editing.

High quality matches from a [TM](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709688865692#UUID-c58dd835-39ea-1a94-02d1-9f2517fd6d75) are inserted into target segments and auto-confirmed. The rest of the job is populated from MT and segments with a QPS score above the threshold are auto-confirmed. Linguists need only focus on low quality matches that require their attention. In some cases, jobs may be fully auto-confirmed and set to completed without any human post-editing.

If set at the organization level, all projects benefit from the workflow and pre-translation can be adjusted for individual project templates or projects.

To use QPS in pre-translation, follow these steps:

1. Select the translation memories and [Phrase Language AI](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709660879516#UUID-b0d64b4f-fa01-f7c3-006a-40e0ee0dedd2) profile for the project.
2. From the Settings ![Setup_gear.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682175399196) page, scroll down to the Project settings section and select Pre-translation.

   The Pre-translation page opens.

   For an individual project template or project, click Edit on the project page.

   The Edit page opens.
3. Optimize the pre-translation settings:

   1. From the Settings menu, click Pre-translation.

      The Pre-translation settings are presented.
   2. Set Pre-translate from translation memory threshold to 100%
   3. Enable Pre-translate from non-translatables.
   4. Enable Pre-translate from machine translation.
   5. Enable Display quality-estimated machine translation matches in Phrase CAT editor.
   6. Set segment status to **confirmed** for:

      - 101% and 100% translation memory matches
      - 100% non-translatable matches
      - Machine translation suggestions (QPS)

        Configure QPS threshold for machine translation according to quality goals. The default value is 100, but a different *good enough* score can be used when lower machine translation quality is acceptable.
   7. Ideally, enable Pre-translate on job creation to ensure pre-translation is applied to all jobs.
   8. Set job to **completed** once to Pre-translated and all segments are confirmed.
   9. Click Save.

      The settings are applied to the project or to the organization.

### Quality Assurance - QA (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709703799324-Quality-Assurance-QA-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-09-08T06:04:29Z  
> Labels: Linguist, Quality Assurance, Project Manager, 2BTr, ar_tms

[Quality assurance](https://support.phrase.com#UUID-34001785-1859-40db-8d3f-cd65ca43b0c3 "Quality Assurance - QA (TMS)") (QA) is a feature built into the editor. It detects translation issues by comparing source and target segments, checking the term base, spelling, content of the tags, and other configured checks. It helps translators detect formal errors and improve overall translation quality and consistency.

##### Important

Issues with [tags](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709695024412#UUID-9f36c0c5-d7f2-0f81-ec55-44efc63d0050) are a common cause of export errors, especially for file types such as [spreadsheets](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709604373532#UUID-a68697a1-3ac9-5b8d-6497-961d901e4c2e) (MS Excel based) and [.XML](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709623320348#UUID-2dc3473c-ad75-e6d1-6d94-f27d2944443c). Always ensure [tags and formatting](https://support.phrase.com#UUID-34001785-1859-40db-8d3f-cd65ca43b0c3_UUID-7ec6b09e-b1f8-8c72-b4d6-4100eba17aae "List of QA Checks") are correct before exporting files.

If set by a project manager, QA checks may be mandatory for projects. If mandatory, QA warnings must be mitigated before the jobs can be set to *Completed*. QA checks are also run on locked segments unless excluded by the project manager. The project's QA settings apply to all jobs it contains.

QA checks can be applied instantly, or manually and are displayed in the [QA pane](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709694857372#UUID-bccfa2a1-8f4d-d877-fc52-4d14891aba36):

- **Instant QA**

  Run on a segment when confirmed. If issues are identified, the segment is not saved to a translation memory until the Linguist resolves them.

  Instant QA can be enforced by project managers in [Access and Security](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709585565980#UUID-424b8fbe-2d60-48eb-891a-a4f1c5004c82) settings.
- **Manual QA**

  Checks all segments in the job. To be run by the Linguist before the job is set to *Completed*.

There is no reporting available for QA results.

#### Quality Assurance Default Setup

Administrators and project managers with rights to modify global settings can configure default QA settings, which apply to all new projects.

To configure default QA settings, follow these steps:

1. From the Settings ![Setup_gear.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682175460380) page, scroll down to the Quality section and click on Quality assurance.

   The Quality assurance page opens.
2. Select required settings and click Save.

   Settings are saved and will be applied to all new projects.

The quality assurance settings interface can also be accessed at the project level by editing a project or by editing a [project template](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709647439772#UUID-94346683-ae2a-16b5-7e16-94a554612687).

By default, all QA warnings can be set to *ignore* by Linguists/Vendors. For some QA checks, the project managers can disable the Can be ignored option in the QA settings so Linguists and Vendors will not be able to ignore these warnings when setting a job to *Complete*.

#### QA Status for Jobs

Whenever a QA check is launched for a job, the outcome is saved with the translation job with different values:

- **QA Warnings: Not launched**

  The QA has not been launched for this job.
- **QA Warnings: Incomplete**

  The QA has been launched for only part of a job (e.g. the user did not click the Show more link at the bottom of the QA warnings list) or the QA launched for the entire job was later edited.
- **QA Warnings: 2 (1 ignored)**

  The QA has been launched and it includes a total of 2 warnings of which 1 was marked as ignored.

Hover over the Confirmed value of a job on a project page to see QA Status.

#### QA Management Options

Only administrators and project managers can configure QA checks in projects. Linguists cannot enable, disable, or add checks themselves.

###### Forcing providers to run a QA check

Providers (Linguists and Vendors) can be prevented from setting a job to *Completed* unless a QA check is run and [warning mitigated](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709694857372#UUID-bccfa2a1-8f4d-d877-fc52-4d14891aba36). Project managers can also select which QA checks are applied and which can be set to *ignore* by Linguists.

To select which QA checks can be ignored, follow these steps:

1. From a project page, click Edit.

   The editing page opens.
2. Click Quality assurance.

   The QA checks table opens.
3. Select Linguists may not set jobs with QA warnings to Completed.
4. Deselect Can be ignored for any QA checks the Linguist/Vendor should not set to *ignore*.
5. Click Save.

   Settings are applied for that project.

###### Ignore in all workflow steps

QA warnings can be ignored across all workflow steps of a job. Once a QA warning is ignored in the first workflow step, it will not be reported again as unresolved in subsequent workflow steps.

To ignore QA warnings across workflow steps, follow these steps:

1. From a project page, click Edit.

   The editing page opens.
2. Click Quality assurance.

   The QA checks table opens.
3. Scroll down to the Other options section and select Ignore in all workflow steps.
4. Click Save.

   Settings are applied for that project.

#### List of QA Checks

The QA checks cover errors that range from spelling errors to tag issues and inconsistent terminology. Some checks can be [selected to be highlighted](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709683847964#UUID-7174fb87-7107-2f32-ce55-5e040de5446c) in the translation table.

| QA check | Function | Instant QA | Highlighted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Linguistic** | Selects all linguistic checks. |  |  |
| Empty target | The target contains no characters or tags. | Yes |  |
| Extra numbers in target | There are no extra numbers in the target. | Yes | Yes |
| Inconsistent translations | - A segment with an identical source but a different target precedes the checked segment. - A segment with an identical target but a different source precedes the checked segment. - Repetition exceptions and segments with an empty target are skipped. - ICU subsegments (or other structured messages) share the same visible source text but differ in metadata such as the context key. | Yes (with batch confirmations) |  |
| Leading and trailing spaces | There is a leading or trailing space in the target but not in the source. | Yes | Yes |
| Maximum target segment length in % of source | The target segment length is greater than the given parameter (default 130%).  This setting is independent of the option below, i. e. it may show warnings even if the target segment complies with the limits set in Maximum target segment length in characters or the source file. | Yes |  |
| Maximum target segment length in characters | The target segment length is greater than the given parameter (default 100).  If the source file contains max. target segment length information (which is imported via the job settings and applied by enabling the Max. target length as set during job creation option), that will override this check. | Yes |  |
| Missing numbers | The number in the source is not present in the target.  For example, the source has the phrase "1 and 2", but the target reads "1 and 3".  Note Is only applied to Latin based numbers. Script based representation of Latin numbers (such as the Bengali ১৮ for 18) are also not recognized. | Yes | Yes |
| Multiple spaces | There are multiple spaces in the target but not in the source. | Yes | Yes |
| Repeated words | Two or more adjacent words in the target are identical. | Yes | Yes |
| Spelling | The target contains misspelled words. | Yes |  |
| Target text identical with source one | - This is a QA check for text copied from the source to the target. - No warning will be displayed for segments containing only plain numbers, tags, or non-translatable characters. - Segments translated using the Non-translatables feature are ignored in this QA check. | Yes |  |
| Trailing punctuation | Trailing punctuation is different in the source and target.  For example, the source ends with "." but the target does not or vice-versa. | Yes | Yes |
| Unedited NT/MT fuzzy match | A fuzzy NT/MT match has been confirmed without being edited. | No |  |
| Unedited TM fuzzy match | A fuzzy TM match has been confirmed without being edited. | No |  |
| **Terminology** | Selects all terminology checks |  |  |
| Forbidden terms | Based on a target term (while a source term is not required). | Yes | Yes |
| Missing terms | - The terms (with status New and Approved) in the source do not have a corresponding term translation in the target. If the Ignore not approved terms option is selected, new terms are not considered. - A forbidden term is used for the translation. (Forbidden terms in the source are ignored.)  Only terms within the source will be checked.  For terms set to Fuzzy match, a suffix of up to a language-specific character limit may follow the term and still count as a match, which can cause false positives on unrelated longer words; set the term to Exact match and add related word forms (such as plurals) as separate term entries to avoid this. | Yes | Yes |
| Not allowed | The target contains strings that are not allowed. Characters, or alternatively, utf-8 codes, can be entered as strings that are *not allowed*.  Numerous strings can be entered if separated by commas.  Strings are case-sensitive. | Yes | Yes |
| **[Formatting and tags](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709695024412#UUID-9f36c0c5-d7f2-0f81-ec55-44efc63d0050)** | Selects all formatting and tags checks. |  |  |
| Empty tag content | The target tag content is empty, while the source tag content is not.  For example, the source reads `<a href="http://bbc.co.uk">` but the target shows "". | Yes |  |
| Inconsistent tag content | The tag content between the source and its corresponding target tag differ.  For example, the source shows `<a href="http://bbc.co.uk">`but the target contains `<"http://">` | Yes |  |
| Nested tags | Paired tags in the target are misplaced.  For example, there is {1>{2>abc<2}{3>abc<3}{4><4}<1} in the source and {1>{2>abc<2}{3>abc{4><3}<4}<1} in the target.  This option is disabled by default, but it is important to enable it for projects with [spreadsheet](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709604373532#UUID-a68697a1-3ac9-5b8d-6497-961d901e4c2e) files. | Yes |  |
| No text between the tags | There is a paired tag with no text between the tags in the target but not in the source.  For example, there is {1>abc<1} in the source and {1><1} in the target. | Yes |  |
| Tags & formatting | Tags/formatting are missing or invalid, or there are missing or redundant line breaks.  Example: the source contains "{1} {2}" but the target reads "{1}". | Yes |  |
| Tags-joined segments | The number of {j} tags is different in the source and target.  For example, the source is "xxx{j}yyy" but the target is "xxx yyy". | Yes |  |
| XLIFF tags | Designed to enforce structural correctness for internal XLIFF tags.  Paired tags (such as *bpt* and *ept*) are in the incorrect order in the completed target file.  For example, the source contains "bpt bpt ept ept" and the target contains "bpt ept ept bpt".  Follows XLIFF schema rules and applies only to XLIFF 1.2 and 2.0 file types. | Yes |  |
| **Workflow** | Selects all workflow checks. |  |  |
| Newer version in a preceding workflow step available | Checks whether newer versions of segments exist in preceding Workflow steps.  For example, a translator has modified a segment in the Translation Workflow step after it was revised in the Revision Workflow step. | Yes |  |
| Not confirmed segments | Checks to make sure each segment is confirmed. | No |  |
| Unresolved comment | Ensures that no segment contains an unresolved [comment](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709700374044#UUID-d5b89fba-f861-b990-6511-8db310f9bb86) in a conversation. | No |  |
| **Custom checks** | - Used to define checks based on [regular expressions](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709636670364#UUID-fecec79b-8d0e-daaa-3327-8435094210ec) as well as descriptions that will be displayed in the editor when such an issue is identified. Will be verified before being able to be saved. - Multiple conditions can be set using the Add button. - If both Source regular expression and Target regular expression are NOT empty, checks whether the counts of the regex matches differ between the source and the target text. - If Source regular expression is NOT empty and Target regular expression is empty, returns a warning when there is a match in the source text. - If Source regular expression is empty and Target regular expression is NOT empty, returns a warning when there is a match in the target text. - A warning is returned if the number of matches for each named group differs between the source and target regular expressions.  [Usage example](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709636670364#UUID-fecec79b-8d0e-daaa-3327-8435094210ec) | Yes |  |

#### Error Messages - QA

##### No results were returned from the QA web service. An error occurred while servicing the request.

Indicates that there was most likely a temporary server issue and QA was unavailable for a few minutes. Wait a couple of minutes and try running QA again. If the issue persists, check the [status page](https://status.phrase.com/) for an incident or contact the [support team](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/requests/new).

### Segmentation Rules (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709712126876-Segmentation-Rules-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-07-30T06:03:48Z  
> Labels: Project Manager, 2BTr, ar_tms

#### Segmentation

Segmentation is the splitting of source texts into smaller parts. This improves the retrieval of previously translated text from a [translation memory](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709688865692#UUID-c58dd835-39ea-1a94-02d1-9f2517fd6d75). Segments are presented in the [editor](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709683847964#UUID-7174fb87-7107-2f32-ce55-5e040de5446c) and can be [filtered](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709720416796#UUID-11936659-047d-2507-3e91-ab2208f2ef73). If a project has workflow steps, changes in segments are presented in the [translation changes pane](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709700120476#UUID-c995498b-b422-3cf9-f93c-432ac1c5ffb4).

Default segmentation rules correspond with specifics of each supported language and can be customized.

[Jobs](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709686763420#UUID-33f88350-daa8-2ab2-e7ce-e35300ec60f8) imported with bad segmentation such as poorly formatted document files or the application of inappropriate segmentation customization can affect TM match values. It is recommended that some time is spent reviewing and preparing the source file before importation; a common problem is the incorrect use of line breaks versus paragraph breaks.

**Example**:

Good segmentation:

- *Translation memories with multilingual target languages are supported and can be used bidirectionally.*

  Match value of 100%.

Poor segmentation

- *Translation memories with multilingual target languages are supported.*

  Match value of 100%.
- *and can be used bidirectionally.*

  Match value of 63%.

#### Customize Segmentation Rules

Customized segmentation rules can be applied to [jobs](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709686763420#UUID-33f88350-daa8-2ab2-e7ce-e35300ec60f8) and [project templates](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709647439772#UUID-94346683-ae2a-16b5-7e16-94a554612687). If a project requires a customized segmentation rule, a template will need to be created for that project. When set as primary, customized segmentation rules are applied to all new jobs imported for that source language.

There are two types of segmentation rules:

- Abbreviations to the .XLSX file
- Regular expression of .SRX files

To use customized rules, download the default rules, modify them, upload the modified file and then apply them to specified jobs.

##### Caution

When adding custom segmentation rules for a space-less CJK source language (while a target language will be using spaces as a word delimiter), ensure leading or trailing spaces are added to the target segments split by the custom rule; this delimits words in the translation. While this happens automatically in segments formed by the default segmentation rules, no spaces are added in manually split segments or those formed by additional custom segmentation rules.

##### Download Default Segmentation Rules

To download the default segmentation rules, follow these steps:

1. From the Settings ![Setup_gear.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682126646428) page, scroll down to the Project settings section and click on Segmentation.

   The Segmentation page opens.
2. Click Export XLSX/SRX.

   The Export XLSX/SRX window opens.
3. Select format:

   - **XLSX** provides an abbreviation list.
   - **SRX** provides regular expression rules.
4. Select the language to be customized from the dropdown list.
5. Click Download.

   The file is downloaded to your system.

To download a previously uploaded segmentation rule, follow these steps:

1. From the Settings ![Setup_gear.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682126646428) page, scroll down to the Project settings section and click on Segmentation.

   The Segmentation page opens.
2. If the File column is not displayed, click Customize to enable it.
3. Click on a filename to download the rule.

##### Edit Abbreviations in an .XLSX File

Abbreviations can be specified for individual languages after which new segments should not be created.

To edit abbreviations, follow these steps:

1. Open the downloaded .XLSX file in an editor.
2. Change the contents with the following formatting:

   The XLSX file must have two columns with no headings.

   - **Column 1**: Abbreviation to be specified
   - **Column 2**: Specification of segmentation behavior

     - **ABBR\_UPPER\_NUM**

       A new segment is *not* be created if the abbreviation is followed by white-space and then by a number, a symbol (math, currency signs, dingbats, etc.) or a word with the first letter in upper case.
     - **ABBR\_NUM**

       A new segment will *not* be created if the abbreviation is followed by white-space and then by a number.
3. Save the edited .XLSX file.

##### Edit Regular Expressions in an .SRX File

Editing .SRX files is a complex process suitable only for users experienced in using [regular expressions](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709636670364#UUID-fecec79b-8d0e-daaa-3327-8435094210ec)

There are several rules that can be changed in an SRX file:

- Import text from an XLSX file without segmentation; one cell is equal to one segment.
- Import text with a new line in order to split one segment into two.
- Use a colon (or any other character) as a segment separator.
- Forbid the use of a semicolon (or any other character) as a segment separator.
- Removing an abbreviation from the list (the text will be segmented).

These rules are *character-based*; only a single character can be used as segment separator. Groups of characters (for example: <p>) cannot be used as a segment separator.

To edit an SRX file, follow these steps:

1. Open the file in a text editor such as [Notepad ++](https://notepad-plus-plus.org/downloads/).
2. Edit using regular expressions or remove the inner segmentation completely.

   Example:

   ![BreakRules_Example.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682126681628)

   - `<rule break="no">`

     The list of rules, where the segment will not be broken. I.E. a list of abbreviations
   - `<rule> <beforebreak>`

     A regular expression for a character before a break (for example, at the end of a sentence ". ? ! :"). If you, for example, don't want segment text after a colon, simply delete `:` from every `<rule><beforebreak>` code.
   - `<rule> <afterbreak>`

     A regular expression for a character after a break (for example, at the start of a new sentence; a space and capital letter).
3. Save the modified SRX file.

##### Upload New Segmentation Rules

To upload modified or new segmentation rules, follow these steps:

1. From the Settings ![Setup_gear.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682126646428) page, scroll down to the Project Settings section and click on Segmentation.

   The Segmentation page opens.
2. Click New.

   The Upload custom XLSX or SRX segmentation file page opens.
3. Select a Language from the dropdown list.
4. Provide a Name for the rule.
5. Click Choose file.

   A file selection window opens.
6. Select the modified rules file for upload.
7. Check Primary if the custom segmentation rules will be the primary segmentation rules for the selected language.
8. Click Create.

   The Segmentation page opens and the rule has been added to the list.

##### Use Custom Segmentation Rules on Job Import

To use custom rules on a job import or configure target segment length, follow these steps:

1. At step 8 of [creating a job](https://support.phrase.com/document/preview/4557#UUID-86543056-6056-5c1b-8666-45bc5d78c2c8), click Segmentation and segment length from the File import settings.

   The Segmentation and segment length options dropdown opens.
2. Select the modified rules from the Source segmentation rules dropdown list.
3. Optionally, configure a limit for target segment length based on project requirements (e.g. subtitles translation):

   - Select Max. target segment length in % of source and enter the preferred percentage to limit the segment length based on the source segment.
   - Select Max. target segment length in characters and enter the character count to limit the segment length by number of characters.
4. Click Create.

   The job is created and added to the list using the specified segmentation rules.

##### Changing Segmentation Example (1 Cell 1 Segment)

Remove all *inner* segmentation rules from an SRX file leaving only the basic segmentation of the whole paragraph, element, or cell being applied. This segmentation rule can be applied to every file type (MS Word, XML, HTML, Excel, etc.).

Example:

|  | A | B |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Peter! Wait! |  |
| 2 | Hello. |  |
| 3 |  |  |

This XLSX example imported with default segmentation will have 3 segments: *Peter!*, *Wait!*, and *Hello*.

If all inner segmentation is removed leaving only the basic segmentation based on the Cell, then there are only two segments: *Peter! Wait!* and *Hello*.

Edit the SRX file to remove all the default segmentation rules, i. e. the code between `<!-- break rules -->` and `</languagerule>`.

Example:

![1cell-1segment-srx.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682111516316)

Cascading can cause this example not to work. In such a case, open the edited SRX file in Notepad++, find the two attributes of the `header` element and change both to `no`.

### Workflow (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709717879324-Workflow-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-09-25T06:04:39Z  
> Labels: Project Manager, 2BTr, ar_tms

#### Available for

- Team, Professional, Business, Enterprise and Software UI/UX plans

Get in touch with [Sales](https://phrase.com/demo/) for licensing questions.

#### Available for

- Team, Ultimate and Enterprise plans (Legacy)

Get in touch with [Sales](https://phrase.com/demo/) for licensing questions.

Translation projects often involve multiple roles, languages, file types, deadlines, and review stages. Without a clear structure, tasks can be missed, overwritten, or delayed. Workflows keep translation projects organized by defining who does what, and when.

A workflow represents the life cycle of a document (referred to as a [job](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709686763420#UUID-fd9f7aa5-833d-8c21-b340-4c0ee162758e "Jobs (TMS)") in Phrase TMS) in the translation process; a sequence of consecutive steps which lead to a desired output.

Workflow steps have a hierarchical structure determined by their order when set up. When a [segment](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709678012828#UUID-753af50b-27d0-e386-418a-452ed30e0083) is edited in a workflow step, it is propagated to a higher workflow step. As long as it remains unconfirmed and unedited, changes to that segment are propagated from the lower workflow step. Once the segment is edited or confirmed in the higher workflow step, changes from the lower workflow steps are not propagated; [changing a step to complete](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/10825557816092#UUID-e517b5b6-f7f5-9c64-1fde-d981f5d24c41 "Job Status (TMS)") while previous steps are still active results in the next step becoming available for [linguists](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709735838492#UUID-911ee8d4-ecc1-0c38-8f71-7c22f1646545) without changes from the previous steps being propagated.

The workflow feature enables the design of custom workflow steps for a project and then assign specific linguists to them. This role is recorded in the linguist's user profile and when a [project manager](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709756503196#UUID-f5990e2a-6aa9-ce27-fe52-bdad461726e6) is assigning linguists to new projects, linguists previously used for a specific workflow step are offered as relevant.

#### Setup Workflow Steps

*Translation*, *Revision* and *Client Review* steps are pre-defined. If more complex or custom workflows are required, these can be constructed with [Orchestrator](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/7681638082716#UUID-854884a1-a259-24f2-8a2b-18395b4ccfd5).

Projects can contain up to 15 workflow steps and once added cannot be removed. The order of the steps is defined in multiples of ten so that if a step is added later, it can be placed between existing steps.

A different set of workflows for different sets of languages can not be set up within one project.

Only workflow steps with a higher hierarchical order can be added to a project with existing workflow steps.

**Example:**

If a project is initially created with steps no. 1, 2 and 4, it would be possible to add a 5th step but not a 3rd step.

To setup workflow steps, follow these steps:

1. From the Settings ![Setup_gear.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682159815196) page, scroll down to the Project settings section and click on Workflow steps.

   The Workflow steps page opens.
2. Click New.

   The Create workflow step page opens.
3. Provide a name, abbreviation, order position and [LQA](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/27529737766044#UUID-8c8a9e28-99dd-f432-f780-331192127c69) if required.
4. Click Create.

   The step is added to the list.

#### File Handover

Final versions of translated files modified outside of Phrase can be added to a job. The addition of a final version to the job does not disrupt the existing workflow.

Enabling file handover adds a file upload field to the final workflow step. Final files can be uploaded at any time, but assigned [linguists](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709735838492#UUID-911ee8d4-ecc1-0c38-8f71-7c22f1646545) must upload the final version before [setting the job to complete](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/10825557816092#UUID-e517b5b6-f7f5-9c64-1fde-d981f5d24c41 "Job Status (TMS)") as it would not be editable by them afterwards.

Permissible file sizes are as per [limits](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5784117234972#UUID-c318163f-0b7f-cb70-4773-980cb156bf43). Multilingual formats (Excel, .XML, .CSV) are not supported.

File handover is not possible in the following cases:

- The file is uploaded for a [continuous job](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709711922972#UUID-16b738e3-887c-6bc1-636e-e1e51761c5b0 "Continuous Jobs - CJ (TMS)").
- The file is uploaded for a job created from a [connector](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709656492572#UUID-98e00ebc-37ac-490b-1577-e8f108fa5a9b).
- The file is multilingual.
- The file is split.

##### Note

*Completed file*: A translated file.

*Final file*: A completed file that has been modified outside of Phrase and imported back in.

**Use Case:**

- When files with richer layouts such as [InDesign](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709612714140#UUID-597144a5-689f-8d02-6cbd-25c84d93471a) files or [presentation slides](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709618524828#UUID-d830a4d4-bb5c-bfe3-7042-554ede7479a6) are translated, the layout may be changed by the translation. Clients may want to receive a final version with corrected layout, original fonts and graphics. It is expected that there will be no further changes to the text as it can no longer be reflected in the [TM](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709688865692#UUID-c58dd835-39ea-1a94-02d1-9f2517fd6d75).

To set up file handover, follow these steps:

1. Select a [project](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709748435484#UUID-fd006a60-d1b0-dc4b-8681-00d5464cd76e) or [project template](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709647439772#UUID-94346683-ae2a-16b5-7e16-94a554612687) that requires file handover and click Edit.

   The project editing page opens.
2. Expand ![Settings_expand.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682111638812) the Workflow settings.

   Workflow settings displayed.
3. Select Enable file handover.

   The last selected workflow step is marked as having File handover enabled. Changing the last selected workflow step always enables file handover for that step.
4. Click Save.

To add a file for handover, follow these steps:

1. From the [jobs](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709686763420#UUID-33f88350-daa8-2ab2-e7ce-e35300ec60f8) table, select a job in the final workflow step.

   The Upload final document field is enabled.
2. Click Upload final document.

   The Upload final document window opens.
3. Select the final file.
4. Click Upload.

   The file appears in the File handover column and is available for download from the [job table](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/10825571430172#UUID-a6d2ff65-0f54-10ab-be2f-2821d32d3c9e "Jobs Table (TMS)") or from a [portal](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709602111132#UUID-560b5531-f46e-bcd6-82d9-9a69f2af4a76).

   Click ![Red_X.png](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682126886300) to remove the file.

#### Managing Workflows

##### [Assigning jobs](https://support.phrase.com/document/preview/4557#UUID-86543056-6056-5c1b-8666-45bc5d78c2c8) in workflow steps

Every active workflow step in a project has a version of the selected job associated with it. Linguists can be assigned to translation and other Linguists to revision with final steps being a client with Linguist or Guest user rights.

If jobs in the first workflow step are still in progress, Linguists assigned to subsequent steps cannot start editing them. For example, proofreaders will not be able to edit jobs in the second workflow step until the jobs are marked as completed in the Translation step.

Different translation memories can also be defined for each workflow step and files can be split in all workflow steps, or be split in only one step.

##### Assigning TMs in workflow steps

When selecting [TM](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709688865692#UUID-c58dd835-39ea-1a94-02d1-9f2517fd6d75)s for projects with workflow, the same translation memories can be selected for all workflow steps, or each workflow step can have its own TM setup.

##### Email notification

When assigning a job to a Linguist or Vendor in the first workflow step, they can be [manually notified by email](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/10825557848220#UUID-438e305c-62e8-70af-9565-8895e16fd94f "Job Tools (TMS)") or automatically when the job is imported to the [project](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709748435484#UUID-fd006a60-d1b0-dc4b-8681-00d5464cd76e).

Linguists assigned in higher steps are automatically notified the moment the job in the previous step is set to Completed. Upon notification, the proofreader starts to work immediately after the translation is completed. If defined, Linguists are notified when the next step is passed or if the job is rejected.

##### Tight deadlines (concurrent steps)

When working with a tight deadline, a revision can be started before the translation is complete but this is to be done cautiously.

If a job has not been completed in the preceding workflow step, the confirmation indicator in the [editor](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709683847964#UUID-7174fb87-7107-2f32-ce55-5e040de5446c) is red with the warning message Preceding workflow step not completed.

The reviser can ignore the warning and carefully go ahead with the revision but *only with segments confirmed by the translator*. If the reviser changes a segment that has not been confirmed in the preceding workflow step (in this case, translation), changes by the translator will not be later propagated to the revision step.

When working with the [CAT desktop editor](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709683873052#UUID-92b9886a-e3a5-6975-8c35-246200ac54ef), the [bilingual MXLIFF](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709739992860#UUID-03e9320f-57b2-e624-e8c7-9b3d2a3da55e) will only include target segments from the previous step that have been added until the moment it was exported.

The option to allow linguists to start a workflow step before the preceding step has been completed is set in [access and security](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709585565980#UUID-424b8fbe-2d60-48eb-891a-a4f1c5004c82). See [CAT preferences](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709683926812#UUID-fb5d0457-58e7-963b-d4dd-4a069f25139c) for editor settings.

##### Workflow automation

When working with projects with multiple languages and workflow steps, a specific workflow step may not be required for all jobs.

To prevent issues caused by skipped workflow steps for certain languages, enable the Workflow automation option in the Workflow [project settings](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/10825091328028#UUID-d7b8121c-4488-b077-5493-6ca7d30d48d5 "Project Settings (TMS)"). When the previous workflow step is completed, the unassigned jobs are automatically marked as completed and move on to the next relevant step in the workflow.

##### Update all workflow steps

The Update all workflow steps option is designed for [continuous project](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709703661468#UUID-575d57e6-43ea-ff19-eec2-2ac475f96341 "Continuous Projects (TMS)") workflows where changes to source content are regularly detected and updates need to be propagated across all workflow steps. When the source is updated, the latest version of the target segments from the latest workflow step is propagated downward and upwards to all preceding and following workflow steps. This ensures consistency between what’s shown in the editor and what’s stored in the TM.

- Workflow propagation follows a hierarchical order. If a segment is edited or confirmed in a higher workflow step, that version becomes the active one and changes from lower workflow steps are no longer propagated.
- In continuous projects, source updates create a new version of the job. Segment versions are not merged, and Phrase TMS always works with the latest job version.
- Workflow steps that were already completed or approved are not reopened. However, their segment content may be replaced by newer versions after an update.
- Editing jobs in higher workflow steps before lower steps are finished, or working in multiple workflow steps at the same time, can affect how changes are propagated.
- Triggering pre-translation on a higher workflow step after the project has already been pre-translated breaks real-time propagation from lower steps. To preserve propagation behavior, apply pre-translation only to the lowest active workflow step.

##### Important

Only activate this feature when there are source updates via [APC](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709647363356#UUID-3fb1230d-d6b0-83ce-cb52-98b96688b553) as it will not work otherwise.

##### Manually changing job status

Project Managers can manually change the status of a job in any workflow step at any time, including resetting a step that has already been marked as Completed back to an earlier status such as Emailed or New. This sends the job back to the assigned Linguist for rework.

Manual status changes are recorded in the job status history. In the project jobs table, hover over a job's status to view the tooltip showing the date and time the job was accepted, completed, or otherwise changed, along with the associated user.

Changing a job's status from Completed back to New resets only the job status. It does not reset the edited or confirmed state of segments. If a segment in a higher step was already edited or confirmed before the job was reopened, translation changes made in a lower step still do not propagate to that higher step.

#### Export Workflow Changes ([Web editor](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709683890204#UUID-b7f5d899-ec2b-4352-a151-d45f6cfb5cd8) only)

Changes in workflow steps can be provided to anyone involved in the translation chain with a summary of the source and all versions of the translations such as translation, revision, and final review. An .HTML table is generated with original text in the first column and a separate column for each workflow step.

This summary cannot be shared with providers (*Exception*: the entire project with all workflow steps is shared with Vendor) but the generated .HTML file can be downloaded and distributed if required.

To export workflow changes, follow these steps:

1. From a project page, select a job with workflow changes for export.
2. From the Tools menu, select Export workflow changes.

   A new browser tab opens with the generated .HTML.

### Notifications (TMS)

> Quelle: https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709702543260-Notifications-TMS  
> Zuletzt aktualisiert: 2026-09-25T06:04:40Z  
> Labels: 2BTr, ar_tms

#### In-app Notifications

Notifications are presented in the top right corner and provide status updates of [jobs](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709686763420#UUID-33f88350-daa8-2ab2-e7ce-e35300ec60f8), [projects](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709748435484#UUID-fd006a60-d1b0-dc4b-8681-00d5464cd76e), and any connection errors.

In-app notifications are also displayed in [CAT editors](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709683847964#UUID-7174fb87-7107-2f32-ce55-5e040de5446c) when [mentioning](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/7681232807708#UUID-0801f553-9b35-4ba4-4a38-46d3fc1e8a34) users in [comment](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709700374044#UUID-d5b89fba-f861-b990-6511-8db310f9bb86) and [LQA](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/27529737766044#UUID-8c8a9e28-99dd-f432-f780-331192127c69) threads. Clicking on a mention notification opens the specific job in the editor, where the relevant thread and segment are focused. Notifications from comments or LQA are distinguished by the appropriate symbol: ![New Comment](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682126959644) is displayed for comments, while ![LQA_new.jpeg](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682159937052) is displayed for LQA assessments.

The notifications can be pinned to the top of the list for later reference, filtered to show only unread notifications using the toggle at the top of the list, or all marked as read at once through the option in the ![vertical_dot_grey.svg](https://support.phrase.com/hc/article_attachments/30682175949084) menu.

Unpinned notifications older than 30 days are automatically deleted. In-app notifications cannot be turned off.

|  |
| --- |
| [Eingebettetes Video/Inhalt](https://www.youtube.com/embed/no94qfAT6GU) |

##### Note

Due to continuous improvements, the user interface may not be exactly the same as presented in the video.

#### Email Notifications

Email notifications must be enabled in the [Access and security](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709585565980#UUID-424b8fbe-2d60-48eb-891a-a4f1c5004c82) settings.

Email notifications are sent to users only after their first login. Until then, the messages are queued. When the user first logs in to TMS, the queued messages are scheduled to be sent.

##### Email Notifications for New Jobs

Email notifications for new jobs tell linguists and vendors that work is available. They use the [Job Assigned](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709617392540#UUID-9344883c-3d65-7641-8b0e-6dfb0aeb17b1) email template. The email goes to the providers assigned to the job and lists the details of each job included, such as file name, language pair, and due date. It also contains a link to the project.

A new job email is sent in either of these ways:

- **Automatically**, when a new job is created with the Notify providers option enabled.
- **Manually**, from [Tools/Email](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/10825557848220#UUID-438e305c-62e8-70af-9565-8895e16fd94f "Job Tools (TMS)") in the jobs table on a project page, or from Notify providers on the [Jobs page](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/10825555367452#UUID-b84e994d-143b-9758-ee5c-8ce224df0d66 "Jobs Page (TMS)").

##### Email Notifications for Mentions

Project managers can configure email notifications on a per-project basis to provide additional visibility for collaboration in large projects with multiple vendors.

Email notifications follow the same rules and recipient logic as existing in-app notifications in TMS.

If enabled, email notifications are sent using a dedicated [email template](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709617392540#UUID-9344883c-3d65-7641-8b0e-6dfb0aeb17b1) when:

- A user is mentioned in segment or job comments and LQA threads.
- A reply is added to an existing comment or LQA thread in which the user is a participant.
- The user is included in a group mention (e.g., @owners, @providers), following the same behavior as in-app notifications.

The email notification contains a link that opens the job in the CAT web editor and focuses the relevant comment, thread, or segment. If a mentioned user has not yet accepted the job, the link opens the job in read-only mode.

Email notifications are sent only to users who currently have access to the relevant job or job part.

To configure email notifications, select Notify users when mentioned in comments or LQA in the [Access and security](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709585565980#UUID-424b8fbe-2d60-48eb-891a-a4f1c5004c82) settings.

**Limitations**

- When comments or LQA issues are created in bulk (e.g., across repeated segments), one email is sent per conversation.
- Email links generated before a [job split](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/10825557848220#UUID-438e305c-62e8-70af-9565-8895e16fd94f "Job Tools (TMS)") may no longer resolve correctly, as new job parts receive new UIDs.
- In multi-step or multi-organization [workflows](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709717879324#UUID-52eea4c5-7d94-1750-40ca-86e757b17916 "Workflow (TMS)"), the email link opens the job part where the conversation was created.
- If multiple email templates of this type exist in TMS settings, the first available template is used automatically.
- Replies notify all existing participants in the conversation, even without a new mention.

##### Email Notifications for New Reference Materials

Project managers can configure email notifications on a per-project basis to notify relevant users when new reference materials are manually added to a project. This notification is available in [Access and security](https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5709585565980#UUID-424b8fbe-2d60-48eb-891a-a4f1c5004c82) settings and is sent only if email notifications are enabled.

Recipients can be selected from project owners, internal providers, and vendor users. A dedicated email template can be used for this notification type.
